analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the challenges of assessing cell-mediated immunity in vaccination trials by developing a T-cell receptor (TCR)-based measure of immunogen recognition. The research evaluated this measure in COV-BOOST, a third-dose COVID-19 vaccine trial, during the Delta and Omicron waves in the United Kingdom. The authors estimated HLA-aware Spike-reactive T cell (HA-TS) breadth using participant HLA genotypes, TCR{beta} repertoires, and a novel SARS-CoV-2 S HLA-linked reference catalog. Higher post-boost HA-TS breadth was associated with lower symptomatic infection risk (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.86). The association remained significant even after adjusting for neutralizing antibody titers and IFN-{gamma} responses. These results suggest that HA-TS breadth could serve as a correlate of protection, offering potential for accelerating vaccine development. However, the study acknowledges limitations posed by HLA-driven heterogeneity and the challenges of live T cell functional assays.

title: Structural insights into subunit exchange inhibition and ligand‐induced dimerization of SARS ‐ CoV ‐2 main protease
abstract: Abstract The SARS‐CoV‐2 main protease (M pro ) is an essential homodimeric cysteine protease that mediates viral polyprotein processing and represents a primary therapeutic target for COVID‐19 treatment. While peptidomimetic inhibitors such as nirmatrelvir have demonstrated clinical efficacy, their effects on M pro quaternary structure dynamics remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests these compounds may paradoxically promote dimerization, a phenomenon termed ligand‐induced dimerization (LID), which could enhance catalytic activity at low inhibitor concentrations. Here, we employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform combining metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen‐deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX‐MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors. We demonstrate that apo‐M pro exists in a dynamic monomer–dimer equilibrium characterized by rapid subunit exchange. Remarkably, peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro . Region‐resolved HDX‐MS revealed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization extending beyond the active site to the N‐finger (residues 1–17) and dimer interface (residues 291–302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N‐finger region provided a sensitive structural marker of ligand‐induced dimerization. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that the observed stabilization arises primarily from dimer formation rather than direct ligand contacts. These findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor‐stabilized dimerization, identify the N‐finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, and demonstrate the power of integrated mass spectrometry for dissecting complex protein assembly dynamics with therapeutic implications for antiviral drug development.

analysis.methods: The study combined metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the structural and dynamic changes in M pro induced by inhibitors.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical structural insights into the behavior of M pro under inhibitor influence, which can inform the design of more effective antiviral therapies targeting this enzyme.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro) under the influence of peptidomimetic inhibitors. It highlights the dynamic monomer–dimer equilibrium of apo-M pro and demonstrates that inhibitors like nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8 kinetically trap the dimeric state, stabilizing it and suppressing subunit exchange. The research employs an integrated mass spectrometry platform, including native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, to reveal conformational changes in M pro that extend beyond the active site to the N-finger and dimer interface. The findings suggest that the N-finger region serves as a sensitive structural marker of ligand-induced dimerization, offering new insights into the mechanisms of inhibitor action and potential implications for antiviral drug development. However, the study is limited to abstract-level evidence and relies on computational methods, which may affect the strength of the conclusions.

The research focused on SARS-CoV-2 and its variants, with no specific mention of study dates or centers.
elements_en.methods: The study combined metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the structural and dynamic changes in M pro induced by inhibitors.
elements_en.main_results: Region-resolved HDX-MS showed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization beyond the active site, affecting the N-finger (residues 1–17) and dimer interface (residues 291–302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N-finger region was observed as a structural marker of ligand-induced dimerization.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization and identify the N-finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, offering new insights into the structural dynamics of M pro and its implications for antiviral drug development.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical structural insights into the behavior of M pro under inhibitor influence, which can inform the design of more effective antiviral therapies targeting this enzyme.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence, and the findings are based on computational and structural analyses rather than direct clinical or biological outcomes. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on in silico methods.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用整合的质谱平台来分析M pro二聚化的动态性质及其受肽模拟抑制剂调控的情况。研究聚焦于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及其变体,未提及具体研究日期或研究中心。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究结合代谢15N标记与原生质谱(nMS)、氢-氘交换质谱(HDX-MS)和分子动力学(MD)模拟,以阐明抑制剂诱导的M pro结构和动态变化。
elements_zh.main_results: 区域解析的HDX-MS显示,抑制剂结合可引起广泛构象稳定化,不仅限于活性位点,还扩展到N-指(残基1–17)和二聚界面(残基291–302)。在N-指区域中观察到交换模式从双峰(EX1)转变为单峰(EX2)的显著转变,作为配体诱导二聚化的结构标记。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现确立了抑制剂稳定二聚化的机制基础,并识别了N-指作为四级结构转变的动态报告基因,为M pro的结构动态及其对抗病毒药物药物开发的潜在影响提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了关于抑制剂影响下M pro行为的关键结构见解,有助于设计更有效的抗病毒药物疗法,以靶向该酶。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于摘要层面的证据,其发现基于计算和结构分析,而非直接的临床或生物学结果。由于依赖于计算机模拟方法,证据强度中等。

title_zh: 关于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2主要蛋白酶亚基交换抑制和配体诱导二聚化的结构见解
source_body_en: Abstract The SARS‐CoV‐2 main protease (M pro ) is an essential homodimeric cysteine protease that mediates viral polyprotein processing and represents a primary therapeutic target for COVID‐19 treatment. While peptidomimetic inhibitors such as nirmatrelvir have demonstrated clinical efficacy, their effects on M pro quaternary structure dynamics remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests these compounds may paradoxically promote dimerization, a phenomenon termed ligand‐induced dimerization (LID), which could enhance catalytic activity at low inhibitor concentrations. Here, we employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform combining metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen‐deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX‐MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors. We demonstrate that apo‐M pro exists in a dynamic monomer–dimer equilibrium characterized by rapid subunit exchange. Remarkably, peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro . Region‐resolved HDX‐MS revealed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization extending beyond the active site to the N‐finger (residues 1–17) and dimer interface (residues 291–302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N‐finger region provided a sensitive structural marker of ligand‐induced dimerization. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that the observed stabilization arises primarily from dimer formation rather than direct ligand contacts. These findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor‐stabilized dimerization, identify the N‐finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, and demonstrate the power of integrated mass spectrometry for dissecting complex protein assembly dynamics with therapeutic implications for antiviral drug development.

title: Correlation Study between Civilian SARS-CoV-2 Wastewater Concentration and COVID-19 Cases among U.S. Military Health System Beneficiaries
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as a new near real-time tool for population-wide COVID-19 surveillance. This study examined the statistical correlation between county-level civilian SARS-CoV-2 wastewater concentration and COVID-19 cases among beneficiaries of the U.S. Military Health System (MHS) from April 2024 to April 2025 in the continental United States. The analysis revealed an overall high correlation for both MHS beneficiaries ( rs = 0.797; 95% CI: 0.626–0.893) and active-duty service members ( rs = 0.800; 95% CI: 0.633–0.892). Further, an assessment of external factors suggested that correlations were stronger in regions with higher MHS populations. title: Structure-based and AI-guided redesign of Sotrovimab for enhanced recognition of SARS-CoV-2 BA.2 and the E340G escape mutant
abstract: Introduction The rapid evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants has substantially compromised the efficacy of several monoclonal antibody therapies, including Sotrovimab, through mutations that disrupt antibody–antigen recognition. Developing antibodies with improved recognition of emerging variants and resistance-associated mutations is therefore essential for maintaining therapeutic effectiveness. Methods Here, we employed an integrated computational framework combining structure-guided antibody engineering, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted sequence design, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and binding free-energy analyses to redesign Sotrovimab against the Omicron BA.2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) and the clinically relevant E340G escape mutant. Residue-level energetic profiling was used to identify destabilizing interface residues, followed by mutational redesign and ProteinMPNN-guided sequence optimization. The resulting candidates were evaluated through 500 ns all-atom MD simulations, complemented by conformational analyses, MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations, residue-level energy decomposition, and dynamic cross-correlation analyses. Results and Discussion The top-ranked redesigned Sotrovimab candidates retained the characteristic immunoglobulin fold while exhibiting improved structural stability, compactness, and reduced conformational fluctuations. Principal component analysis and free-energy landscape calculations further revealed more confined and energetically favorable conformational states, suggesting enhanced dynamic compatibility with the target RBD. MM/PBSA calculations indicated substantially more favorable binding free energies for both redesigned candidates against the BA.2 RBD and E340G mutant. Residue-level energy decomposition and dynamic cross-correlation analyses further demonstrated improved energetic complementarity and intermolecular communication across the antibody–antigen interface. These improvements were accompanied by enhanced hydrogen-bonding, hydrophobic, and van der Waals interactions, together with increased engagement of the conserved N343-linked glycan, potentially providing additional stabilization to the antibody -antigen complex. Among the redesigned candidates, Sotrovimab-design-2 consistently exhibited the most favorable structural and energetic characteristics. Conclusion Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of integrating AI-guided sequence optimization with structure-based antibody engineering to improve antibody recognition of SARS-CoV-2 variants and resistance-associated mutations. This framework provides a computational foundation for developing mutation-resilient therapeutic antibodies against evolving viral pathogens.

abstract_zh: 引言 新冠病毒Omicron变体的快速进化显著削弱了包括Sotrovimab在内的多种单克隆抗体疗法的有效性,这些变化通过干扰抗体-抗原识别机制实现。因此,开发能够更好地识别新兴变体并具有抗逃逸突变能力的抗体对于维持治疗效果至关重要。方法 在本研究中,我们采用了一种整合的计算框架,结合结构引导的抗体工程、人工智能(AI)辅助的序列设计、分子动力学(MD)模拟和结合自由能分析,对Sotrovimab进行改造,以针对Omicron BA.2受体结合域(RBD)和具有临床意义的E340G逃逸突变体。通过残差级能量谱分析确定了不稳定界面残基,随后进行突变设计和由ProteinMPNN引导的序列优化。所得候选抗体通过500纳秒全原子MD模拟进行评估,并辅以构象分析、MM/PBSA结合自由能计算、残差级能量分解和动态交叉相关分析。结果与讨论 排名最高的Sotrovimab改造候选抗体保留了特征性的免疫球蛋白折叠结构,同时表现出增强的结构稳定性、紧凑性和减少的构象波动。主成分分析和自由能景观计算进一步揭示了更为受限且能量更有利的构象状态,表明其与目标RBD的动态兼容性得到了增强。MM/PBSA计算显示,这两个改造候选抗体对BA.2 RBD和E340G突变体的结合自由能显著更有利。残差级能量分解和动态交叉相关分析进一步证明了抗体-抗原界面处更优的能量互补性和分子间通信。这些改进伴随着增强的氢键、疏水和范德华相互作用,以及保守的N343连接糖蛋白的更高参与度,可能为抗体-抗原复合物提供额外的稳定性。在所有改造候选抗体中,Sotrovimab-design-2始终表现出最有利的结构和能量特性。结论 这些发现表明,将人工智能引导的序列优化与基于结构的抗体工程相结合,能够有效提升抗体对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体及抗逃逸突变能力的识别。该框架为开发针对不断演变的病毒病原体的抗逃逸突变治疗性抗体提供了计算基础。

title: Immunogenicity and safety of inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine (CoronaVac) using a two-dose primary protocol in children and adolescents (Immunita-002, Brazil): a phase IV one-year follow-up
abstract: Long-term evidence on the durability and quality of immune responses induced by the inactivated whole-virus CoronaVac vaccine in children and adolescents remains limited. We evaluated humoral and cellular immunity and safety over 12 months after completion of the primary vaccination schedule. In this phase IV longitudinal study, 640 children and adolescents aged 3–17 years who received two doses of CoronaVac were followed for 12 months. Humoral immunity was assessed by anti-Spike (anti-S) and anti-Nucleocapsid (anti-N) IgG ELISAs and neutralizing antibody assays against the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 B.1 lineage and Omicron BA.1 and BA.5 subvariants. Cellular immunity was evaluated through antigen-specific stimulation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, multiplex quantification of soluble immune mediators, and immune network analysis. Safety and suspected COVID-19 cases were monitored throughout follow-up. Anti-S and anti-N IgG seropositivity remained high throughout follow-up (90-96% and 93-98%, respectively). Neutralizing antibodies against the ancestral B.1 lineage remained high in both age groups, although seropositivity decreased to 80% at 12 months among children aged 3–11 years. In contrast, cross-neutralization against Omicron BA.5 increased over time, reaching 100% seropositivity in both age groups at 12 months. Vaccination was associated with changes in chemokines, inflammatory and regulatory cytokines, and growth factors, alongside dynamic immune network remodeling. Antigen-specific PBMC stimulation demonstrated cytokine and chemokine responses one year after vaccination, with distinct profiles following ancestral and Omicron Spike stimulation. No additional adverse events were reported during the final six months. Previously reported serious adverse events resolved without vaccine-related sequelae, and no clinically reported COVID-19 cases occurred during the final six months of surveillance. CoronaVac induced persistent humoral responses and was associated with longitudinal changes in antigen-stimulated immune activity over 12 months. Integrated immunological analyses provide insights into the durability and coordination of immune responses following primary vaccination in children and adolescents, while the mechanisms underlying immune memory and the relationship between immune responses and clinical protection remain to be elucidated.
authors: Jordana Grazziela Alves Coelho dos Reis

In this phase IV longitudinal study, 640 children and adolescents aged 3–17 years who received two doses of CoronaVac were followed for 12 months. Humoral immunity was assessed by anti-Spike (anti-S) and anti-Nucleocapsid (anti-N) IgG ELISAs and neutralizing antibody assays against the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 B.1 lineage and Omicron BA.1 and BA.5 subvariants. Cellular immunity was evaluated through antigen-specific stimulation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, multiplex quantification of soluble immune mediators, and immune network analysis. Safety and suspected COVID-19 cases were monitored throughout follow-up. Anti-S and anti-N IgG seropositivity remained high throughout follow-up (90-96% and 93-98%, respectively). Neutralizing antibodies against the ancestral B.1 lineage remained high in both age groups, although seropositivity decreased to 80% at 12 months among children aged 3–11 years. In contrast, cross-neutralization against Omicron BA.5 increased over time, reaching 100% seropositivity in both age groups at 12 months. Vaccination was associated with changes in chemokines, inflammatory and regulatory cytokines, and growth factors, alongside dynamic immune network remodeling. Antigen-specific PBMC stimulation demonstrated cytokine and chemokine responses one year after vaccination, with distinct profiles following ancestral and Omicron Spike stimulation. No additional adverse events were reported during the final six months. Previously reported serious adverse events resolved without vaccine-related sequelae, and no clinically reported COVID-19 cases occurred during the final six months of surveillance. CoronaVac induced persistent humoral responses and was associated with longitudinal changes in antigen-stimulated immune activity over 12 months. Integrated immunological analyses provide insights into the durability and coordination of immune responses following primary vaccination in children and adolescents, while the mechanisms underlying immune memory and the relationship between immune responses and clinical protection remain to be elucidated.
authors: Jordana Grazziela Alves Coelho dos Reis

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the immunogenicity and safety of the inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine CoronaVac in children and adolescents over a one-year follow-up period. The research aimed to assess humoral and cellular immunity and safety, with 640 participants aged 3–17 years receiving two doses of the vaccine. Humoral immunity was measured using IgG ELISAs and neutralizing antibody assays against the ancestral B.1 lineage and Omicron subvariants, while cellular immunity was analyzed through PBMC stimulation and immune network profiling. Results showed persistent anti-S and anti-N IgG responses, with neutralizing antibodies against B.1 remaining high but decreasing in younger children. Cross-neutralization against Omicron BA.5 increased, reaching 100% seropositivity in both age groups. Safety monitoring indicated no additional adverse events in the final six months, and previously reported serious events resolved without sequelae. The study suggests CoronaVac induces durable immune responses and immune network changes, though the relationship between these responses and clinical protection remains unclear. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and lack of control groups.

title: Schistosoma mansoni Infection Alters Antibody Subclass Profiles but Preserves SARS-CoV-2 mRNA Vaccine-Induced Neutralizing Activity in a Murine Model
abstract: Abstract Objectives Helminth infections can modulate host immune responses and potentially influence immunogenicity of vaccines against unrelated pathogens. This study investigated the effects of Schistosoma mansoni infection on immune responses to COVID-19 mRNA vaccine (BNT162b2) on in a murine model. Methods Two experiments were conducted using C57BL/6J mice assigned to three groups: uninfected and unvaccinated controls, S. mansoni -infected vaccinated mice, and uninfected vaccinated mice. The experiments differed in parasite inoculum and BNT162b2 vaccine dose. IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a antibodies against the spike-protein S1 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing activity was assessed using an in vitro virus neutralization assay. For Experiment 1 (Exp 1), bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of spleen tissues and measurement of cytokine production by peptide-stimulated splenocytes were also performed. Results Vaccination induced robust spike-specific antibody responses in both infected and uninfected mice. In Exp 1, infected mice exhibited significantly higher total IgG and IgG2a titres than uninfected vaccinated mice following the booster dose. In Experiment 2 (Exp 2), antibody titres were comparable between vaccinated groups. The IgG2a/IgG1 ratio was consistently higher in uninfected vaccinated mice, suggesting that S. mansoni infection altered vaccination-induced antibody subclass profiles. In Exp 1, liver egg burden was inversely correlated with IgG2a titres (Spearman’s ρ = −0.87, p = 0.0054), but this association was not observed in Exp 2. Peptide-stimulated splenocytes from infected mice showed significantly lower levels of the Th1-associated cytokines in infected mice. Despite these immunological changes, neutralizing activity did not differ significantly between infected and uninfected vaccinated mice in either experiment. Neutralizing titres were positively correlated with total spike-specific IgG and IgG2a titres in both experiments. mansoni infection modified Th1-associated immune response to BNT162b2 vaccination, particularly antibody subclass distribution, without consistently reducing spike-specific antibody titres or SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing activity. These findings suggest that helminth-associated immune modulation can alter vaccine-induced immune responses without necessarily compromising the generation of functional antiviral antibodies. Further studies involving direct viral challenge and longer-term immune assessments are needed to determine whether these responses confer equivalent protection in infected and uninfected hosts.

title_zh: 曼氏血吸虫感染改变了抗体亚类谱但保持了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 mRNA 疫苗诱导的中和活性
source_body_en: Abstract Objectives Helminth infections can modulate host immune responses and potentially influence immunogenicity of vaccines against unrelated pathogens. This study investigated the effects of Schistosoma mansoni infection on immune responses to COVID-19 mRNA vaccine (BNT162b2) on in a murine model. Methods Two experiments were conducted using C57BL/6J mice assigned to three groups: uninfected and unvaccinated controls, S. mansoni -infected vaccinated mice, and uninfected vaccinated mice. The experiments differed in parasite inoculum and BNT162b2 vaccine dose. IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a antibodies against the spike-protein S1 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing activity was assessed using an in vitro virus neutralization assay. For Experiment 1 (Exp 1), bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of spleen tissues and measurement of cytokine production by peptide-stimulated splenocytes were also performed. Results Vaccination induced robust spike-specific antibody responses in both infected and uninfected mice. In Exp 1, infected mice exhibited significantly higher total IgG and IgG2a titres than uninfected vaccinated mice following the booster dose. In Experiment 2 (Exp 2), antibody titres were comparable between vaccinated groups. The IgG2a/IgG1 ratio was consistently higher in uninfected vaccinated mice, suggesting that S. mansoni infection altered vaccination-induced antibody subclass profiles. In Exp 1, liver egg burden was inversely correlated with IgG2a titres (Spearman’s ρ = −0.87, p = 0.0054), but this association was not observed in Exp 2. Peptide-stimulated splenocytes from infected mice showed significantly lower levels of the Th1-associated cytokines in infected mice. Despite these immunological changes, neutralizing activity did not differ significantly between infected and uninfected vaccinated mice in either experiment. Neutralizing titres were positively correlated with total spike-specific IgG and IgG2a titres in both experiments. mansoni infection modified Th1-associated immune response to BNT162b2 vaccination, particularly antibody subclass distribution, without consistently reducing spike-specific antibody titres or SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing activity. These findings suggest that helminth-associated immune modulation can alter vaccine-induced immune responses without necessarily compromising the generation of functional antiviral antibodies. Further studies involving direct viral challenge and longer-term immune assessments are needed to determine whether these responses confer equivalent protection in infected and uninfected hosts.

title: Long COVID: Clinical Presentation, Proposed Mechanisms, Management, and the Emerging Role of Hsp90 as a Therapeutic Target
abstract: Long COVID, also termed post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), affects a substantial minority of people after acute COVID-19 and is now recognized as a distinct clinical entity rather than slow convalescence. This review has two aims: to critically appraise the evidence for the principal proposed mechanisms of long COVID and to evaluate whether heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) represents a candidate molecular node that intersects several of these mechanisms and may provide a therapeutically tractable target, without implying primacy over other pathways involved in disease pathogenesis. We first summarise the clinical presentation and the diagnostic difficulty created by symptom heterogeneity and by overlap with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and other post-infectious syndromes. Then the leading candidate mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, viral antigen persistence, reactivation of latent herpesviruses, autoimmunity, endothelial and microvascular dysfunction, and skeletal muscle and mitochondrial abnormality, grading the strength of the supporting human evidence and stating the principal uncertainties for each, are evaluated. Further, we discuss the roles of Hsp90 on SARS-CoV-2 replication, immune evasion, endothelial barrier dysfunction, and chaperone-directed autoimmunity. Evidence on Hsp90 inhibition is deliberately presented in both directions: several preclinical studies report reduced viral load and inflammation, whereas one inhibitor failed to reduce viral shedding and increased mortality in infected mice, indicating that Hsp90 is a potential therapeutic target because of its involvement across multiple biological processes relevant to long COVID. Management is discussed by symptom domain, with clinical evidence distinguished throughout from in vitro, in silico and animal data, and candidate repurposed agents are summarised with the highest level of evidence currently available for each. In summary, no pharmacological therapy is yet supported by adequate randomised evidence in long COVID, and the value of Hsp90 as a target will depend on isoform selectivity, treatment timing and biomarker-defined patient selection.

title: Dysregulation of redox-inflammatory markers in COVID-19: a multi-parameter analysis with disease severity
abstract: Abstract Viral infections are one of the biggest threats ever known to humankind. Viral mutability against the human defense system makes them deadly. Virus manipulates host gene expressions, dictating the course of the disease using inflammation-induced oxidative stress. Characterized by uncontrolled Reactive oxygen species levels and weakened antioxidant defenses, which significantly impact viral disease severity. SARS-CoV-2, a constant threat due to its ability to mutate, showcases this interplay, emphasizing the need to understand host cellular responses. Unraveling these viral modulation patterns offers insight into predicting disease severity and identifying therapeutic targets. The study used infected groups (Severe, Moderate, and Mild) and a control group. The samples were collected using a non-probability stratified sampling approach and were collected early after diagnosis to minimize treatment-related variability: at hospitalization for severe cases, within 12 hours of clinic visit for moderate cases, and within 24 hours of RT-PCR confirmation for mild cases. Disease severity classification was performed by clinicians based on clinical symptoms and oxygen saturation (SpO2). This research delves into assessing the intricate interplay between the severity of the viral infection and inflammation-induced redox imbalance by expression profile of key antioxidant genes (GPx, NRF2, SOD2), pro-inflammatory genes (ACE2, NOS2), and RNA-binding gene (HuR), by comparing the total hydroperoxides as an indirect markeer for ROS, serum Ang II levels, and clinical data among the groups infected individuals. Significant expressional dysregulation of proinflammatory, oxidative, and anti-oxidative markers is found among the study groups, especially in the severe group. ACE2, GPx, and SOD2 were downregulated, while NOS2, HuR, and Nrf2 were upregulated, which indicates a shift towards a pro-oxidant state, such as twice the amount of ROS in both severe and moderate groups, and Serum Ang II levels are halved in the severe group. Clinical biomarkers were also elevated. These findings establish a strong correlation between redox-inflammatory dysregulation and the severity of infections.

source_records.title: Dysregulation of redox-inflammatory markers in COVID-19: a multi-parameter analysis with disease severity.
source_records.abstract: Background Viral infections remain a major global health threat. Viruses manipulate host gene expression, dictating the course of the disease using inflammation-induced oxidative stress. Characterized by uncontrolled reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and weakened antioxidant defenses, which influence disease severity. SARS-CoV-2 exemplifies this interaction, highlighting the importance of understanding host molecular responses to identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Methods The study included infected groups (Severe, Moderate, and Mild) and a control group. Samples were collected using a non-probability stratified sampling approach and were collected early after diagnosis to minimize treatment-related variability: at hospitalization for severe cases, within 12 h of a clinic visit for moderate cases, and within 24 h of RT-PCR confirmation for mild cases. Disease severity classification was based on clinical symptoms and oxygen saturation. This research assesses the intricate interplay between the severity of the viral infection and inflammation-induced redox imbalance using the expression profiles of key antioxidant genes (GPx, Nrf2, SOD2), pro-inflammatory genes (ACE2, NOS2), and an RNA-binding gene (HuR). Total hydroperoxides were measured as an indirect marker of ROS, along with serum Angiotensin II levels and clinical data. Result The findings demonstrate a coordinated pro-oxidant and inflammatory shift associated with severe COVID-19, characterized by significant dysregulation of redox and inflammatory markers. ROS levels were approximately twofold higher in the severe and moderate groups, while serum Angiotensin II levels were reduced by approximately half in the severe group. Clinical biomarkers were also elevated and correlated with disease severity. Collectively, these findings identify a multi-parameter molecular signature of severe COVID-19 that may help explain disease progression and inform future host-targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: Post-Pandemic Burden of Illness Among Patients in Germany Aged ≥60 Years with Acute or Persistent COVID-19
abstract: Background/Objectives: Post-pandemic, real-world evidence on COVID-19 in elderly patients in Germany is limited. This study describes the clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, quality of life, and healthcare resource use among elderly patients with COVID-19. Methods: Data were derived from the Adelphi Real World COVID Disease-Specific ProgrammeTM, a cross-sectional survey of physicians and patients aged ≥60 years with acute (≤4 weeks post-diagnosis) or persistent (symptom duration ≥ 12 weeks) COVID-19 from January to July 2024. Analyses were descriptive; comparisons between groups were not performed. Results: 151 physicians provided data for 400 patients (acute COVID-19, n = 200; persistent COVID-19, n = 200). The mean patient age was 68.1 (acute) and 70.1 (persistent) years. Most patients were male (acute, 56.0%; persistent, 58.5%) and retired (acute, 68.0%; persistent, 78.5%). The most common concomitant condition was hypertension (acute, 37.5%; persistent, 35.5%). Tiredness/fatigue was the most common physician-reported symptom (57.5% acute; 67.5% persistent). For patients with acute COVID-19 that received prescribed treatment (n = 62/200, 31.0%), antivirals were most commonly used (n = 59/62, 95.2%). Mean number of consultations from the index COVID-19 diagnosis to survey date was 2.7 over a median of 17.0 days (Q1–Q3: 7.0–44.0) and 5.0 over a median of 164.0 days (Q1–Q3: 128.0–225.0) for patients with acute or persistent COVID-19, respectively. Self-reported data were provided by 98 (acute) and 107 (persistent) patients. The most common patient-reported worst symptoms were headaches (n = 15/98, 15.3%; acute) and tiredness (n = 14/107, 13.1%; persistent). Mean EQ-5D-5L index score (German weighting) was 0.79 for both groups. EQ-VAS scores were 66.1 (acute) and 66.0 (persistent). Conclusions: Elderly patients with acute or persistent COVID-19 have a notable burden of illness. Prioritizing care and interventions in these populations in the post-pandemic era is warranted.

title: Neutralizing immunity across SARS-CoV-2 variants in kidney disease: broad deficits and sex-related heterogeneity after China’s Omicron wave
abstract: Background Variant-specific SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing responses in kidney disease (KD) remain incompletely characterized after China’s 2022–2023 Omicron wave. We compared these responses and their heterogeneity between participants with KD and healthy controls (HC) sampled in the same region. Methods This cross-sectional study included 380 participants: 197 HC and 183 participants with KD, sampled in Zhejiang Province from March to early April 2023. Pseudovirus assays measured neutralization against the prototype strain (PT), BA.4/5, and XBB.1.5. KD/HC geometric mean ratios (GMRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Group differences and interactions with sex, age, and vaccination-dose category were assessed using log 10 -transformed titers. Disease categories and confirmed infection before sampling were examined in exploratory analyses. Results KD participants had significantly lower titers against PT, BA.4/5, and XBB.1.5, with KD/HC GMRs of 0.167 (95% CI, 0.110–0.255), 0.491 (0.359–0.672), and 0.626 (0.489–0.802), respectively. Group-by-sex interactions were significant for all three viruses (interaction P = 0.0006, 0.0163, and 0.0067, respectively), with larger relative HC–KD differences among women. Receipt of ≥3 doses, compared with 0–2 doses, was associated with higher PT titers in both groups, whereas no significant overall dose associations were detected for BA.4/5 or XBB.1.5. No significant group interactions with age or vaccination-dose category were detected. Exploratory analyses showed lower PT and BA.4/5 titers in glomerular/immune-mediated than in metabolic/vascular kidney disease. In the questionnaire subgroup, confirmed infection before sampling was associated with higher BA.4/5 titers without a significant group-by-infection interaction. Conclusions KD was associated with lower neutralization across all three viruses, with consistently larger relative HC–KD differences among women. These findings highlight sex-related heterogeneity in post-wave neutralizing immunity and support prospective studies integrating renal phenotype, treatment, vaccination history, and clinical outcomes.

title: Biosafety level-3 cryo-electron tomography of active severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 virions.
abstract: Understanding the structural properties of pathogenic viruses in their native, infectious state is critical for rational vaccine and drug development. However, conducting cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) under biosafety level 3 (BSL-3) containment presents significant challenges. Here, we established and validated a high-end cryo-EM workflow within a BSL-3 facility, comprehensively integrating facility design, containment measures, sample handling, cryo-transfer systems, and decontamination protocols. To demonstrate the utility and reproducibility of this workflow, we applied cryo-electron tomography to investigate severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in its native, active state. Our observations confirm that unfixed viral particles display pleomorphic features comparable to those previously reported in fixed or inactivated preparations, validating that these structural characteristics represent native features rather than artifacts of chemical fixation. Furthermore, spatial redistribution of surface spikes was observed. The establishment of this robust BSL-3 cryo-EM workflow provides a practical blueprint for the structural characterization of emerging high-consequence pathogens, supporting pandemic preparedness, vaccine development, and antiviral discovery.

title: Host RNA-binding protein LARP6 controls SARS-CoV-2 programmed −1 ribosomal frameshifting
abstract: ABSTRACT Programmed −1 ribosomal frameshifting (−1PRF) is essential for the balanced expression of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) proteins and efficient viral replication, yet how host factors modulate this process remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify the host RNA-binding protein La-related protein 6 (LARP6) as a host regulator of this mechanism. Structural analysis and mutational dissection of the SARS-CoV-2 frameshifting element reveal that a three-stem-loop pseudoknot downstream of the slippery sequence is critical for efficient −1PRF. Using RNA pulldown and mass spectrometry, we identify LARP6 as a host factor that associates with the −1PRF pseudoknot. LARP6 associates with the viral RNA in a pseudoknot-dependent manner through multiple RNA-binding domains, and both loss- and restore-of-function analyses demonstrate that LARP6 promotes −1PRF efficiency. Mechanistically, LARP6 associates with ribosomal components in an mRNA-dependent manner, and changes in LARP6 expression are accompanied by corresponding changes in ribosome-associated RNA occupancy at the frameshifting region, consistent with a potential role in modulating ribosomal pausing. In a SARS-CoV-2 luciferase replicon, LARP6 overexpression increased RdRp protein levels, providing additional support for LARP6-mediated promotion of −1PRF in a viral genomic context. Together, our findings identify LARP6 as a host regulator of SARS-CoV-2 −1PRF and suggest that LARP6 may regulate frameshifting through its association with the viral pseudoknot and ribosomes. IMPORTANCE Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) relies on programmed −1 ribosomal frameshifting (−1PRF) to regulate the production of viral replicase proteins, making this process an important point of control in the viral life cycle. Although the viral RNA structures that promote −1PRF have been extensively studied, how host factors contribute to this process remains less well understood. Our study identifies LARP6 as a host protein associated with the SARS-CoV-2 −1PRF pseudoknot and reveals a potential link between LARP6-viral RNA interaction and ribosome behavior at the frameshifting site. These findings expand the current understanding of −1PRF regulation beyond viral RNA structures and suggest that host RNA-binding proteins may contribute to the control of viral gene expression by interacting with structured RNA elements. This work highlights the interaction of host RNA-binding proteins with viral RNA structures as a potentially important layer of translational regulation in coronaviruses.

title: The unequal burden of COVID-19 across Canadian provinces: Social determinants and public health responses
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed substantial social and regional inequalities across Canada. This study aims to examine variations in COVID-19 incidence across Canadian provinces between February 2020 and December 2022. The analysis investigates how social determinants, public health policy responses, and provincial political contexts were associated with confirmed COVID-19 cases across different levels of pandemic severity. STUDY DESIGN: This study employs a longitudinal ecological panel design. METHODS: The study uses weekly panel data from all ten Canadian provinces and integrates epidemiological health outputs, social determinants, public health policy measures, and political governance characteristics. Methodologically, the study applies the Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR) approach to examine heterogeneous relationships across different quantiles of confirmed COVID-19 cases. RESULTS: The findings reveal that the associations between the explanatory variables and COVID-19 cases varied across pandemic severity levels. Lower income, lower employment, lower education, limited healthcare access, and housing affordability pressures were generally associated with higher infection levels, particularly during severe outbreak periods. Government policy interventions also demonstrated heterogeneous associations across different levels of pandemic intensity. In addition, provincial political contexts were associated with variations in infection patterns across the distribution of confirmed cases. CONCLUSION: The findings highlight that effective pandemic preparedness depends not only on social determinants and public health measures, but also on broader structural, institutional, and governance contexts that shape policy priorities, resource allocation, and population health responses during future public health crises.

title: Microbial Diversity and Clinical Challenges of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia in COVID-19 Patients: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention
abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a serious lung infection that develops in patients receiving mechanical ventilation for at least 48 h. Critically ill COVID-19 patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) are particularly vulnerable to VAP, which contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality. This review summarizes current knowledge on the epidemiology, microbial diversity, clinical indicators, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of VAP in COVID-19 patients. The reported incidence of VAP among mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients ranges widely from 6% to 86%, reflecting differences in diagnostic criteria and study settings. The predominant bacterial pathogens include Staphylococcus aureus, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, and Enterobacter spp., with fungal pathogens such as Candida spp. and Aspergillus fumigatus also implicated. VAP in COVID-19 patients can progress to complications including lung abscess, particularly in severe cases, and is associated with prolonged ICU stays and increased mortality. Diagnosis relies on clinical, radiological, and microbiological criteria, with biomarkers such as procalcitonin showing promise for early detection. Empirical broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy is typically initiated, guided by local resistance patterns and individual risk factors, followed by pathogen-directed treatment when possible. Preventive strategies—including reducing airway colonization, preventing aspiration, and minimizing the duration of mechanical ventilation—are essential to reduce the VAP burden in this population. Given the high prevalence of multidrug-resistant pathogens and the complexity of diagnosis in COVID-19 patients, further research is needed to develop novel antimicrobial strategies and optimize preventive protocols.

title: mRNA-based anti-COVID-19 vaccines induced higher B cells and IgG levels than whole virus-based: A pilot study on Egyptian individuals
abstract: BackgroundB cells are critical components of vaccine-induced humoral immunity. However, circulating total B-cell measurements do not by themselves establish antigen specificity, memory differentiation, neutralizing activity, or protection. Aim: This exploratory observational study compared circulating CD19+ B-cell numbers and anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) binding antibody levels according to COVID-19 vaccine platform and time since vaccination.MethodsSixty-one participants were included: 52 vaccinated participants and 9 non-vaccinated participants. Vaccinated participants had received Pfizer (BNT162b2), ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, or inactivated-virus vaccines (Sinopharm or Sinovac). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed by flow cytometry using CD19 to quantify total circulating B cells, while anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike-RBD binding antibodies were measured using the Elecsys Anti-SARS-CoV-2 S assay.ResultsTotal CD19+ B-cell percentages and absolute numbers were not significantly different between the vaccinated platform groups and the non-vaccinated controls. Anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike-RBD binding antibody levels were significantly higher in vaccinated participants than in controls. The relationship between circulating CD19+ B-cell frequency and antibody concentration was weak.ConclusionThese exploratory findings suggest persistent humoral immune responses after COVID-19 vaccination but do not establish superiority of one vaccine platform. Because the study was limited by sample size, heterogeneous. vaccination histories, incomplete objective ascertainment of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, and use of a binding-antibody assay rather than a functional neutralization assay, the findings should be interpreted as preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies.

title: Nanotechnology-enabled drug delivery systems during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The COVID-19 outbreak has shown that the success of treatment is not only based on the drug’s inherent activity but also its capacity to get to the appropriate biological target at the right time and in a sufficient amount. Considering this, drug delivery systems based on nanotechnology have been gaining ground as potential platforms capable of overcoming formulation and drug delivery constraints related to many COVID-19 drugs, such as low solubility, instability, short half-life, limited access to the cell interior, and off-target toxicity affecting non-target cells. This piece of writing provides an overview of the main therapeutic approaches utilized during the COVID-19 crisis and aligns them with the delivery needs of various drug modalities, such as small molecules, biologics, nucleic acids, and combination therapies. Moreover, this review highlights the ability of nanoscale systems to enhance local exposure and minimize systemic exposure, coupled with the ability to control drug release and the impact of these nanosystems on pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics based on existing experimental and clinical data. Lung-targeted nanocarriers are the focus of this article, given the respiratory tract tropism of SARS-CoV-2. The rationale behind pulmonary delivery, aerosol deposition physics, lung biological barriers, and major safety issues are described and supported by nanocarrier properties for the lung and their applicability for SARS-CoV-2. In addition, the review discusses how nano-based systems can improve pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic performance by enhancing local drug exposure, reducing systemic distribution, and enabling controlled release. Finally, the quality of evidence from existing clinical studies is analyzed in detail, and important translational barriers hindering translation to clinical applications, such as good manufacturing practice compliant production, batch consistency, formulation-device compatibility, regulations, and scalability, are highlighted.

source_records.abstract: The COVID-19 outbreak has shown that the success of treatment is not only based on the drug’s inherent activity but also its capacity to get to the appropriate biological target at the right time and in a sufficient amount. Considering this, drug delivery systems based on nanotechnology have been gaining ground as potential platforms capable of overcoming formulation and drug delivery constraints related to many COVID-19 drugs, such as low solubility, instability, short half-life, limited access to the cell interior, and off-target toxicity affecting non-target cells. This piece of writing provides an overview of the main therapeutic approaches utilized during the COVID-19 crisis and aligns them with the delivery needs of various drug modalities, such as small molecules, biologics, nucleic acids, and combination therapies. Moreover, this review highlights the ability of nanoscale systems to enhance local exposure and minimize systemic exposure, coupled with the ability to control drug release and the impact of these nanosystems on pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics based on existing experimental and clinical data. Lung-targeted nanocarriers are the focus of this article, given the respiratory tract tropism of SARS-CoV-2. The rationale behind pulmonary delivery, aerosol deposition physics, lung biological barriers, and major safety issues are described and supported by nanocarrier properties for the lung and their applicability for SARS-CoV-2. In addition, the review discusses how nano-based systems can improve pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic performance by enhancing local drug exposure, reducing systemic distribution, and enabling controlled release. Finally, the quality of evidence from existing clinical studies is analyzed in detail, and important translational barriers hindering translation to clinical applications, such as good manufacturing practice compliant production, batch consistency, formulation-device compatibility, regulations, and scalability, are highlighted.

title: Effect of Pharmacist Involvement in COVID-19 Vaccination Campaign on Vaccine Coverage
abstract: Abstract To address the COVID-19 pandemic, promoting vaccination emerged as a preferred strategy to mitigate the harmful consequences of non-pharmaceutical interventions. In Europe, a measure adopted by several states was to authorize pharmacists to administer vaccines. The objective of this chapter is to assess whether this involvement could improve vaccination coverage. To do this, the synthetic control group method is used, due to a European framework conducive to its establishment. The results show an improvement in coverage with the first dose in Italy, but a degradation with the second dose. In Ireland, the opposite situation is observed. In France, due to the early adoption of the measure, no significant results were obtained. These elements imply for the legislator that the pharmacist can have different effects on vaccination coverage and that this must be considered taking into account epidemiological and vaccine issues, the spatial distribution of healthcare provision, and potentially its regulation.

title: Predictors of Preterm Delivery in the COVID-19 Era: A Retrospective Cohort Study of a Large, Integrated HealthSystem
abstract: INTRODUCTION Preterm delivery is the leading cause of perinatal mortality and long-term neonatal morbidity in the United States, and rates are rising. Research has shown that COVID-19 infection may increase the possibility of preterm delivery. However, these studies disproportionately focus on third trimester and iatrogenic cases, often overlooking risk across the entire pregnancy or without adjusting for prior preterm delivery and sociodemographic factors. To address these gaps, the authors investigated the association between COVID-19 at any point in pregnancy and preterm delivery while exploring other predictors of preterm delivery. METHODS The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study of members pregnant between March 2020 and March 2021, comparing odds of preterm delivery for those with and without COVID-19. Using logistic regression and χ2 tests, the authors explored associations between preterm delivery and other sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Data were abstracted from electronic medical records. RESULTS Of 14,250 participants, 994 (7%) experienced COVID-19 infection during pregnancy. Overall, 1313 (9%) had preterm delivery. In univariate logistic regression analyses, those with COVID-19 were more likely to be < 35 years old, Hispanic or Black, non-English-speaking, obese, and multiparous. COVID-19 infection during pregnancy was associated with increased odds of preterm delivery in the authors' unadjusted model but not in the multivariable adjusted model. Being ≥ 35 years old, Hispanic, Black, nulliparous, hypertensive, immunocompromised, or having a prior preterm delivery or gestational or chronic diabetes were significantly associated with higher odds of preterm delivery in the authors' multivariable model. CONCLUSION COVID-19 infection throughout pregnancy was not associated with increased odds of preterm delivery. Racial disparities and other key covariates like history of preterm delivery may confound the reported increase in preterm delivery.

title: Beyond Small Molecules: Computational and AI-Assisted Protein and Peptide Engineering Against the SARS-CoV-2 Nsp12–Nsp7–Nsp8 Replication Complex
abstract: Antiviral development against SARS-CoV-2 has focused largely on small-molecule inhibitors of the main protease and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and on antibodies targeting spike. Antigenic evolution has reduced the activity of many spike-directed antibodies, while resistance-associated substitutions have been identified for enzyme inhibitors. The nsp12–nsp7–nsp8 replication complex offers a complementary target: its subunit interfaces support assembly and processive RNA synthesis and may be accessible to engineered proteins and peptides. This review examines the structural and functional evidence for targeting these interfaces, the reported peptide and protein inhibitors, and the relevance of deep-learning-based binder design. The literature reviewed here reveals a methodological gap. Replication-complex inhibitors have predominantly been developed through molecular dynamics, interface analysis, docking, and structure-guided engineering, whereas contemporary generative design methods have been validated on other targets, including spike. These precedents support investigation of generative binders against the replication complex but do not establish their antiviral efficacy or resistance barrier. A proposed development framework integrates structural ensembles, interface energetics, sequence variation, and mechanistic validation. Intracellular delivery, target accessibility, proteolytic stability, and resistance remain important barriers to translation.

title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data
abstract: The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid population growth. From early sequence data collected in the US and the UK between 2021 and mid-2022, we identified two features—genetic diversity and graph connectivity—that allow us to reliably estimate growth rates of newly emerged lineages. To test our model, we used data collected from mid-2022 to end-2024 and accurately inferred the growth rates of lineages that appeared during this period. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for data collected in 2023 when the sequencing efforts were relatively high (thousands of sequences per day) in the US and the UK, our model correctly identified the most rapidly expanding lineages when they were still at low frequencies. Overall, our work provides a scalable and adaptable tool to estimate the growth rate of newly emerged SARS-CoV-2 lineages.

source_records.title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data.
source_records.abstract: The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid population growth. From early sequence data collected in the US and the UK between 2021 and mid-2022, we identified two features-genetic diversity and graph connectivity-that allow us to reliably estimate growth rates of newly emerged lineages. To test our model, we used data collected from mid-2022 to end-2024 and accurately inferred the growth rates of lineages that appeared during this period. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for data collected in 2023 when the sequencing efforts were relatively high (thousands of sequences per day) in the US and the UK, our model correctly identified the most rapidly expanding lineages when they were still at low frequencies. Overall, our work provides a scalable and adaptable tool to estimate the growth rate of newly emerged SARS-CoV-2 lineages.

title: Shield-and-Amplify Nanoparticle Vaccines Retune Immunodominance for Broad Protection against SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Abstract Antigenic variation severely constrains the durability and breadth of vaccine-induced protection against rapidly evolving viruses. Although conserved epitopes can support cross-variant immunity, antibody responses to viral glycoproteins are often biased toward exposed, mutable immunodominant epitopes, leaving conserved protective sites subdominant. We previously identified a cryptic, conserved class 5 epitope (the 6D6/7D6 epitope) on the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) capable of eliciting broad cross-neutralization. Here, we present a modular “shield-and-amplify” nanoparticle vaccination strategy to redirect immunodominance toward this subdominant epitope. We engineered site-specific N-linked glycans─alongside the native N343 glycan to mask variable immunodominant regions while preserving accessibility to the class 5 epitope. The resulting glycan-masked RBD antigen (RGM) was displayed on p239 nanoparticles via nanobody-mediated assembly, yielding multivalent RGM@p239 immunogens. Antigenic profiling revealed that glycan shielding preserved recognition by 6D6 and 7D6 antibodies while reducing binding of representative class 1–4 antibodies by at least 80%. In immunized animals, RGM@p239 enriched 7D6-competitive serum antibodies blocking approximately 70–80% of serum binding to RGM and broadened cross-variant neutralization against 8 representative variant strains, including detectable activity against Omicron lineages. Furthermore, RGM@p239 reduced disease severity after Omicron EG.1 challenge in a hamster model. These results support a model in which glycan shielding and nanoparticle multivalency act as complementary immune-focusing modules: shielding attenuates competing responses, while multivalency amplifies responses to conserved subdominant epitopes. This study establishes a nanovaccine design strategy to address antigenic variation by focusing immunity on conserved viral vulnerabilities.

title: ICU utilization, capacity strain, and mortality before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: RATIONALE: The COVID-19 pandemic created a unique instance of hospital capacity strain including deviations in ICU bed utilization. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate trends in ICU utilization among patients with common critical illness syndromes before, during, and after the pandemic, and across degrees of hospital capacity strain. hospitals across two health systems, 2013-2024, we performed a retrospective cohort study among high-acuity patients with sepsis and/or acute respiratory failure (ARF) who did not require mechanical ventilation or vasopressor support in the emergency department. We modeled ICU admission rates and hospital mortality across eras and associations between validated hospital strain indices and ICU admission. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: ICU admission rates decreased markedly from the pre-pandemic to the pandemic era and were sustained in the post-pandemic era: sepsis (n = 136,153) 24% (24-24%) pre-pandemic, 16% (15-16%) pandemic, and 14% (14-14%) post-pandemic; ARF (n = 63,290) 36% (35-36%) pre-pandemic, 25% (25-26%) pandemic, and 23% (22-24%) post-pandemic; all p < 0.001. Increasing hospital capacity strain was associated with reduced predicted probability of ICU admission (sepsis: 29% [29-30%] ICU admission at lowest strain to 9% [8-9%] at highest strain; ARF: 51% [49-52%] at lowest strain to 15% [14-16%] at highest strain; all p < 0.001). Compared to the pre-pandemic era, in the post-pandemic era patients with sepsis (11% [11-11%] vs. 14% [13-14%]) and ARF (12% [11-12%] vs. 14% [14-15%]) had reduced mortality (both p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Among high acuity patients with sepsis and ARF who did not require initial life support, ICU admission rates decreased during and after the pandemic.
journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

title: Five elements of psychological support in disaster recovery during the COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria, Australia between 2020 and 2022
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated public health interventions had profound effects on mental health worldwide. Pandemic preparedness must incorporate strategies to support mental health and psychological recovery, which should be underpinned by the five essential elements of disaster recovery – safety, calm, efficacy, connectedness, and hope. Residents of Victoria, Australia, experienced stringent non-pharmaceutical public health interventions to mitigate the spread of COVID-19 and associated health and health system impacts. Data from seven cross-sectional surveys of adults (the CARE Study) between April 2020 and April 2022 was used to explore how anxiety, depression, and the five elements presented in Victorians over time. Multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) was utilised to understand the essential elements most closely related to mental health. Symptoms of depression and anxiety fluctuated over the pandemic, peaking in September 2021, when Victoria was midway through an 82-day long lockdown. This coincided with lowest observed levels of efficacy, hope, and connectedness. Anxiety symptoms were lowest in May 2020, when participants’ efficacy, hope and connectedness were highest. MCA results suggest that a stronger sense of efficacy, hope and connectedness was associated with lower anxiety and depression. Conversely, high levels of anxiety and depression were associated with lower efficacy, less hope, and feeling disconnected. These results highlight efficacy, connectedness and hope as key targets for mental health interventions in outbreak scenarios. Further work is required to understand the nuances of resilience and psychological response in the context of a pandemic, to facilitate rapid identification of at-risk groups and tailor effective, targeted interventions.
journal: Journal of Disaster Science and Management

title: The absence of microbiome in germ-free mice exacerbates the pathogenicity of mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 MA10
abstract: Abstract Germ-free mice, which are devoid of microbiota, provide a powerful system to define the contribution of the microbiome to host responses during infection. Severe COVID-19 outcomes are associated with multiple comorbidities that are themselves characterized by microbiome dysbiosis; however, the causal role of the microbiota in SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis remains poorly understood. Here, we use germ-free mouse models to evaluate the impact of the microbiome on disease severity following infection with mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 MA10. Comparison with conventionally housed mice revealed that the absence of the microbiome markedly exacerbates SARS-CoV-2–induced disease in both C57BL/6 and Swiss Webster backgrounds. Germ-free mice exhibited greater weight loss, impaired lung function, worsened pulmonary pathology, and pronounced alterations in circulating cytokine and chemokine profiles compared with conventional controls. These findings show that resident microbiota limit SARS-CoV-2 pathogenicity and establish germ-free COVID-19 models as a powerful platform to identify protective microbial taxa and microbiota-based interventions to reduce severe disease.

title: SARS-CoV-2 susceptibility and vulnerability of human blastocysts during in vitro preimplantation development
abstract: Human preimplantation embryos express the SARS-CoV-2 entry factors ACE2, TMPRSS2 and BSG (CD147) on trophectoderm (TE) cells, suggesting susceptibility to infection. Likewise, SARS-CoV-2-pseudotyped reporter viruses induced cytopathic effects in blastocysts, while the zona pellucida (ZP) appeared to confer partial protection. The impact of authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection on embryonic lineage specification and developmental competence has not been established. Here, we exposed cryopreserved human embryos, donated under ethics approval and informed consent, to authentic SARS-CoV-2 (B.1.617.2, Delta variant). While embryos with an intact ZP remained uninfected, laser-assisted hatching rendered 19/21 (90.5%) of embryos susceptible to infection, as confirmed by detection of viral dsRNA. Moreover, SARS-CoV-2 infection had a pronounced effect on blastocyst development with a possibly fatal outcome. Compared to mock-treated embryos (n = 47), infected blastocysts (n = 48) showed a significantly reduced surface area (p = 0.0003), reduced total cell number (p = 0.0139), and reduced NANOG+ epiblast cell numbers (p = 0.0054) 24 hours post-exposure, while the number of GATA4+ primitive endoderm cells remained unaffected (p = 0.5255). Intriguingly, despite viral replication being largely confined to the trophectoderm (TE), this selective epiblast reduction suggests a disruption of TE-derived paracrine signaling required for epiblast specification. Finally, prolonged viral replication resulted in embryonic lysis and death. Digital transcriptomic profiling (mock, n = 29 embryos; SARS-CoV-2, n = 28 embryos; each in n = 5 minipools) revealed upregulation of innate antiviral and inflammatory genes, including IFIH1, IRF7, NOD2, and TNFRSF1A, as well as the recently identified SARS-CoV-2 entry factor TMEM106B, alongside altered developmental signatures concerning genome activation, pluripotency, and lineage-specific programs. These findings show that ZP disruption makes human blastocysts susceptible to productive SARS-CoV-2 infection, with adverse consequences for lineage allocation and direct implications for biosafety and virological counselling in medically assisted reproduction practice. title: A Novel B-Cell-Targeted Adjuvant APRIL Improves the Breadth and Persistence of Anti-SARS-CoV-2 Immunity
abstract: Background: A broad, robust, and long-lasting antibody response is essential for effective anti-SARS-CoV-2 immunity and the prevention of breakthrough infections. As a key member of the tumor necrosis factor superfamily, a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) participates in multiple B cell fate processes, including B cell survival, class-switch recombination, and plasma cell (PC) differentiation, but its potential utility as a SARS-CoV-2 vaccine adjuvant remains largely unexplored. Methods: Balb/c mice were immunized with recombinant XBB.1.5 S protein formulated with alum, with or without the addition of APRIL. Serum, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), and fecal samples were collected for measuring antigen-specific IgG/IgA titers and antibody avidity by ELISA. Neutralization against Delta, BA.2.12.1, BF.7, XBB.1.5, and JN.1 was determined in HEK293-ACE2 cells, while cellular responses were assessed by flow cytometry and Enzyme-Linked Immunospot (ELISPOT). Gene expressions were quantified by RT-PCR. Results: APRIL augmented the immunogenicity of XBB.1.5 S in a dose-dependent manner. It promoted the generation of both systemic and mucosal antibodies, broadened the binding breadth and avidity, and conferred superior neutralizing activity against multiple variants. During a 20-week post-immunization monitoring period, mice maintained effective antibody titers and retained the capacity to neutralize diverse variants. Mechanistically, APRIL was associated with upregulated AICDA and UNG mRNA expressions, accompanied by expansion of the B cell repertoire, differentiation into PCs and antigen-specific memory B cells, and maintenance of high-avidity long-lived PCs. Conclusions: APRIL acts as an effective adjuvant that elicits broad-spectrum, long-lasting immunity against SARS-CoV-2 variants. It represents a promising immunostimulatory component for optimizing the performance of recombinant spike protein vaccines.

title: Letter to the Editor: Coronavirus disease 2019, multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and children’s hearts: Finding answers with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: The article refers to “Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3” by OV et al published in the World Journal of Clinical Pediatrics , multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its cardiovascular complications. MIS-C frequently causes cardiovascular complications, including coronary artery dilatation, low left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction, diastolic dysfunction, myocarditis, and pericardial effusion, decreases over time, usually resolving within 6-9 months after the disease onset. Echocardiographic evaluations reveal mild to moderate LV dysfunction, resolving within two weeks. Severe dysfunction normalizes after approximately 1.5 months. Global longitudinal strain proves valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage. Long-term effects based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) data indicate the persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosisupto12 months after the initialevent. Signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period. CMRI is an important additional method in the assessment of children who have experienced multisystem inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19, especially in patients with persistent symptoms or abnormal data from other cardiac findings.

title: Do vaccines move votes? Chinese COVID-19 donations and UN General Assembly alignment
abstract: Abstract When President Xi Jinping declared China's COVID-19 vaccines a "global public good", it ignited a fierce debate over whether Beijing was practicing pure altruism or deploying a strategic tool to buy geopolitical influence. Yet, existing work documents who received these doses rather than the geopolitical impact of their receipt, failing to explain why vaccine donations produced such non-uniform political returns. This paper resolves this puzzle by showing that donation operates as a strategic signal under uncertainty, meaning alignment is strictly conditional on a recipient’s initial political distance from China. The model predicts political movement among recipients that begin politically distant, but a saturation effect with limited returns among those with close existing ties. Utilizing a staggered difference-in-differences design applied to UN General Assembly ideal point estimates from 2015 to 2023, I confirm this precise pattern. Politically distant recipients show a statistically significant shift toward China after donation, whereas no comparable effect is observed among countries with close existing ties. Ultimately, material generosity only buys influence within limits set by a recipient's prior beliefs.

title: Multi-model insights into racial and ethnic heterogeneities in early COVID-19 transmission and severity in the U.S.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic was marked by unequal disease burden across racial and ethnic groups in the US. Using a multi-model ensemble framework, we retrospectively assessed the impact of racial and ethnic heterogeneities in COVID-19 transmission and disease severity on mortality during the winter 2020-2021 surge in California and North Carolina. Models incorporating race and ethnicity projected mortality more accurately than null models, while the ensemble outperformed all individual models on average by weighted interval scores. Eliminating transmission heterogeneities produced larger mortality reductions than eliminating severity differences alone, particularly for Latino populations in California (55% reduction) and Black populations in North Carolina (28% reduction). Reducing severity heterogeneity also lowered mortality, with the greatest benefit among Black populations in both states (21% and 16% reductions in California and North Carolina, respectively). Eliminating both transmission and severity heterogeneity yielded the largest reductions overall, predicting 49-70% lower mortality across racial and ethnic groups in California and 23-40% in North Carolina. Mitigating transmission inequities also produced indirect benefits for non-targeted populations, highlighting the broad impact of reducing disparities in exposure risk and access to protective resources.

title: Computational evaluation of chromone–tetrazole hybrids as noncovalent inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro
abstract: Emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants continue to demand orally tractable, non-covalent inhibitors of the conserved main protease (M pro ). Here, chromone-phenyl-tetrazole hybrids were prioritized using a multiscale computational strategy that connects drug-likeness, binding stability, free-energy ranking, conformational behavior, and quantum-level electronic features. The series showed favorable oral drug-like profiles and low-to-moderate predicted acute toxicity. Among the stable M pro complexes, M2 displayed the strongest computed affinity (MM/GBSA ΔG bind = −38.8 kcal·mol − 1), driven mainly by dispersion with limited desolvation cost, whereas M4 showed the most direct catalytic-dyad engagement through His41/Cys145-supported anchoring. DFT analysis rationalized these complementary profiles: M2 and M4 exhibited narrower HOMO-LUMO gaps (4.00 eV) and higher electronic softness, while ELF/NCI maps revealed heteroatom-centered electron reservoirs and weak intramolecular preorganization. The derived pharmacophore consists of a planar chromone π-platform bearing a carbonyl/phenolic acceptor-donor edge, a para-phenyl spacer for conjugation and hydrophobic occupancy, and a methoxy-tetrazole polar/π-rich head for Glu166/Phe140/His163 anchoring. Overall, M2 and M4 emerge as complementary lead chemotypes for experimental validation and structure-guided optimization against M pro .

title: Climate-Driven Perturbations in Influenza Subtype Positivity Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered global influenza transmission patterns. Whether the associations among meteorological conditions, visibility, and influenza subtype (A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria) positivity changed after the pandemic remains unclear. We compared these associations before and after the COVID-19 pandemic in northern China. Objective This study aimed to characterize changes in the associations of meteorological variables and visibility with influenza subtype positivity before and after the COVID-19 pandemic and to identify subtype-specific nonlinear patterns and thresholds. Methods Using 13 years of influenza surveillance and environmental data, we applied Extreme Gradient Boosting enhanced with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to characterize the relative importance and direction of associations between environmental variables and influenza subtype positivity. Generalized additive models (GAMs) were subsequently used to characterize nonlinear association patterns and identify thresholds at which the direction of model-estimated associations changed. Results Absolute humidity (AH) remained the most influential environmental factor for A/H3N2 and A/H1N1, accounting for 32.2% and 38.5% of relative feature importance, respectively. Visibility increased in importance after the pandemic, rising from being the fourth to the second most influential environmental indicator. GAM analysis identified thresholds corresponding to points where the direction of the associations changed. For A/H3N2, AH below 4 g/m 3 was associated with positive SHAP values, whereas higher AH was predominantly associated with negative SHAP values. For A/H1N1, the direction of association changed at an AH threshold of 4.5 g/m 3 (95% CI 4.0-4.8) in the postpandemic period. Additionally, relative humidity (RH) demonstrated a complex nonlinear association with A/H3N2 positivity, with transition points at 45.1% (95% CI 43.5%-46.1%) and 69.7% (95% CI 69.2%-70.2%) in the prepandemic period and at 48.7% (95% CI 46.7%-50.4%) and 70.6% (95% CI 66.3%-72.6%) in the postpandemic period. RH values within these ranges were associated with negative SHAP values, whereas values outside these ranges were associated with positive SHAP values. In contrast, visibility showed opposing association patterns for the A/H3N2 and B/Victoria subtypes after the pandemic. Visibility below 17.1 km (95% CI 16.3-17.4) was associated with negative SHAP values for A/H3N2, whereas visibility below 18.4 km (95% CI 18.0-18.9) was associated with positive SHAP values for B/Victoria. Conclusions AH remained a key environmental determinant of influenza A subtype positivity, while visibility became more important after the pandemic and showed opposing association patterns for A/H3N2 and B/Victoria. The identified nonlinear thresholds highlight subtype-specific environmental associations and may inform influenza surveillance and risk assessment under changing environmental conditions.
