Whether the associations among meteorological conditions, visibility, and influenza subtype (A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria) positivity changed after the pandemic remains unclear. We compared these associations before and after the COVID-19 pandemic in northern China. Objective This study aimed to characterize changes in the associations of meteorological variables and visibility with influenza subtype positivity before and after the COVID-19 pandemic and to identify subtype-specific nonlinear patterns and thresholds. Methods Using 13 years of influenza surveillance and environmental data, we applied Extreme Gradient Boosting enhanced with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to characterize the relative importance and direction of associations between environmental variables and influenza subtype positivity. Generalized additive models (GAMs) were subsequently used to characterize nonlinear association patterns and identify thresholds at which the direction of model-estimated associations changed. Results Absolute humidity (AH) remained the most influential environmental factor for A/H3N2 and A/H1N1, accounting for 32.2% and 38.5% of relative feature importance, respectively. Visibility increased in importance after the pandemic, rising from being the fourth to the second most influential environmental indicator. GAM analysis identified thresholds corresponding to points where the direction of the associations changed. For A/H3N2, AH below 4 g/m3 was associated with positive SHAP values, whereas higher AH was predominantly associated with negative SHAP values. For A/H1N1, the direction of association changed at an AH threshold of 4.5 g/m3 (95% CI 4.0-4.8) in the postpandemic period. Additionally, relative humidity (RH) demonstrated a complex nonlinear association with A/H3N2 positivity, with transition points at 45.1% (95% CI 43.5%-46.1%) and 69.7% (95% CI 69.2%-70.2%) in the prepandemic period and at 48.7% (95% CI 46.7%-50.4%) and 70.6% (95% CI 66.3%-72.6%) in the postpandemic period. RH values within these ranges were associated with negative SHAP values, whereas values outside these ranges were associated with positive SHAP values. In contrast, visibility showed opposing association patterns for the A/H3N2 and B/Victoria subtypes after the pandemic. Visibility below 17.1 km (95% CI 16.3-17.4) was associated with negative SHAP values for A/H3N2, whereas visibility below 18.4 km (95% CI 18.0-18.9) was associated with positive SHAP values for B/Victoria. Conclusions AH remained a key environmental determinant of influenza A subtype positivity, while visibility became more important after the pandemic and showed opposing association patterns for A/H3N2 and B/Victoria. The identified nonlinear thresholds highlight subtype-specific environmental associations and may inform influenza surveillance and risk assessment under changing environmental conditions.

title: Learning from COVID-19 to strengthen hantavirus preparedness and public health response
abstract: Years after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the world continues to face significant health, social, and economic challenges, while emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases remain a growing global public health concern. This trend highlights the importance of interconnected health systems and reveals both the strengths and weaknesses of global public health preparedness and response. In this context, we present a comparative analysis of the COVID-19 pandemic and the recent Andes virus outbreak, focusing on their epidemiological and virological characteristics, and discussing the effectiveness of the COVID-19 public health responses. We also explore key lessons that can be applied to future zoonotic threats in the context of rapidly changing ecosystems. The results reveal that COVID-19 and hantavirus infections share several molecular and clinical features but differ in their transmission patterns. COVID-19 spreads efficiently between humans and caused a global pandemic, whereas Hantavirus infections are mainly transmitted from rodents to humans and remain geographically localized despite a higher case fatality rate. While vaccines are available for COVID-19, none exist for Hantavirus disease. The study also highlights the value of artificial intelligence, epidemic intelligence, and the One Health approach for improving outbreak prediction, detection, and surveillance.

title: Neuropsychiatric long COVID is associated with altered SARS-CoV-2-specific cellular-humoral coordination and diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity up to 12 months post-COVID-19 symptom onset
abstract: ABSTRACT Long COVID is a chronic multisystemic condition estimated to affect approximately 400 million people worldwide. Although underlying mechanisms remain elusive, persistent SARS-CoV-2 reservoirs and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) reactivation have been implicated. We compared SARS-CoV-2- and EBV-specific cellular and humoral immunity between 27 long COVID individuals with ≥2 neuropsychiatric symptoms and 27 matched recovered participants at 3–6 months post-COVID-19 symptom onset (PSO). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were assessed for IFN-γ, IL-2, TNF, and granzyme B T-cell responses against SARS-CoV-2, EBV, and HCMV. Sera were evaluated for neutralizing activity against live ancestral SARS-CoV-2 and EBV, while EBV reactivation was assessed by anti-early antigen-diffuse IgG and anti-viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM. We observed no significant differences in SARS-CoV-2-, EBV-, or HCMV-specific Th1-type/cytotoxic T-cell responses or live virus neutralization between long COVID and recovered groups at 3–6 months PSO. Although SARS-CoV-2-specific IFN-γ and IL-2 T-cell responses correlated with serological neutralizing capacity in recovered participants, no such associations were observed in the long COVID group, suggesting altered coordination between cellular and humoral immunity. EBV reactivation was only detected in one neuropsychiatric long COVID participant. However, EBV anti-VCA IgG antibody levels were significantly diminished in long COVID participants at 3–6 months PSO. Reports of fatigue at 12 months PSO were also associated with reduced EBV neutralizing capacity at 3–6 months PSO. Diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity and dysregulated coordination between SARS-CoV-2-specific cellular and humoral immunity may thus represent potential prognostic markers for neuropsychiatric long COVID development and fatigue up to 12 months PSO. IMPORTANCE We performed a comprehensive analysis of cellular and humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and human cytomegalovirus in individuals with neuropsychiatric long COVID, a subgroup that remains poorly characterized. Although no differences in virus-specific Th1-type or cytotoxic T-cell immunity were observed between individuals with long COVID and recovered individuals, altered coordination between SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell and neutralizing humoral immunity was observed in the long COVID group at 3–6 months post-COVID-19 symptom onset (PSO). Diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity was also associated with neuropsychiatric long COVID and fatigue up to 12 months PSO. Together, these findings suggest that altered SARS-CoV-2-specific cellular-humoral immune coordination and diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity may contribute to the development or persistence of neuropsychiatric long COVID and highlight a promising future direction for mechanistic studies. title: Epigenetic alterations in the placenta associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy
abstract: Abstract Histone modifications play a key role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulatory potential. Previously, reduced levels of trimethylated histone H3K4me3 and acetylated H3K9ac were observed in placentas from women with preeclampsia. Building on these findings, this study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy or at delivery is associated with changes in placental histone modifications. Immunohistochemical staining, exploratory western blot analysis, and qualitative immunofluorescence were performed on placental sections from 60 patients stratified into four groups: women with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery, women with prior infection during gestation, vaccinated controls, and unvaccinated controls. H3K4me3 levels in the syncytiotrophoblast were significantly reduced in both SARS-CoV-2-exposed groups compared to unvaccinated controls, with the most pronounced reduction observed in women with prior infection during gestation. H3K9ac levels did not differ significantly between groups in any compartment after correction for multiple comparisons. No significant associations were found between SCT H3K4me3 levels and maternal age, gestational age, or birthweight, and a sensitivity analysis excluding cases with additional placental pathologies confirmed the robustness of the findings. As no gene expression profiling was performed, functional or transcriptional consequences of the observed H3K4me3 changes cannot be inferred. These descriptive findings warrant further investigation integrating epigenetic and transcriptomic approaches to clarify their functional relevance for placental biology and pregnancy outcomes.

title: Comparative Computational Analysis of Natural Compounds Against SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein Structural Conformations
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 Spike glycoprotein plays a critical role in viral entry into host cells through its interaction with the human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an important target for antiviral drug discovery. This study employed an integrated computational approach to investigate the binding potential of twenty natural compounds against two experimentally determined SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein structures (PDB IDs: 6M17 and 7A91). Molecular docking identified Amentoflavone as the most favourable ref-erence compound against both structures, with binding energies of -10.4 and -9.8 kcal/mol, respectively. Further evaluation of Amentoflavone analogues identified A63 (CHEMBL187504) as a promising candidate, exhibiting more favourable docking scores of approximately -11.3 kcal/mol against 6M17 and -10.1 kcal/mol against 7A91. Molecular dynamics simulations over 100 ns revealed structure-dependent differences in conforma-tional behaviour, residue flexibility, protein compactness, solvent exposure and intermo-lecular hydrogen-bond persistence. MM-PBSA calculations further indicated favourable binding free energies for all four investigated complexes, with 6M17-Amentoflavone (-78.450 ± 13.922 kJ/mol) and 7A91-A63 (-80.769 ± 16.410 kJ/mol) exhibiting the most fa-vourable energetic profiles for their respective structures. Energy decomposition high-lighted van der Waals and electrostatic interactions as major favourable contributors, while residue-wise analysis identified potential amino acid interaction hotspots involved in ligand stabilisation. Overall, the findings demonstrate that Amentoflavone and its ana-logue A63 exhibit promising, structure-dependent computational binding profiles against SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein structures. These findings provide a basis for further structural optimisation and experimental investigations to establish their potential to interfere with Spike-mediated viral entry.

title: Influenza A/B, RSV and SARS-CoV-2 Co-Detection Among Adults with Acute Respiratory Illness in Zimbabwe, 2022–2023: A Sub-Study of a COVID-19 Vaccine Effectiveness Study
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) cause overlapping respiratory illness, but Zimbabwean adult multipathogen data remain limited. We described influenza and RSV detection and co-detection with SARS-CoV-2 among adults enrolled in the ZIMCOVVAR study. Methods: This retrospective sub-study included nasopharyngeal specimens from adults with acute respiratory illness recruited in six Zimbabwean provinces during 2022-2023. Following exclusion of duplicate and unlinked records, 1,429 participants were analyzed. Influenza A, influenza B, and RSV were tested by multiplex real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR); recorded target cycle thresholds (Ct) ≤30 were provisionally classified as signals. Valid target-specific denominators remained unresolved. Proportions, confidence intervals, monthly patterns, and associations with SARS-CoV-2 status were examined. Results: The analytic cohort comprised 281 SARS-CoV-2-positive and 1,148 negative participants; median age was 35 years and 68.2% were female. Ct-defined influenza A, RSV, and influenza B signals occurred in 191/1,429 (13.4%), 53/1,429 (3.7%), and 2/1,429 (0.1%), respectively. Influenza A was recorded in 68/281 (24.2%) SARS-CoV-2-positive versus 123/1,148 (10.7%) negative participants. RSV was recorded in 3/281 (1.1%) versus 50/1,148 (4.4%), respectively. These are provisional signals per linked record, not valid-result positivity estimates; testing-group exclusion reversed the adjusted association. Conclusions: The selected adult cohort showed recorded influenza and RSV detections alongside SARS-CoV-2, supporting continued investigation of multiple respiratory pathogens in symptomatic adults. The findings require cautious interpretation because of nonrepresentative sampling and unresolved testing-group effects; quality-assured, multi-season surveillance is needed to inform local prevention planning.

title: Delayed first contact in a universally insured population: time to care and COVID-19 outcomes in Mexican primary care
abstract: Time from symptom onset to first care may be a modifiable determinant of COVID-19 outcomes, but it is rarely quantified in primary care. This retrospective cohort study included all 5,248 confirmed SARS-CoV-2 cases (RT-PCR or certified rapid antigen test) notified to the national surveillance system (SINOLAVE) by a large family medicine unit of the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) in Leon, Mexico, between April 2020 and April 2021. Pandemic waves were classified using the official IMSS definition. Wave profiles were compared with chi-square tests and Bonferroni correction, and predictors of death were assessed by multivariable logistic regression, with sensitivity analyses adjusting for severity signs at first contact. Of the cases, 53.8% were female, mean age was 41.1 years, and 317 deaths (6.0%) were registered. Median time to first care was 3 days (interquartile range: 2-5). Case fatality was 3.0% among patients presenting within 3 days and 9.1% among those presenting later. Later presentation (> 3 days) was associated with death (adjusted odds ratio = 1.98; 95% confidence interval: 1.47-2.65), but the association was attenuated after adjustment for severity signs at first contact (adjusted odds ratio = 1.20; 95% confidence interval: 0.85-1.69), which were more frequent among later presenters (21.8% vs. From the first to the second wave, fever (76.1% to 56.9%), diabetes (22.8% to 9.6%), and case fatality (10.5% to 4.8%) decreased, whereas anosmia and dysgeusia increased (all p < 0.001). Surveillance data cannot distinguish clinical progression during delay from late presentation of already severe patients. Delay persisted despite universal entitlement to care, indicating that insurance coverage alone did not ensure timely presentation; prospective cohorts measuring severity at onset are needed.

title: Barriers and Enablers of COVID-19 Vaccination Among Black, Eastern European, and Low Socioeconomic Status Communities in Canada
abstract: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated existing health inequities in Canada and globally. Vaccination remains a key protective behaviour, but some population groups have lower uptake. We aimed to identify factors that influence COVID-19 vaccine uptake in three groups prioritised by local public health officials in Ontario, Canada. Methods We partnered with local public health units and community members from prioritised communities (Black, Eastern European, and neighbourhoods with low uptake) to investigate population-specific barriers and enablers of COVID-19 vaccine uptake using behavioural science. Interviews in English, French, Arabic, Ukrainian, Russian, and Polish (with interpreters/translators) explored factors influencing COVID-19 vaccination (first dose and first booster dose). The Theoretical Domains Framework guided data collection and analysis. Results We interviewed 68 participants (78% female; M age = 35–42 years, range = 19–75 years) across three groups, with diverse self-identified races and ethnicities. Half (52%) had received two doses and 25% had received one or zero. Many expressed hesitancy or fear regarding COVID-19 vaccines. Social influences was a prominent domain. Six themes of barriers and enablers were identified: 1) knowledge, resources and skills to access vaccine; 2) salient experiences with vaccines or infection; 3) personal risk assessment; 4) trust versus mistrust in health systems; 5) interplay between vaccine mandates and intention; and 6) memory and attention. Conclusions Findings illustrate barriers and enablers for specific populations with low vaccine uptake. Context‐specific, community‐driven trust‐building efforts remain essential for improving uptake. Further work should elucidate the behavioural, social and environmental determinants of vaccination among underserved populations and communities across global diasporas.

title: Health conditions of migrant men during the COVID-19 pandemic: a cross-cultural reflection in the light of Leininger’s Theory Condiciones de salud de los hombres migrantes durante la pandemia de COVID-19: reflexión transcultural a la luz de la Teoría de Leininger Desafios de saúde de homens migrantes na covid-19: análise transcultural sob o Modelo de Purnell e a Teoria de Leininger
abstract: A pandemia de covid-19 acentuou desigualdades sociais, econômicas e sanitárias, afetando desproporcionalmente populações vulneráveis. Este estudo objetivou analisar as condições de saúde de homens imigrantes, refugiados e solicitantes de asilo durante a pandemia de covid-19, à luz da Teoria da Diversidade e Universalidade do Cuidado Cultural (TDUCC). Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, de natureza teórico-reflexiva, fundamentada na TDUCC, proposta por Madeleine Leininger. Foram identificadas 12 problemáticas relacionadas às condições de saúde dos homens migrantes, destacando-se a precarização social, o racismo institucional, a hesitação vacinal e o déficit na atenção psicossocial. A pandemia intensificou desigualdades estruturais e repercutiu negativamente na saúde física, mental e social. A análise fundamentada na TDUCC permitiu interpretar essas problemáticas segundo as modalidades de preservação ou manutenção cultural, acomodação ou negociação cultural e reestruturação ou repadronização cultural do cuidado. A pandemia evidenciou a urgência de políticas culturalmente sensíveis e de ações de enfermagem culturalmente competentes. O cuidado culturalmente congruente constitui uma estratégia relevante para reduzir barreiras de acesso e promover a equidade e a justiça social na atenção à saúde dos homens migrantes.

source_records.title: Health conditions of migrant men during the COVID-19 pandemic: a cross-cultural reflection in the light of Leininger’s Theory Condiciones de salud de los hombres migrantes durante la pandemia de COVID-19: reflexión transcultural a la luz de la Teoría de Leininger Desafios de saúde de homens migrantes na covid-19: análise transcultural sob o Modelo de Purnell e a Teoria de Leininger
source_records.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accentuated social, economic, and health inequalities, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations. This study aimed to analyze the health conditions of immigrant, refugee, and asylum-seeking men during the COVID-19 pandemic, in the light of the Theory of Culture Care Diversity and Universality (TCCDU). This is a narrative literature review of a theoretical-reflective nature, based on the TCCDU, proposed by Madeleine Leininger. Twelve problematic issues related to the health conditions of migrant men were identified, highlighting social precarization, institutional racism, vaccine hesitancy, and the deficit in psychosocial care. The pandemic intensified structural inequalities and negatively impacted physical, mental, and social health. The analysis based on the TCCDU allowed the interpretation of these problematic issues according to the modalities of cultural care preservation or maintenance, cultural care accommodation or negotiation, and cultural care repatterning or restructuring. The pandemic highlighted the urgency for culturally sensitive policies and culturally competent nursing actions. Culturally congruent care constitutes a relevant strategy for reducing access barriers and promoting equity and social justice in the healthcare of migrant men.

title: Translational Tools to Track the SARS-CoV-2 Pandemic
abstract: The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 virus has driven research towards multiple new directions, namely that of RNA therapeutics due to the successful development of the mRNA vaccines. Presently, gene therapy represents a new strategy towards many infectious diseases. With the rise of circular RNA and anti-sense technologies for therapeutics, we sought to combine these aspects with the negative-strand synthesis mechanism of SARS-COV-2 such that the virus would mechanistically attack itself upon infection. While successful as a proof-of-concept study, it requires extensive remodeling and experimentation to determine the efficacy of such a design. However, during this study of therapeutic development, it became paramount to understand fundamental aspects of the SARS-CoV-2 lifecycle, particularly how and why it was phenotypically changing. While it is clear pre-omicron variants utilised the TMPRSS2-mediated pathway for viral replication, the utility of this route is now unclear within Omicron variants and warrants investigation to understand the trajectory of SARS-COV-2 evolution, and thus further improve the current viral surveillance platform. Findings regarding the Omicron lineage have proven more fruitful, with results conclusively demonstrating that the lineage has undergone a tropism shift. With focus on the ACE2-TMPRSS2 complexing as the likely cause for inefficient viral replication, results determined that disruption of this complex by ACE2 binding to SLC6A19 or SLC6A20 to create a Chaperone-ACE2 environment rescued TMPRSS2-mediated host cell entry. This biology was then integrated into viral surveillance platforms, which enabled isolation of primary Omicron variants from nasal swabs. Whilst prior studies suggest the Omicron lineage to enter via endocytosis, the work herein resolves the in vitro mechanisms of these initial observations and importantly expands factors linked to ACE2 and TMPRSS2 that reveal a new paradigm of SARS-CoV-2 host cell factors. Here, the inclusion of ACE2 binding solute carriers SLC6A19 and SLC6A20 reveals how the largest pool of ACE2 in vivo exists, and how this pool has influenced SARS-CoV-2 replication over the pandemic.

title: Pre-pandemic Probable Sarcopenia and COVID-19-Related Healthcare Utilization Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults : A Retrospective Cohort from Health and Retirement Study.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia has become a significant concern that detrimentally affects older adults' health. Patients with sarcopenia demonstrated higher disease severity and mortality rates of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). This study aims to evaluate the effect of pre-pandemic probable sarcopenia on COVID-19 related healthcare demands among older adults living in community settings. Methods The study was conducted using a Health and Retirement Study, a national representative dataset for older adults in the US. The study included participants with COVID-19 diagnosis and retrospectively assessing their sarcopenia status using a SARC-F questionnaire. Results The study cohort included 354 participants with COVID-19 with a mean age of 61.03 years (SD = 9.49). Probable sarcopenia was identified in 13.56% of the study population. In adjusted analyses, probable sarcopenia was independently associated with higher odds of COVID-19-related emergency room visits (OR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.03-4.57), hospitalization (OR = 3.12, 95% CI: 1.37-7.12), and oxygen or ventilator requirement (OR = 3.15, 95% CI: 1.08-9.21). Female sex was associated with lower odds of hospitalization and oxygen/ventilator requirement. Non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic participants demonstrated significantly higher odds of COVID-19-related healthcare utilization compared with Non-Hispanic White participants. No statistically significant interaction effects were observed between probable sarcopenia and sex or physical activity. Conclusion Pre-pandemic probable sarcopenia was independently associated with increased COVID-19-related healthcare utilization among community-dwelling older adults. These findings highlight the importance of early identification and management of sarcopenia in older adults to potentially reduce severe COVID-19 outcomes. Further studies are warranted to evaluate targeted preventive interventions.

source_records.title: Pre-pandemic Probable Sarcopenia and COVID-19-Related Healthcare Utilization Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults : A Retrospective Cohort from Health and Retirement Study.
source_records.abstract: Background Sarcopenia has become a significant concern that detrimentally affects older adults' health. Patients with sarcopenia demonstrated higher disease severity and mortality rates of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). This study aims to evaluate the effect of pre-pandemic probable sarcopenia on COVID-19 related healthcare demands among older adults living in community settings. Methods The study was conducted using a Health and Retirement Study, a national representative dataset for older adults in the US. The study included participants with COVID-19 diagnosis and retrospectively assessing their sarcopenia status using a SARC-F questionnaire. Results The study cohort included 354 participants with COVID-19 with a mean age of 61.03 years (SD = 9.49). Probable sarcopenia was identified in 13.56% of the study population. In adjusted analyses, probable sarcopenia was independently associated with higher odds of COVID-19-related emergency room visits (OR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.03-4.57), hospitalization (OR = 3.12, 95% CI: 1.37-7.12), and oxygen or ventilator requirement (OR = 3.15, 95% CI: 1.08-9.21). Female sex was associated with lower odds of hospitalization and oxygen/ventilator requirement. Non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic participants demonstrated significantly higher odds of COVID-19-related healthcare utilization compared with Non-Hispanic White participants. No statistically significant interaction effects were observed between probable sarcopenia and sex or physical activity. Conclusion Pre-pandemic probable sarcopenia was independently associated with increased COVID-19-related healthcare utilization among community-dwelling older adults. These findings highlight the importance of early identification and management of sarcopenia in older adults to potentially reduce severe COVID-19 outcomes. Further studies are warranted to evaluate targeted preventive interventions.

title: Associations between substance use and symptomatic Long COVID in the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)‐adult cohort study
abstract: AIMS: To determine whether frequency of tobacco, cannabis and binge alcohol use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 test result or COVID-19 symptom onset is associated with (1) presence of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and (2) development of symptomatic Long COVID over 12 months of follow-up, among those without Long COVID at study entry. DESIGN: Prospective cohort study with cross-sectional and longitudinal components. SETTING: Multi-site study conducted across 83 clinical sites in the United States. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 9477 adults enrolled between October 2021 and July 2024 (median age 43 years; 74% female). MEASUREMENTS: Self-reported frequency of tobacco product, cannabis and binge alcohol use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 test infection (never, monthly or less, weekly or none). Symptomatic Long COVID was defined using the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)-Adult Long COVID Research Index, with scores ≥ 11 classified as symptomatic Long COVID and lower scores classified as indeterminate. Covariates included sociodemographic characteristics, clinical comorbidities and COVID-19 related factors. RESULTS: At study entry 20% of participants met criteria for symptomatic Long COVID. In the 12 months preceding infection, 14%, 21% and 38% reported any tobacco product, cannabis or binge alcohol use. At study entry, compared with no use, weekly or more tobacco use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.37, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.13-1.67]; weekly or more cannabis use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID (aOR = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.00-1.52); and weekly or more binge alcohol use was associated with lower odds (aOR = 0.73, 95% CI = 0.58-0.91) of symptomatic Long COVID. Monthly or less use of any substance was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at study entry. Among participants without symptomatic Long COVID at study entry, weekly or more tobacco use, compared with no use, was associated with higher odds of developing symptomatic Long COVID over 12 months of follow-up (aOR = 1.29, 95% CI = 1.03-1.62). Neither cannabis nor binge alcohol use was statistically significantly associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12-month follow-up. SUMMARY: Among adult participants of the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER) study, weekly or more tobacco use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and at 12 months among participants who did not meet criteria for symptomatic Long COVID at study entry. Weekly or more cannabis use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12 months. Weekly or more binge alcohol use was associated with lower odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12 months.

title: Socioeconomic inequalities in healthcare access during the COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan
abstract: Abstract Objective Large-scale public health crises, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, can disrupt access to essential healthcare services and exacerbate existing inequalities. This study investigates barriers to healthcare access in Kazakhstan during the COVID-19 pandemic, with a focus on socioeconomic factors associated with failed access to healthcare. Methods A cross-sectional, face-to-face survey was conducted between June and July 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic using a multistage stratified sampling approach to recruit 1,021 adults across Kazakhstan. Analyses were weighted to account for differential selection probabilities and calibrated to the national population distribution by region, urban/rural residence, sex, and age. Anticipated (hypothetical) and experienced barriers to COVID-19-related care were assessed descriptively. Failed access to healthcare was defined as the inability to obtain at least one needed healthcare service. Associations between socioeconomic factors and failed access to general healthcare services were examined using survey-weighted modified Poisson regression with a log link and robust variance estimation. Results Among the 991 respondents included in the final study sample, 753 (75.5%) reported needing at least one healthcare service during the pandemic; of these, 21.7% ( n = 164) failed to access at least one needed service. The most frequently inaccessible services included health products (e.g., eyeglasses, mobility aids, and basic medical supplies) (31.7%), emergency care (21.5%), and inpatient medical care (20.2%). Commonly reported COVID-19-related barriers included fear of infection (38.9%), fear of hospitalization and its consequences (24.7%), and concerns about income loss due to isolation (23.9%). In multivariable analysis, failed access to healthcare was significantly associated with having a chronic condition (ARR, 1.54; 95% CI, 1.14–2.07), being unemployed (ARR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.12–2.57), and experiencing food insecurity (ARR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.01–1.77). Conclusion Health system disruptions may disproportionately affect socioeconomically vulnerable populations. Strengthening social protection and ensuring continuity of essential healthcare services may help reduce inequalities in healthcare access during future public health emergencies.

title: COVID-19 vaccination, clinical presentation and 14-day outcomes in Cumilla, Bangladesh: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Community evidence from Bangladesh on how vaccination, clinical presentation and short-term outcomes intersected during the early COVID-19 vaccine rollout is limited. We assessed test positivity, clinical characteristics, vaccination status and 14-day outcomes among people tested for suspected COVID-19 in six upazilas of Cumilla district. Methods Cross-sectional study of 320 adults tested between 1 April and 31 May 2021, with a retrospective day-by-day 14-day symptom history and outcome assessment for the 86 test-positive cases. Test results (reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction [RT-PCR], n = 286; rapid antigen, n = 34) came from laboratory records; other data were collected by structured telephone interview. We estimated odds ratios, fitted a multivariable logistic regression for positivity, and described symptom trajectories and outcomes. Results Eighty-six participants tested positive (26.9%; 95% CI 22.3–32.0); cases had a mean age of 42.5 years, 54.7% were men and 90.7% were symptomatic. In the adjusted model (n = 297), symptomatic presentation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.18; 95% CI 3.64–18.41) and recent contact with a confirmed case (aOR 2.73; 1.50–4.97) were associated with positivity; age, sex, comorbidity and smoking were not. At least one vaccine dose was reported by 38.4% of cases and 51.7% of test-negative participants (aOR 0.55; 0.31–0.97), but this estimate was imprecise, attenuated in sensitivity analyses (RT-PCR-only aOR 0.75; 0.40–1.38) and does not represent vaccine effectiveness. At 14 days, 56 cases (65.1%) remained in home isolation, 15 (17.4%) were hospitalized without oxygen, 8 (9.3%) needed oxygen, 5 (5.8%) intensive care and 2 (2.3%; 95% CI 0.6–8.1) died. Conclusions Symptoms and recent exposure were the strongest correlates of a positive test, but symptoms alone had poor specificity, so testing remained essential. About one in three cases was hospitalized or died within 14 days. The observational design, mixed testing methods and recalled symptom histories preclude causal inference about vaccination.

In the adjusted model (n = 297), symptomatic presentation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.18; 95% CI 3.64–18.41) and recent contact with a confirmed case (aOR 2.73; 1.50–4.97) were associated with positivity; age, sex, comorbidity and smoking were not. At 14 days, 56 cases (65.1%) remained in home isolation, 15 (17.4%) were hospitalized without oxygen, 8 (9.3%) needed oxygen, 5 (5.8%) intensive care and 2 (2.3%; 95% CI 0.6–8.1) died. Conclusions Symptoms and recent exposure were the strongest correlates of a positive test, but symptoms alone had poor specificity, so testing remained essential. About one in three cases was hospitalized or died within 14 days. The observational design, mixed testing methods and recalled symptom histories preclude causal inference about vaccination.

title: Application of Data Science for COVID-19 Modeling in Africa: A Comparative Study of ARIMA and ANN Models, a Retrospective Time-Series Analysis.
abstract: Background and aims The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the urgent need for robust forecasting tools to guide public health responses in Africa, where data infrastructure remains limited, and epidemic dynamics differ substantially from high-income settings. Methods Daily COVID-19 surveillance data were obtained from the WHO COVID-19 Dashboard for Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa, and Tunisia. ARIMA models were fitted using the auto.arima function in R, with stationarity assessed using Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) and Kwiatkowski-Phillips-Schmidt-Shin (KPSS) tests. ANN models were implemented using the nnetar algorithm, configured with lag parameter p = 7, seasonal lag p = 1, hidden layer size of 10 nodes, and 20 repeats. Model accuracy was evaluated using root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and R-squared ( R 2 ). Results ARIMA outperformed ANN for four countries (Egypt, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria), while ANN performed better for three countries (Ghana, Tunisia, South Africa). Egypt achieved the highest forecast accuracy (MAPE = 0.09% for ARIMA). South Africa presented the greatest forecasting challenge due to high volatility and multiple distinct waves, though ANN substantially outperformed ARIMA in this setting, reducing RMSE by 56% and MAPE by 51%. Negative R 2 values for six of seven countries reflected the structural inability of backward-looking autoregressive models to anticipate variant-driven wave peaks, consistent with limitations documented in COVID-19 forecasting literature. Conclusion Neither model is universally superior; model selection should be context-dependent. ANN is recommended for settings with stable case fatality rates and complex non-linear dynamics (e.g., Ghana) and for high-volume settings with multiple distinct waves (e.g., South Africa). ARIMA is recommended for moderate-transmission settings with more linear patterns where interpretability is prioritized.

title: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
abstract: Abstract Immunocompromised individuals remain at risk of severe COVID-19. This multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity of co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 with a bivalent (Ancestral/BA.1) mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. A total of 139 immunocompromised adults received AZD7442 followed 28 days later by vaccination. AZD7442 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. Serum AZD7442 concentrations peaked at day 28 and remained detectable across disease cohorts at day 180. Anti-Spike antibody responses increased after AZD7442 and reached their highest levels after vaccination. Although binding antibodies against Omicron variants increased post-vaccination, neutralisation of Omicron remained limited after both AZD7442 and vaccination. Vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies targeting S2, the S1 N-terminal domain and receptor-binding domain epitopes not bound by AZD7442, and increased S2-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-induced T-cell responses were cross-reactive between ancestral and Omicron variants. Our findings support consideration of combined antibody and vaccine strategies in future therapeutic antibody development. The trial is registered with the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number registry (ISRCTN53507177).

title: Detection of SARS-CoV-2 in Semen Months After COVID-19: Potential Evidence of Low-Level Replicative Persistence.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Viral persistence is considered one of the key mechanisms driving long COVID symptoms. The male genital tract (MGT), particularly the testis, is an immune-privileged site that may serve as a viral reservoir for SARS-CoV-2. However, the presence of SARS-CoV-2 in semen and its long-term infectiousness remains controversial. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate the long-term presence and potential replicative activity of SARS-CoV-2 in semen, evaluating whether the virus can persist and maintain low-level culture signals in the MGT well beyond the acute phase of infection. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This observational, prospective, cross-sectional study included 38 men treated at Mater Dei Hospital, Brazil, between October 2020 and October 2021, who had recovered from mild to moderate COVID-19 and consented to participate. Semen samples were collected from mildly symptomatic participants at approximately 1 month (15- 45 days), 3 months, and 6 months after symptom onset. The moderately symptomatic group provided a single sample approximately 6 months post-infection. Semen analysis and SARS-CoV-2 detection were performed using RT-qPCR, followed by viral isolation in Vero CCL-81 cells. Potential viral persistence and replication signals were evaluated through immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). RESULTS: SARS-CoV-2 was detected by RT-qPCR in 21 of 38 patients (55%), with high cycle threshold (Ct 38-39) values observed for more than 6 months post-infection. Following inoculation into Vero cell cultures, a low-level in vitro expansion of viral copies was identified in a subset of samples from mild and moderate patients. The potential presence of the virus was further supported by the presence of viral proteins via immunofluorescence and the identification of structures morphologically compatible with coronavirus-like particles by TEM. CONCLUSION: This study provides evidence of the long-term persistence of viral RNA and culture-derived signals suggestive of restricted or low-level replicative activity in semen. These findings suggest that the MGT may serve as a viral reservoir, highlighting the importance of longitudinal semen analysis for monitoring viral persistence and reservoir dynamics after clinical recovery.

title: Novel paper-based electrochemical system for detection of anti-spike protein antibodies from SARS-CoV-2
abstract: A disposable paper-based electrochemical biosensor for detecting anti-spike protein antibodies in nasopharyngeal swab samples is presented for the first time, featuring the innovative use of carbon dots derived from a biological source and a liposome/spike protein biorecognition element complex. The optimised electrochemical sensing platform is described and characterised in terms of its structural and functional properties. The sensor showed a linear response between 0.0010 and 10 μg mL − 1 , demonstrating high sensitivity, a low limit of detection (LOD) of 1.78 pg mL − 1 , and good selectivity against anti-nucleocapsid protein antibodies. Real nasopharyngeal swab samples were tested for the first time with this paper-based electrochemical system for anti-spike antibody detection. This approach was designed to mimic the virus’s response while ensuring greater sensitivity and selectivity. Overall, a new electrochemical method for screening anti-spike antibodies was developed to monitor vulnerable populations for new SARS-CoV-2 infections and track the development of adaptive immunity within communities, contributing to the development of future point-of-care analysis without the need for specialised personnel or laboratory facilities.

The sensor showed a linear response between 0.0010 and 10 μg mL − 1 , demonstrating high sensitivity, a low limit of detection (LOD) of 1.78 pg mL − 1 , and good selectivity against anti-nucleocapsid protein antibodies. Real nasopharyngeal swab samples were tested for the first time with this paper-based electrochemical system for anti-spike antibody detection. This approach was designed to mimic the virus’s response while ensuring greater sensitivity and selectivity. Overall, a new electrochemical method for screening anti-spike antibodies was developed to monitor vulnerable populations for new SARS-CoV-2 infections and track the development of adaptive immunity within communities, contributing to the development of future point-of-care analysis without the need for specialised personnel or laboratory facilities.

title: Epidemic-phase-dependent selection within clades contributes to punctuated SARS-CoV-2 evolution.
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 evolution is characterized by punctuated lineage replacement, with successor variants often show substantial antigenic shifts. However, immune evasion alone does not ensure spread, as many immune-evasive variants are rapidly lost, underscoring the complex selective constraints shaping SARS-CoV-2 evolution that remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate the dynamics of prevalence, viral population diversity, and haplotype fitness across eight major SARS-CoV-2 clades, and their associations with functional metrics of transmissibility and immune evasion. We show that the viral fitness landscape within individual clades is modulated by epidemic phase: selection initially favors transmissibility but progressively shifts toward immune escape after the epidemic peak. This reveals an evolutionary asynchrony between viral diversification and selection: the transmission surge generates the greatest viral diversity, yet selection during this phase differs from that encountered later. As a result, immune-evasive variants favored late may be suppressed earlier, creating a mismatch that constrains continuous within-clade adaptation. Furthermore, incorporating epidemic progression into fitness prediction substantially improves predictive performance, emphasizing the importance of accounting for dynamic selection. Our findings connect macroscopic epidemiology with microscopic viral evolution, providing a conceptual framework for understanding and forecasting the evolutionary trajectories of epidemic viruses.

title: Experiences of Peer Navigators Implementing an Equity-Focused Intervention to Improve COVID-19 Testing and Vaccination Among Spanish-Speaking Latines in the U.S. South.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected Latine communities in the United States, with Spanish-speaking Latine populations having higher rates of infection, hospitalization, and mortality. Our community-based participatory research partnership developed and in 2023 implemented and evaluated Nuestra Comunidad Saludable ( Our Healthy Community ), a Spanish-language intervention designed to increase COVID-19 testing and vaccination through community-based peer navigation and mHealth. After follow-up data collection, individual in-depth interviews were conducted in Spanish in 2024 with 10 community-based peer navigators, known as Navegantes , to understand their experiences implementing the intervention. Themes were identified through constant comparison. All Navegantes were native Spanish speakers, with a mean age of 45.7 ( SD = 12.6, range: 21-66), and immigrated from seven Latin American countries. Fifteen themes emerged within four domains: (1) Navegante Engagement (e.g., Navegantes were highly committed to the intervention); (2) Training and Support (e.g., Activity Logs offered Navegantes "cues to action" and structure for tracking and reporting intervention activities); (3) Implementation Experiences (e.g., Navegante s were able to tailor and personalize COVID-19 messaging to meet the unique needs of each member of their social networks); and (4) Future Directions (e.g., an intervention like Nuestra Comunidad Saludable could be implemented to address other health issues within Latine communities). Interviews identified important learnings about Navegantes ' experiences implementing the Nuestra Comunidad Saludable intervention. They also revealed valuable insights into the COVID-19 pandemic, barriers to accessing resources, and Latine community health needs and priorities that warrant future exploration and intervention.

title: Conectividad digital, movilidad del hogar y riesgos alimentarios durante el confinamiento por COVID-19 en México Digital connectivity, household mobility and food risks during the COVID-19 lockdown in Mexico
abstract: This article studies the impact of internet access and private transportation on food access and consumption quality during the COVID-19 lockdown in Mexico. We use data from the 2020 National Health and Nutrition Survey and the Latin American and Caribbean Food Security Scale to estimate ordinal probit models and treatment effect estimators. We analyze how digital connectivity and household mobility influence the likelihood of experiencing food insecurity and reducing healthy food consumption. The findings reveal that digital networks are associated with a lower probability of facing food insecurity, while private transportation shows favorable, but territorially heterogeneous, associations. Households with minors are also shown to be a particularly vulnerable group in this analysis. Evidence is provided on the complementary role of connectivity and mobility in mitigating food risks in contexts of exogenous economic shocks, highlighting that their relevance depends on territorial conditions and supply opportunities.

title: Beyond the Lungs: Unveiling the Long-term Hepatobiliary Complications of COVID-19
abstract: Although primarily known for its respiratory involvement, SARS-CoV-2 infection has increasingly been associated with significant effects on multiple organ systems, including the hepatobiliary tract. Over the course of the pandemic, it was shown that COVID-19 can trigger a variety of liver and cholangiocyte impairments through many overlapping mechanisms. These include entry of the virus into liver cells that express angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptors, impaired immune responses, ischemic injury, and adverse reactions to therapeutic drugs. These may lead to persistent hepatic enzyme abnormalities, biliary stasis, secondary sclerosing cholangitis, or fibrosis. Individuals who have underlying liver disease, such as liver cirrhosis or non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), are especially susceptible to serious complications and unfavorable outcomes. Uncommon immune-mediated conditions, such as post-COVID-19 vaccination autoimmune-like hepatitis, have been reported. Therefore, ongoing assessment of liver function and careful long-term follow-up are recommended for patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome, especially those at high risk. This review discusses current evidence to provide an overview of the mechanisms, manifestations, and long-term consequences of COVID-19 involving the hepatobiliary tract.
journal: Journal of Pure and Applied Microbiology

title: Visual-verbal scanning and attention performance in individuals with long COVID-19-related dysautonomia
abstract: Long COVID-19-related dysautonomia is associated with persistent cognitive and visual complaints, but brief clinically feasible tools for characterizing visual-attentional performance are needed. In this case-control study, 48 individuals with long COVID-19-related dysautonomia and 30 healthy controls completed the Modified Adult Developmental Eye Movement Test (ADEM-d), a timed visual-verbal reading/scanning task that requires sequential saccadic deployment, and the Continuous Visual Attention Test (CVAT). Compared with controls, the study group showed longer adjusted horizontal (median 73.63 vs. 54.69 s), vertical (66.35 vs. 50.66 s), and distractor (83.97 vs. 64.55 s) reading times (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001; rank-biserial r = 0.58–0.60), whereas the horizontal/vertical ratio did not differ significantly ( p = 0.108). On the CVAT, the study group showed longer reaction time (378.5 vs. 320.0 ms; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), greater reaction-time variability (96.0 vs. 62.5 ms; p = 0.001), and more omission errors ( p = 0.028). Across the full sample, distractor-condition ADEM-d time was positively associated with omission errors, reaction time, and reaction-time variability (Spearman rho = 0.55–0.58; all p < 0.001). These findings indicate altered functional visual-verbal scanning and visual-attentional performance in this cohort. Because the ADEM-d does not directly record eye movements, the results do not demonstrate a primary saccadic motor deficit; additionally, the absence of a long-COVID group without dysautonomia prevents attribution of the findings specifically to dysautonomia. The ADEM-d and CVAT may nevertheless provide brief screening information to identify individuals who require more detailed visual, oculomotor, or neuropsychological assessment.

title: Opioid agonist therapy in and beyond the COVID-19 pandemic: A descriptive policy analysis across Canadian jurisdictions
abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted widespread rapid changes to opioid agonist therapy (OAT) policy in Canada, reshaping how care was delivered to people with opioid use disorder. To better understand how OAT policy changes varied across jurisdictions, we conducted a comparative policy analysis identifying federal, provincial, and territorial OAT policy changes that occurred during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: Policy documents (n = 88) were sourced from grey literature, targeted website searches, and recommendations from relevant knowledge experts conducted between June-July 2024 and May-July 2025. A combined content and thematic analysis approach was employed to organize identified policy changes (n = 300) into eight policy areas: expanded prescribing permissions, take-home dosing, witnessed dosing, medication delivery, urine drug screening, virtual care, slow-release oral morphine, and injectable OAT. RESULTS: Across jurisdictions, policies governing OAT evolved considerably during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, though the scope and durability of these changes varied significantly. Federal exemptions enabled policy changes, specifically in expanding prescribing authorities and medication delivery. These authorities were translated differently across regions spanning narrow renewal-focused roles to broader clinical discretion. Policies addressing take-home dosing and monitoring requirements showed the greatest divergence, with provinces such as Ontario and Nova Scotia adopting more permissive approaches, while Saskatchewan and Manitoba maintained more restrictive, structured approaches. CONCLUSIONS: Pandemic circumstances supported the implementation of OAT policy changes that increased flexibility and permissiveness of OAT delivery. However, uneven implementation risks the perpetuation of geographic and equity-based disparities, emphasizing the need for coordinated and equity-focused OAT policy.

title: Nasal mucosal humoral responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination priming schedules in the UK: a substudy of the Com-COV single-blind, randomised, non-inferiority trial.
abstract: Background Mucosal surfaces form the first line of defence against respiratory pathogens. Most licensed COVID-19 vaccines are delivered intramuscularly and elicit strong systemic immunity. Whether such vaccines generate locally derived nasal mucosal responses remains uncertain. In this substudy, we aimed to investigate mucosal and systemic antibody responses following different intramuscular SARS-CoV-2 priming vaccination schedules. Methods In the Com-COV single-blind, randomised, non-inferiority trial, adults aged 50 years or older who were COVID-19 unvaccinated and SARS-CoV-2 infection-naive were enrolled across eight sites in the UK between Feb 11, 2021, and Feb 26, 2021. Participants were randomised to receive homologous or heterologous vaccination schedules using ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 (ChAd) and BNT162b2 (BNT), administered at either a 28-day or 84-day interval. This substudy collected nasal lining fluid using nasosorption strips in long-interval cohorts. Anti-spike and anti-nucleocapsid IgG and IgA were quantified in serum and nasal samples by electrochemiluminescence immunoassay. Correlations were assessed using Pearson's coefficients. Findings Mucosal lining fluid samples were collected from 101 participants (mean age 59·1 years [SD 5·0]; 49 [49%] women; 33 [33%] non-White ethnicities). Significant increases in mucosal anti-spike IgA from baseline were seen for ChAd-BNT (geometric mean concentration was 612·8 AU/mL [95% CI 363·6-1032·7]) and BNT-BNT (906·4 AU/mL [619·36-1325·8]). This corresponded to fold rises of 2·78 (1·39-5·54) for ChAd-BNT and 3·11 (1·76-5·50) for BNT-BNT. Mucosal anti-spike IgA trajectories did not mirror vaccination-induced systemic markers, including serum anti-spike IgG (r=0·13, 0·03-0·23, p=0·013). Instead, mucosal anti-spike IgA trajectories correlated with mucosal anti-nucleocapsid IgA (r=0·78, 0·74-0·82, p=5 × 10 -77 ), consistent with mucosal SARS-CoV-2 exposure. Across all schedules, no evidence existed of de novo nasal IgA induction following one or two intramuscular doses, irrespective of baseline serostatus. Observed increases in nasal anti-spike IgA were more consistent with intercurrent mucosal SARS-CoV-2 exposure than direct vaccine effect. Nasal IgG appeared to reflect systemic vaccine responses, whereas SARS-CoV-2 exposure was associated with additional changes in mucosal IgG. Interpretation Intramuscular immunisation induces robust systemic immunity and remains central to emergency and routine vaccination schedules. However, intramuscular immunisation does not appear to generate de novo local nasal IgA, levels of which have been associated with protection beyond that conferred by serum IgG. Interpretation of vaccine-induced mucosal responses could be confounded by asymptomatic community exposure. Mucosally delivered vaccines are a biologically plausible complementary strategy to enhance protection and reduce transmission, and thus, need further investigation. Funding National Institute for Health Research, the UK Vaccine Taskforce, John Fell Fund, University of Oxford, and Oxfordshire Health Services Research Committee.

title: Viral genome surveillance via modifiable microarray sequencing and a supervised stack ensemble neural network model: SARS-CoV-2 as a case study
abstract: Introduction Continued SARS-CoV-2 evolution underscores the need for scalable genomic surveillance methods that are faster and less resource-intensive than conventional sequencing alone. This study evaluated a viral genome surveillance strategy that combines modifiable microarray-based resequencing with supervised ensemble machine learning to improve base-calling accuracy. Methods Building on a previously reported full-genome tiling microarray platform, we extracted expanded image-derived features from resequencing arrays. Features included probe intensity means and standard deviations across sense and antisense strands and multiple exposure times, yielding 48 input features per genomic position. Using 35 clinical SARS-CoV-2 samples, we created training, validation, and held-out test datasets and trained more than 12,000 neural network models under multiple preprocessing and hyperparameter configurations. Top-performing base models were combined using stacked ensemble learning with logistic regression and neural network meta-models. Results In held-out testing on clinical samples with cycle threshold ≤24, the stacked ensemble models achieved high per-position base-calling accuracy (>99%). Because accuracy was computed across thousands of correlated genomic positions per specimen, these values should be interpreted as per-position performance rather than as an estimate of performance across independent clinical specimens. Discussion In this proof-of-concept evaluation using a limited set of archived clinical SARS-CoV-2 samples, microarray sequencing coupled with stacked ensemble learning produced high per-position base-calling accuracy in high-viral-load specimens and enabled recovery of many Illumina-confirmed variants. The approach may be adaptable to other viral targets through microarray redesign and model retraining. However, broader validation across larger, more genetically diverse and contemporary sample sets—including more mutation-rich lineages and lower viral load specimens—will be needed to establish robustness beyond this early-isolate, Ct-qualified evaluation.

title: COVID-19 Is Not an Independent Risk Factor for Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: BackgroundPost-intensive care syndrome (PICS) affects many ICU survivors, leading to persistent physical, cognitive, and mental health issues. The COVID-19 pandemic raised concerns about whether SARS-CoV-2 infection increases PICS risk. This study aimed to evaluate whether COVID-19 is an independent risk factor for PICS and to identify other contributing factors.MethodsThis retrospective cohort included 92 patients treated for respiratory failure in three ICUs at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin between July 2020 and September 2021. Patients were divided into COVID-19 (n = 49) and non-COVID-19 (n = 43) groups. At three months post-discharge, outpatient assessments consisted of demographic data, ICU-related variables, and evaluations of physical (handgrip dynamometry, Timed Up and Go test), cognitive (Mini-Cog, Animal Naming Test), and psychological health (PHQ-4). PICS was defined as at least one abnormal test; severity was graded by the number of affected domains. Logistic and ordinal regression analyses assessed whether COVID-19 was independently associated with PICS prevalence and severity.ResultsPICS was present in 71.4% of COVID-19 and 62.8% of non-COVID survivors (p = 0.378). Multivariable analysis showed no significant association between COVID-19 and PICS or its severity (OR = 1.46; 95% CI 0.50-4.23; p = 0.486; and OR = 1.09; 95% CI 0.45-2.68; p = 0.845, respectively).ConclusionsCOVID-19 was not independently associated with PICS in ICU survivors. Both groups experience high rates of long-term impairments, highlighting the importance of rehabilitation and follow-up care for all ICU survivors.

title: Towards normalization of cognitive function and psychiatric morbidity in patients with neurological symptoms post COVID-19: a longitudinal study
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Few studies of cognitive impairment in COVID-19 convalescents have assessed patients longitudinally. The aim of this study was to examine the course of performance-based cognitive functions from 6 (T1) to 12 (T2) months after COVID-19 in patients compared with healthy controls, and to investigate the effect of psychiatric diagnosis and fatigue on cognitive function trajectories. METHODS: Eighty-one patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection reporting neurological symptoms were assessed at T1 and 67 patients at T2 with neuropsychological assessment and a semi-structured psychiatric interview. Fatigue was assessed using the Giessener Beschwerdebogen questionnaire (GBB). Sixty-one, confirmed SARS-CoV-2 antibody negative, healthy controls underwent neuropsychological assessment and completed GBB. RESULTS: At T1, patients performed significantly (p < 0.001 to 0.031) worse across the different cognitive domains, except for verbal fluency, than healthy controls. title: Randomised trial of hyperimmune immunoglobulin in hospitalised COVID-19: pre-therapy Fc receptor binding SARS-CoV-2 antibody associated with better outcomes.
abstract: Neutralising monoclonal antibodies prevent and treat COVID-19 if administered early after infection with sensitive SARS-CoV-2 variants. Despite containing high neutralising antibodies, hyperimmune intravenous immunoglobulin (hIVIG) generally fails to mitigate severe COVID-19. We probed potential reasons for this discrepancy in a recent large, randomised trial (NCT04546581). Multiplex bead arrays were used to measure SARS-CoV-2 specific FcγR binding and neutralising activity in pre-treatment sera from 481 subjects (231 placebo vs. Associations between pre-therapy antibody FcγR engagement and day 7 clinical outcome were evaluated. Elevated levels of FcγRIIIa engagement by baseline spike (S)-specific antibody were associated with better clinical outcomes in COVID-19 hospitalised patients across both hIVIG- and placebo-treated groups (OR=0.43, 95%CI 0.30-0.63). Higher nucleocapsid (N) antibody-mediated FcγR engagement and surrogate neutralisation in pre-treatment sera were also modestly associated with improved outcomes. Higher pre-therapy S-specific FcγR binding antibody was also associated with reduced SARS-CoV-2 viral loads. Higher pre-therapy S-specific FcγR binding antibody, but not additional FcγR binding antibody provided by hIVIG, was associated with improved outcomes in severe COVID-19. Pre-existing FcγR engaging antibody, along with rapid production of these antibodies in placebo-treated subjects, may dilute potential benefits from hIVIG therapy. This work helps guide development of more strategic, targeted treatment of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection with antibody-based therapeutics.

title: Beyond Vulnerability: Autonomy, Social Participation, and the Experiences of Older Adults During the COVID-19 Lockdown
abstract: Abstract Background During the COVID-19 pandemic, people aged 75 years and over in Spain experienced substantial excess mortality and were disproportionately affected by restrictive measures intended to protect them from infection. These measures limited mobility and access to essential services and had important consequences for social relationships, autonomy, and well-being. This study aimed to explore the experiences of people aged 75 years and over and their family caregivers during the COVID-19 lockdown in Spain, focusing on the political, social, and personal impacts of pandemic measures and strategies to address emerging challenges. Methods A qualitative study informed by a critical social perspective was conducted between March and October 2023. Participants included 37 people aged 75 years and over and 70 family caregivers from diverse urban and rural settings across 11 Spanish provinces. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and discussion groups exploring experiences of the lockdown, perceptions of pandemic policies, and individual and family coping strategies. Data were analysed using a multilayered discourse analysis. Results Although protective measures were intended to safeguard older adults, participants described how age-based restrictions could reinforce stereotypes of frailty and dependency, contributing to stigmatization and social isolation. Restrictions also disrupted family and social routines and affected emotional well-being and social connection. At the same time, participants described diverse strategies to cope with these challenges, including physical activity, the use of technology, and engagement in meaningful daily routines. These strategies supported autonomy, social connection, and resilience, although their feasibility varied across individuals and circumstances. Conclusions Pandemic responses targeting older adults may have unintended consequences when protection is prioritized over autonomy and social participation. Recognizing older adults as active agents and incorporating their perspectives into emergency planning may contribute to more inclusive responses that protect health while preserving autonomy, dignity, and social connectedness.

title: Disparities in long COVID diagnosis among a care-seeking population in the Midwestern United States: An approach to identifying underdiagnosis.
abstract: Objective To identify predictors of Long COVID diagnosis among patients seeking care for Long COVID symptoms to document potential underdiagnosis and diagnostic disparities. Methods In this retrospective study using electronic health records from a midwestern healthcare system, we identified adults with SARS-CoV-2 between July 1, 2021 and October 31, 2022 (index date) and 1+ follow-up visits with a Long COVID-associated symptom 90 to 365 days after index (follow-up period). Using modified Poisson regression, we examined the probability of Long COVID diagnosis by age, sex, race/ethnicity, language preference, insurance, COVID-19 vaccination status, and hospitalization at index. Results Within our analytic sample (n = 34,585), 1.9% of patients were diagnosed with Long COVID. Patients who were ≥ 30 years (versus 18-29), hospitalized at index (versus not), or had 8+ healthcare encounters during follow up (versus one) had a higher probability of Long COVID diagnosis. Conversely, patients with non-English language preference (versus English) had a lower probability of diagnosis (aPR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.24, 0.81), as did patients with Medicare (aPR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.39, 0.67) or Medicaid (aPR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.56, 0.89) versus private insurance. Conclusions Results suggest Long COVID underdiagnosis for patients who experience barriers to care, including patients with a language barrier or public insurance.

title: Understanding the Support Needs of People With Long COVID: A Qualitative Study in Aotearoa New Zealand.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long COVID is a multi-system condition that affects an increasing number of individuals. Little is known about the support needs of people living with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences and healthcare access challenges of people with long COVID to better inform service design. METHODS: Co-design methodology was used, informed by the Stanford Design Thinking process and knowledge mobilisation approaches. Participants were recruited via snowballing, through professional networks and support groups. People with lived experience of long COVID were invited to participate in a 2-h workshop, facilitated by researchers, conducted between March and September 2024. Participants were asked to create a depiction of their experience of long COVID and describe their creation to the group; descriptions were audio-recorded, transcribed and thematically analysed. The inclusion of people with lived experience of long COVID as co-investigators ensured that the study was designed and conducted to forefront their knowledge and experience. RESULTS: Eight workshops were conducted, including 30 participants, between March and August 2024. Of these, 25 (83%) were female; of the 25 who provided their age, most were aged 45 to 64 years (n = 18, 72%), four (16%) were aged 25 to 44 years and three (12%) aged 65 years or older. Five key themes emerged: (i) lack of assistance; (ii) systemic barriers; (iii) absence of long COVID clinics; (iv) financial strain; and (v) low quality of care. A sixth theme identified personal coping strategies. CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand face major barriers to care, including inadequate services, financial hardship, and fragmented healthcare pathways. Findings support improved pathways and primary health care education in long COVID. A person-centred, coordinated, and accessible model of care is needed. LIVED EXPERIENCE OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was designed with two people with lived experience of long COVID included as co-investigators, and a further one on the Advisory Board. All participants had lived experience of long COVID.

title: Temporal Changes in Body Mass Index among Patients with Severe COVID-19 in Japan.
abstract: To characterize temporal changes in body mass index (BMI) among patients with severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) admitted to intensive care units in Japan. We conducted a retrospective observational study using the Japanese Intensive care PAtient Database. We included 8,159 patients with confirmed COVID-19 admitted to 95 intensive care units during fiscal years 2020-2023. BMI distributions were compared across fiscal years and 10 epidemic waves. Sensitivity analyses restricted the cohort to patients with viral pneumonia, patients requiring advanced respiratory support, and patients without major comorbidities. BMI was highest in 2020-2021 and declined markedly from 2022 onward. The distribution showed a distinct downward shift between the fifth and sixth epidemic waves and remained lower thereafter. This pattern persisted across sensitivity analyses despite higher severity scores in 2022 and less frequent invasive respiratory support and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. The phenotype of patients reaching critical illness changed during the pandemic. Risk factors derived from early-pandemic cohorts should therefore be interpreted dynamically as viral variants, population immunity, and clinical context evolve.

title: Age-related differences in long COVID symptoms and outcomes: a cross-sectional study in Jordan.
abstract: Background Long coronavirus disease (COVID) causes persistent physical, psychological, and functional symptoms. This study compared symptom prevalence and outcomes between younger (<60 years) and older (≥60 years) Jordanian adults with long COVID. Methods This cross-sectional study included adults with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and symptoms persisting ≥2 months. An Arabic questionnaire was administered online or by telephone. Fatigue, functional status, dyspnea, and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Fatigue Severity Scale, Post-COVID-19 Functional Status (PCFS) scale, modified Medical Research Council scale, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Group comparisons and multivariable logistic regression were performed, adjusting for sex, smoking, comorbidity, and vaccination. Results Among 938 participants, 596 (63.5%) were younger than 60 years. Fatigue was common in both groups (93.3% vs. Younger adults reported more dyspnea, muscle pain, dizziness, anxiety/depression, and brain fog (all P<0.05). Older adults had more severe functional limitation (PCFS grade 4: 24.6% vs. 16.1%; P=0.002) and greater depressive symptom severity (P=0.029). After adjustment, younger age was associated with lower odds of moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.624; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.468-0.830; P=0.001), but not with severe functional limitation (aOR, 1.340; 95% CI, 0.949-1.891; P=0.096). Conclusion Younger adults reported a broader range of symptoms, whereas older adults experienced greater functional impairment and depressive symptom severity. Age remained independently associated with depressive symptoms but not severe functional limitation.

title: Epistasis detection and fitness valleys in SARS-CoV-2 evolution
abstract: Probabilistic prognosis of virus evolution, vital for the design of effective vaccines and antiviral drugs, requires the knowledge of adaptive landscape including epistatic interactions. Although epistatic interactions can, in principle, be inferred from abundant sequencing data by various methods, it has been shown previously that genetic linkage between evolving sites obscures their signature and requires averaging over several independent populations. Here we probe the limits of epistasis detection based on pairwise correlations conditioned on the state of a third site on synthetic sequences evolved in a Monte Carlo algorithm with known epistatic pairs in two scenarios: an initially-diverse population in the presence of recombination and mutation, with a uniform epistatic network, and an initially–uniform population in the presence of mutation and a fitness valley. In either scenario, the detection error decreases with the number of independent populations and increases with the sequence length. In the first scenario, the accuracy is enhanced by moderate recombination and is maximal, when epistasis magnitude approaches the point of full compensation. In the second scenario, simulation predicts the spontaneous crossing of a fitness valley and forming a new large strain. The method is then applied to several thousands of sequences of SARS-CoV-2. Results obtained under equal sampling from world regions are consistent with the existence of fitness valleys connecting groups of viral variants.

title: Radical Changes in Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacterales in Poland During the COVID-19 Pandemic and War in Ukraine
abstract: INTRODUCTION: A marked increase in carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) occurred in Poland during COVID-19 and full-scale war in Ukraine. This study aimed to descriptively analyze the characteristics of the growing number of CPE in the country. METHODS: In 2019-2024, 10,339 unique CPE isolates were collected. First, this study included an analysis of isolate and patient data. Then, 1130 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from July to September 2019, 2021 and 2024 were screened by PCR for hypervirulence (hvKp) genes. All PCR-positive isolates plus representative negatives (n = 639) were sequenced and analysed with bioinformatic tools. RESULTS: CPE increased biphasically, with ~ 153% growth in 2019-2021 and ~ 36% in 2022-2024. During COVID-19, the increase retained the clonality and carbapenemase content of K. pneumoniae, with the predominant (> 70%) NDM-1-producing ST11 genotype, present since 2012/2013. Otherwise, in 2022-2024, the ST11 decreased to ~15%, owing to multiple clones/genotypes, including ST147, ST307 and ST395. Around 30% of the 2024 isolates carried hvKp genes. In 2022, multiple new genotypes were identified originally in Poland, Germany or elsewhere from Ukrainian patients. CONCLUSIONS: The study provided a recent view of CPE epidemiology in Poland and also highlighted the risk of further expansion of dangerous organisms from Eastern Europe.
