title: Investigating the impact of the Covid-19 epidemic on mortality and fertility indicators in Qom province and comparing it with national indicators from 2019 to 2023
abstract: Objective (s): Communicable and non-communicable diseases are always associated with many impacts on fertility rates, mortality, and disease burden. The present study aimed to investigate the impact of COVID-19 on fertility and mortality indicators. Methods: The present study was a mixed-method study that was conducted in two phases: a descriptive cross-sectional study and a review study. In the descriptive phase, statistical data were reviewed during 3 time periods before the COVID epidemic (March 2017 to March 2020), during the epidemic (March 2020 to March 2021), and after the epidemic (March 2021 to March 2023) for 24 months. In the second phase, a review study was conducted on the impact of the COVID-19 epidemic on mortality and fertility indicators, as well as maternal-fetal outcomes in Iran over the past years, which was searched through the electronic databases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Persian Database (SID) for articles up to 2023. The source of the study of outcomes and complications related to the mother and newborn was obtained through a review study. Data analysis was performed using descriptive statistics in SPSS software and expressed using numbers, percentages, and graphs. Results: The general fertility rate in the pre-epidemic period was estimated at about 3.5%, which decreased to 1.3% during and after the epidemic . The stillbirth rate in the pre-epidemic period was reported to be approximately 4.6%, which decreased to 3.8% in the post-epidemic period. The crude birth rate in the pre-epidemic and post-epidemic periods was also 1.4% and 1.05%, respectively. In terms of maternal outcomes during and after the COVID-19 epidemic , most pregnant mothers faced the risk of cesarean section, premature birth, and prolonged hospital stay. In terms of neonatal outcomes, fetal heart rate abnormalities, hospitalization in the neonatal intensive care unit, and the need for resuscitation in the first minute were the most reported outcomes. Vaccination coverage decreased during and after the epidemic . Conclusion: The study findings showed that fertility and crude birth rates have decreased during and after the epidemic . Also, during the Covid-19 period, maternal and fetal complications such as respiratory complications, preterm labor, premature rupture of membranes, preeclampsia, coagulation disorders, and cardiopulmonary disorders of pregnant mothers and newborns increased. Therefore, awareness raising to prevent any type of infection during pregnancy that can affect the occurrence of pathological consequences in the mother and newborn, as well as improving and continuing prenatal care, seems necessary.

title: Who should bear the cost of COVID-19 non-vaccination? An equity analysis using a luck egalitarian framework in a South African insured population
abstract: Abstract Background Personal choice in health behaviours raises difficult questions of equity: when individuals freely decline effective health interventions, who should bear the resulting costs? This question sits at the heart of debates about personal responsibility in health financing, yet it has rarely been examined empirically. Luck egalitarianism offers a framework for assessing these questions: inequalities arising from brute luck (circumstance) should be compensated, while those from option luck (genuine choice) may legitimately be borne by individuals. Applying this framework requires distinguishing empirically between non-vaccination due to choice and non-vaccination due to constrained circumstance — a distinction that has rarely been operationalised in real-world health financing contexts. COVID-19 vaccination in South Africa's privately insured population, where vaccines were freely available and access barriers minimal, offers a favourable setting for such an inquiry. Methods Using de-identified claims data for approximately 550,000 members of two South African medical schemes (March 2020–December 2022), we estimated each individual's predicted probability of vaccination based on demographic and clinical characteristics using logistic regression. We compared observed and predicted uptake across probability strata to infer whether non-vaccination reflected personal choice or constrained circumstance. We then modelled excess costs attributable to non-vaccination using a zero-inflated negative binomial model, comparing observed expenditure with a counterfactual in which all members were vaccinated. Excess costs were calculated across predicted probability strata. Results Predicted and observed vaccination rates aligned closely, suggesting that residual non-vaccination in higher-probability groups reflected personal choice rather than constrained circumstance. source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Personal choice in health behaviours raises difficult questions of equity: when individuals freely decline effective health interventions, who should bear the resulting costs? This question sits at the heart of debates about personal responsibility in health financing, yet it has rarely been examined empirically. Luck egalitarianism offers a framework for assessing these questions: inequalities arising from brute luck (circumstance) should be compensated, while those from option luck (genuine choice) may legitimately be borne by individuals. Applying this framework requires distinguishing empirically between non-vaccination due to choice and non-vaccination due to constrained circumstance — a distinction that has rarely been operationalised in real-world health financing contexts. COVID-19 vaccination in South Africa's privately insured population, where vaccines were freely available and access barriers minimal, offers a favourable setting for such an inquiry. Methods Using de-identified claims data for approximately 550,000 members of two South African medical schemes (March 2020–December 2022), we estimated each individual's predicted probability of vaccination based on demographic and clinical characteristics using logistic regression. We compared observed and predicted uptake across probability strata to infer whether non-vaccination reflected personal choice or constrained circumstance. We then modelled excess costs attributable to non-vaccination using a zero-inflated negative binomial model, comparing observed expenditure with a counterfactual in which all members were vaccinated. Excess costs were calculated across predicted probability strata. Results Predicted and observed vaccination rates aligned closely, suggesting that residual non-vaccination in higher-probability groups reflected personal choice rather than constrained circumstance. Observed costs exceeded predicted costs by an average of 22% under a universal vaccination scenario, with the excess concentrated among older adults and those with comorbidities. Among younger, low-risk members, predicted costs slightly exceeded observed expenditure, as the fixed cost of vaccination was not offset by avoided hospitalisation. Conclusions The study empirically distinguished choice-based from circumstance-based non-vaccination and quantified the financial consequences of that distinction in the pseudo-laboratory setting of the study. This offers an empirical basis for assessing the equity of responsibility-based financing arrangements, and for deliberating when personal responsibility should inform health financing design.

title: SARS-CoV-2 infection as a potential trigger of aplastic anemia in the context of clonal hematopoiesis
abstract: Background Aplastic anemia (AA) is a rare, immune-mediated bone marrow failure syndrome in which viral infections are recognized as established triggers; however, the role of SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination in its pathogenesis is not well understood. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, we assessed temporal trends in all patients diagnosed with AA between 2009 and 2025 and analyzed patients diagnosed between 2020 and 2023 in detail. Clinical characteristics, SARS-CoV-2 antibody profiles, serological autoimmune parameters, and cytokine signatures were assessed and compared according to infection and vaccination status. Stored serum samples from the routine diagnostic work-up, collected around diagnosis and before immunosuppressive treatment, were available for all patients diagnosed between 2020 and 2023. Results Of 65 patients, 36 were diagnosed before (2009–2019) and 29 during or after the pandemic (2020–2025). There was a non-significant increase in the annual numbers from 2020 onwards (median 4.5 vs. 3; p = 0.06) and a significantly higher median age at AA diagnosis (64 vs. 43 years; p = 0.01). Of the 18 patients from the early pandemic years (2020–2023), only two reported prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, but 67% exhibited anti-nucleocapsid antibodies, suggesting a high prevalence of unrecognized infections. Antibody kinetics indicated that most infections occurred close to AA onset. Serological autoimmune parameters were infrequent and not associated with infection or vaccination status. Irrespective of infection/vaccination status, cytokine profiling revealed a consistent inflammatory signature with markedly elevated TNFβ and IL-13. Three patients with serological evidence of infection showed pronounced activation of IL-1α, IL-6, and IL-10, marked lymphocytic bone marrow infiltration, and mutations associated with clonal hematopoiesis ( ASXL1 , DNMT3A , TET2 ). One of these patients relapsed after a SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. Conclusions In this single-center case series, most patients with AA diagnosed during the pandemic had serological evidence of a previous, often unrecognized SARS-CoV-2 infection, which in most cases occurred close to disease onset. Although this temporal association does not establish causality, it is compatible with SARS-CoV-2 acting as a trigger of AA in susceptible individuals. Vaccination was not associated with autoimmune phenomena. Whether clonal hematopoiesis contributes to disease susceptibility should be investigated in larger, multicenter cohorts.

title: COVID-19 and Active Tuberculosis Exhibit Distinct Maturation-Associated Neutrophil Transcriptional Programs
abstract: Neutrophils can promote pathogen control or drive tissue-damaging inflammation, but the mechanisms that determine these divergent outcomes remain poorly defined. COVID-19 and active tuberculosis (TB) offer a purposeful comparison since both are pulmonary infections with substantial neutrophil involvement, yet differ in pathogen class, inflammatory duration, and the balance between neutrophil-associated host defense and pathology. We therefore tested whether their divergent neutrophil programs align with distinct maturation-associated transcriptional states. We integrated six publicly available whole-blood bulk RNA-sequencing datasets, comprising three COVID-19 and three active TB cohorts. A curated panel of 770 genes covered activation, degranulation, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, chemotaxis, cell surface receptors, and maturation. Study-associated variation was reduced using ComBat-Seq, and differential expression relative to disease-appropriate controls was assessed with DESeq2. Most genes changed in the same direction in both diseases, but 348 (45.2%) differed significantly in response magnitude, with 159 genes showing a stronger response in COVID-19 and 189 in TB. COVID-19 samples showed reduced expression of the maturation markers CD10 (MME) and CD16 (FCGR3A), alongside elevated expression of granule-cargo and NET-associated genes, including MPO and ELANE, consistent with a greater contribution from immature, emergency granulopoiesis-derived neutrophil populations. In contrast, TB samples showed higher maturation-associated, receptor, oxidative, and recruitment responses, consistent with a relatively mature receptor-competent neutrophil transcriptional signature. Independent COVID-19 Ward and pulmonary TB cohorts showed directional agreement for maturation and NET-associated signatures (100% and 90% concordance, respectively), while chemotaxis and select receptor and degranulation genes showed weaker reproducibility indicating that maturation represents the most consistently reproduced axis of distinction between the two diseases. Together, these findings identify maturation-associated transcription as the most consistently reproduced axis distinguishing COVID-19 from TB. These signatures provide candidate biomarkers for future studies linking neutrophil states to clinical outcomes and informing host-directed therapeutic strategies that preserve antimicrobial function while limiting immunopathology.

title: Phylodynamic analysis of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic in the Gambia: a 2-year genomic surveillance investigation
abstract: Abstract The dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 viral spread are well documented in high income countries. However, limited sequence data in low-and middle-income countries have hampered our understanding of the virus’s spatiotemporal circulation within Sub-Saharan Africa. We used Bayesian phylogeographic inference to reconstruct the origin and migration pattern of SARS-CoV-2 sequenced in The Gambia during the pandemic. Our findings suggest high and continuous rates of viral imports, with at least 94 independent introductions between March 2020 and January 2022. Viral import was mostly associated with countries in Southern Europe, Western Africa, and Southern Asia. Gambia transmission clusters initiated prior to lockdown persisted longer during the pandemic, while clusters that emerged around the introduction of COVID-19 vaccines in The Gambia had shorter persistent times. The higher number of inferred introduction events suggests that international and regional travel continued to contribute substantially to viral movement into The Gambia despite the implementation of border control measures. Thus, a well-defined protocol at entry points, coupled with a well-structured genomic surveillance system, is essential for monitoring lineages and enabling early detection and control.

title: Cognitive Failures, Private Self-Awareness and Quality of Life in Post-COVID-19 Adults
abstract: Abstract This study aimed to describe the perceived levels of cognitive failures, private self-awareness, and quality of life in post-COVID-19 Brazilian adults; investigate the sociodemographic and clinical predictors of these cognitive and psychological outcomes in the post-COVID-19 group; as well as compare these variables between post-COVID-19 adults and controls. A cross-sectional study with an online survey ( N = 391) was conducted. Cognitive Failures Questionnaire, Self-Reflection and Insight Scale and World Health Organization Quality of Life assessment were used to access cognitive and psychological dimensions. Shapiro-Wilk test was conducted to verify data distribution. One-way ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis examined associations. Multiple linear regression tested association between sociodemographic and clinical variables with cognitive failures, self-reflection, insight and quality of life. Independent t-test and Mann-Whitney U test compared groups. Most participants reported perceived worsening in memory, followed by attention, quality of life, self-reflection, and insight. Gender, psychiatric conditions and quantity of symptoms were significantly associated with higher levels of cognitive complaints in COVID-19 survivors. Post-COVID-19 adults presented significantly higher perceived levels of cognitive failures compared to control group, especially non-binary individuals and women. The present study suggests that specific sociodemographic and clinical factors are linked to the perceived cognitive and psychological long-term negative effects post-COVID-19. Interventions should develop an inclusive approach that considers the specific needs of gender-diverse populations, individuals with pre-existing psychiatric conditions, those with lower income, and individuals with greater number of symptoms, since these factors were significantly associated with one or more adverse cognitive and psychological outcomes.

title: Institutional trust, access inequities and social accountability during COVID-19 vaccination in federalised Nepal: a multi-site qualitative study.
abstract: Introduction Nepal's transition to a three-tier federal system devolved substantial responsibility for health-service delivery to subnational governments, while the COVID-19 pandemic created an early test of intergovernmental coordination, service accessibility and public trust. We examined how institutional trust, access to vaccination and citizen engagement interacted during Nepal's COVID-19 vaccine rollout across contrasting local contexts. Methods We conducted a multi-site qualitative case study in three purposively selected municipalities in Bara, Dailekh and Kailali districts. 27 key informant interviews and six focus group discussions were conducted (total n=62 participants; 35 in focus groups) with community, civil-society and community-health stakeholders. A semistructured topic guide addressed vaccine knowledge and confidence, access, health-system performance, institutional trust and citizen participation. The inquiry was conceptually informed by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) framework for institutional trust and the IAP2 Spectrum of Public Participation. title: Fiscal Policy Responses of Indonesia During the COVID-19 Crisis: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has caused a global economic crisis that has impacted national economic stability, particularly in developing countries such as Indonesia. The Indonesian government has responded to this crisis through various expansionary fiscal policies aimed at maintaining economic stability and accelerating post-pandemic recovery. This study aims to systematically review Indonesia's fiscal policy response during the COVID-19 pandemic through a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach. The literature selection process was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. The literature search was conducted using Publish or Perish (PoP) on the Google Scholar database, followed by a screening and selection process using Rayyan. A total of 989 articles were identified, and after going through the selection stage, 12 articles that met the inclusion criteria were obtained. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive qualitative analysis and supplemented with bibliometric analysis using VOS viewer. The results showed that Indonesia's fiscal policy during the COVID-19 pandemic was expansive and adaptive, focusing on increasing government spending, fiscal stimulus, tax relaxation, and strengthening social protection programs. These policies have proven to be effective in preventing economic contraction and supporting short-term recovery. However, the effectiveness of fiscal policy still faces challenges related to fiscal sustainability, institutional coordination, and policy targeting. This study is expected to contribute academically and practically as a reference in formulating more adaptive fiscal policies in facing future crises.

title: Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Incidence During and After COVID-19 Social Distancing in Korea: A Nationwide 16-Year Interrupted Time-Series Analysis
abstract: Background Pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a rare but devastating event. However, the extent to which large-scale public health interventions, such as COVID-19 social distancing policies, affected the incidence of pediatric OHCA remains unclear. Methods We conducted a nationwide interrupted time-series analysis using data from the Korea Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Registry (2008-2023). The primary outcome was the monthly incidence of OHCA among individuals aged 0-18 years. The study period was divided into three phases: pre-intervention (January 2008-February 2020), social distancing (March 2020-April 2022), and post-lifting (May 2022-December 2023). We used segmented Poisson regression, adjusted for population size and seasonal variation, to estimate changes in monthly incidence at each policy change and reported the results as incidence rate ratios (IRRs). To determine whether these changes differed by age, we compared children with adults (19-64 years) and elderly individuals ([≥]65 years). Results Of the 456,839 registry entries, 10,965 were pediatric OHCAs, of which 6,891 underwent resuscitation in the emergency department. The crude incidence was 7.04, 7.14, and 8.35 per 100,000 person-years in the three phases, respectively. Before the pandemic, incidence rose slightly (annual IRR 1.006 [95% CI 1.001-1.012]; P = 0.032). At the implementation of social distancing, incidence fell immediately (IRR 0.926 [95% CI 0.865-0.991]; P = 0.027), without a significant change in slope (P = 0.081). After restrictions were lifted, incidence rose immediately (IRR 1.138 [95% CI 1.048-1.235]; P = 0.002) and then declined gradually (monthly IRR 0.993 [95% CI 0.988-0.999]; P = 0.023). These changes were confined to children aged 1-11 years (implementation IRR 0.812 [95% CI 0.666-0.991]; post-lifting IRR 1.562 [95% CI 1.278-1.909]). The pattern of change differed significantly by age group (P < 0.001), mainly because incidence rose in children, but not in adults or elderly individuals, after restrictions were lifted. Conclusions Nationwide social distancing was associated with a transient decrease in pediatric OHCA incidence, which was concentrated among children aged 1-11 years and was followed by a rebound above the expected level after restrictions were lifted. Surveillance of pediatric OHCA should account for abrupt changes in children's daily environments, including the closure and reopening of schools and childcare facilities.

title: The Course and Outcomes of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome during COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Purpose: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with limited access to healthcare. The aim was to investigate the course and outcomes of carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) during this time. Methods: We included 63 patients with CTS from one of our previous studies. Patients were contacted telephonically between August 2024 and March 2026. The mean time-interval between previous and the current assessment was 5.33 ± 0.60 years. Patients were interviewed regarding severity and treatment of CTS. Results: 23 (36.5%) of patients underwent surgery. This group was characterized by the higher male proportion and the worse baseline Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire (BCTQ) score. BCTQ improved in all patients but to the more extent in those who received surgery. Conclusion: Pandemic was associated with low rate of surgery for CTS. Surgical treatment was associated with better outcome, although patients not treated surgically might also improve. Worse clinical symptoms and male gender may be associated with pursue of surgical therapy during its limited availability.

title: SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro as an efficient endopeptidase for fusion tag removal in recombinant protein production
abstract: Fusion tags are widely employed to enhance recombinant protein expression, solubility, and purification. However, efficient tag removal is often necessary to obtain proteins in their native form. In this study, SARS-CoV-2 3C-like protease (3CLpro) was evaluated as a sequence-specific protease for fusion-tag removal using a recombinant fusion protein substrate under standard protein purification conditions. A substrate containing the canonical recognition sequence AVLQ↓SG was efficiently cleaved by 3CLpro, whereas no detectable cleavage was observed for a variant substrate harboring the sequence TVRLQ↓SG. Biochemical characterization demonstrated that 3CLpro maintained cleavage activity across a range of pH values and temperatures and in the presence of reagents commonly used for protein purification and stabilization. 3CLpro-mediated cleavage was successfully integrated into different fusion-protein processing workflows, including in-solution cleavage, on-column cleavage, and dialysis-coupled cleavage. To further evaluate the practical utility of 3CLpro, a modular expression vector (pET_RPLa) incorporating a 3CLpro cleavage site was constructed and validated using the light chain of botulinum neurotoxin serotype A (LC-BoNT/A) as a model protein. Following expression and purification, the fusion protein (6 × His-GST-AVLQSG-LC-BoNT/A) retained SNAP25-cleaving activity and was efficiently processed by 3CLpro. Together, these results support the potential use of SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro as a versatile sequence-specific protease for fusion-tag removal and recombinant protein processing.

title: IRF7 variants in fully vaccinated Iranian patients with severe COVID-19: a pilot observational study
abstract: Severe and critical cases of COVID-19 infections have been reported in healthy and fully vaccinated individuals, raising concerns about host genetic factors that may contribute to disease severity despite full vaccination. The type I interferon (IFN) signaling pathway plays a crucial role in antiviral immunity, and rare and deleterious mutations in its regulatory genes, including IRF7 and TLR7 , have been associated with severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. This study aims to investigate rare or functionally relevant variants in IRF7 and TLR7 in patients who developed severe or critical COVID-19 despite full vaccination. Thirteen patients aged up to 65 years with severe or critical COVID-19 were enrolled between December 1, 2021, and December 30, 2023. All had received at least two doses of the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. Patients with underlying comorbidities or known immunodeficiencies were excluded from the study. In addition, 30 mild or asymptomatic COVID-19 patients were included in the study as a control group. Genomic DNA was extracted, and PCR was performed to amplify selected exons of IRF7 (exons 1–3, 8–9) and TLR7 (exon 3 in males). Variants were annotated and classified according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines. Nine patients (69%) carried at least one IRF7 variant. Common benign polymorphisms were observed in several patients and controls. In contrast, the rare variants, including rs386749598, rs746951093, rs201036875, and c.381G > C, were detected only in patients with severe or critical COVID-19. The recurrent rs386749598 variant was identified in 38.5% of patients but was absent in all control subjects. No variants were detected in TLR7 in either group. Our preliminary findings suggest a possible association between rare IRF7 variants and severe COVID-19 despite full vaccination. However, larger studies and functional analyses are required to confirm their biological and clinical significance.

source_records.abstract: Severe and critical cases of COVID-19 infections have been reported in healthy and fully vaccinated individuals, raising concerns about host genetic factors that may contribute to disease severity despite full vaccination. The type I interferon (IFN) signaling pathway plays a crucial role in antiviral immunity, and rare and deleterious mutations in its regulatory genes, including IRF7 and TLR7 , have been associated with severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. This study aims to investigate rare or functionally relevant variants in IRF7 and TLR7 in patients who developed severe or critical COVID-19 despite full vaccination. Thirteen patients aged up to 65 years with severe or critical COVID-19 were enrolled between December 1, 2021, and December 30, 2023. All had received at least two doses of the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. Patients with underlying comorbidities or known immunodeficiencies were excluded from the study. In addition, 30 mild or asymptomatic COVID-19 patients were included in the study as a control group. Genomic DNA was extracted, and PCR was performed to amplify selected exons of IRF7 (exons 1–3, 8–9) and TLR7 (exon 3 in males). Variants were annotated and classified according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines. Nine patients (69%) carried at least one IRF7 variant. Common benign polymorphisms were observed in several patients and controls. In contrast, the rare variants, including rs386749598, rs746951093, rs201036875, and c.381G > C, were detected only in patients with severe or critical COVID-19. The recurrent rs386749598 variant was identified in 38.5% of patients but was absent in all control subjects. No variants were detected in TLR7 in either group. Our preliminary findings suggest a possible association between rare IRF7 variants and severe COVID-19 despite full vaccination. However, larger studies and functional analyses are required to confirm their biological and clinical significance.

title: Effect of starting metformin on severe and long COVID-19 among people living with type 2 diabetes in England: a new user cohort study in OpenSAFELY-TPP
abstract: Introduction Observational studies report lower COVID-19 mortality among metformin users, but most used prevalent-user designs comparing long-term survivors with heterogeneous controls. Randomised trials suggest little or no mortality effect. No large observational study has used a new-user design to estimate the effect of starting versus not starting metformin on severe and Long COVID outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). We aimed to estimate this effect on COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, COVID-19 diagnoses, and Long COVID among adults with T2D in England. Research design and methods Using OpenSAFELY-TPP linked NHS electronic health records, we conducted a population-based cohort study with a landmark new-user design. Adults aged 18-85 years newly diagnosed with T2D (August 2018-August 2019) were classified as starting metformin monotherapy within 6 months or not starting any antidiabetic drug, based on prescription data. Follow-up began 6 months after diagnosis and before the UK pandemic (avoiding immortal time) for up to 2 years. We estimated intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects using weighted Cox and pooled logistic regression, with negative (bone fracture) and positive (diabetes-related death) control outcomes. Results Of 52,341 eligible people, 19,599 (37.4%) started metformin. For COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, the maximally adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of metformin versus no antidiabetic was 1.17 (95% CI 1.02-1.35; 2-year risk difference 0.36%, 95% CI 0.09-0.62; intention-to-treat). The per-protocol HR for COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death was 1.11 (95% CI 0.96-1.29). The Long COVID estimate was imprecise (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.83-2.33; intention-to-treat). For bone fracture (negative control) the estimate was null (HR 1.00), but for diabetes-related deaths (positive control) it was elevated (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.09-1.81), indicating unmeasured confounding. Conclusions The risks of severe and long COVID were slightly higher among people who started metformin, compared with those who did not start. These results plausibly reflect unmeasured confounding. These findings align more closely with randomised evidence than earlier prevalent-user studies and argue against a clinically meaningful benefit of starting metformin for COVID-19 prevention in newly diagnosed T2D. What is already known on this topic Observational studies and their meta-analyses have consistently reported 30-40% lower COVID-19 mortality among metformin users, yet most used prevalent-user designs that compare long-term survivors with mixed control groups and can overstate benefit. Randomised trials suggest little or no effect on mortality. What this study adds Using a new-user design in more than 52,000 adults with newly diagnosed T2D, risks of severe and long COVID were slightly higher among people who started metformin, compared with those who did not start. These results plausibly reflect unmeasured confounding rather than harm. How this study might affect research, practice or policy These findings align with randomised evidence and argue against a clinically meaningful benefit of starting metformin for preventing severe or Long COVID in people with T2D. They also illustrate how new-user designs can reconcile discrepant observational and trial results and should be prioritised in future drug-repurposing studies. Lay summary Metformin is a medication commonly used to treat type 2 diabetes. During the COVID-19 pandemic, some studies suggested it might also protect against severe COVID-19, but many such studies had design limitations that could have made metformin look more beneficial than it truly is. In this study, we used NHS health records from over 52,000 adults in England who were newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes to examine whether starting metformin shortly after diagnosis reduced the risk of being hospitalised or dying from COVID-19, being diagnosed with COVID-19. We found no evidence that starting metformin protected against any of these outcomes, although the effect on long COVID was imprecisely estimated. Our findings are consistent with results from clinical trials and suggest that metformin should not be expected to prevent severe COVID-19 in people with type 2 diabetes.

title: Personalized cognitive and physical Telerehabilitation in post-COVID-19 condition and ME/CFS: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Background Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) share fatigue, post-exertional symptom exacerbation, and cognitive impairment. Aims To explore preliminary effects and feasibility of personalized telerehabilitation in PCC and ME/CFS. Methods This pilot randomized controlled trial analyzed 79 participants with baseline and 16-week assessments: 46 intervention and 33 standard-care controls. Individualized asynchronous cognitive and motor training was prescribed four times weekly and adapted weekly. Outcomes included neuropsychological performance, self-reported symptoms, and six-minute walk test performance. Feasibility measures included platform-recorded adherence and System Usability Scale (SUS) scores. Results Between-group change comparisons and domain-level Time × Group interactions were not significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Within-intervention improvements in sustained attention and semantic verbal fluency remained significant after FDR correction (both pFDR = 0.028). Exploratory principal component analysis identified PC1, explaining 27.2% of cognitive change variance. Covariate-adjusted regressions showed higher PC1 scores in intervention participants (β = 0.715, p = 0.043) and a positive association with motor adherence within this group (β = 0.089, p = 0.005); these p-values were not corrected for multiple comparisons. Median motor and cognitive adherence were 99.75% and 100.00%, respectively; median SUS was 77.5. Conclusion Recorded adherence and usability provided preliminary support for feasibility under individualized clinical support, whose contact intensity was not systematically recorded. Domain-level analyses did not establish differential cognitive benefit after FDR correction. Exploratory PCA findings require confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials.

title: Structural Biology of the SARS-CoV-2 Proteome: Experimental Context, Functional Interpretation, and Intervention Research
abstract: Structural biology has defined key features of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) proteome, although structural coverage and functional support remain uneven. This review connects representative structures of structural, nonstructural, and accessory proteins with evidence from biochemical, cellular, computational, and intervention studies. We ask when structural observations support biological interpretations and what additional evidence connects those interpretations to intervention outcomes. Structural coverage, experimental context, and functional support are recorded as separate dimensions across selected proteins, complexes, virions, replication organelles, and variant studies. Selected cases show that resolved structures can coexist with disputed functions; where the evidence compared here allows, we state which interpretations we regard as adequately supported and which remain candidate explanations. Differences between studies can also reflect complementary observations at different scales. Antiviral, antibody, and vaccine studies show how structures contribute to design and mechanistic interpretation, whereas clinical outcomes concern specific products, populations, and endpoints. Major gaps concern native assemblies, the physiological relevance of some accessory-protein findings, and the translation of molecular recognition into antiviral efficacy or protective immunity.

title: Mild COVID-19 presentations in unexposed individuals favour development of long-lived immune responses to SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Abstract Background Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), originally reported in Wuhan, China in December 2019 rapidly spread throughout the world resulting in a global pandemic from March 2020. Caused by infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the clinical spectrum ranges from asymptomatic to severe and fatal disease. Most patients experience uncomplicated disease, with a wide range of clinical presentations including, headache, fever, cough, dyspnea, sore throat, fatigue, asnomia, myalgia, abdominal pain, diarrhea and nausea. It is well documented that immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 contribute to both immune protection and pathogenesis. Although much useful research has focussed on immune responses predisposing to severe COVID-19, much less is known on whether diverse uncomplicated disease presentations influence the quality and/or magnitude of the immune response to the virus. Methods To address this knowledge gap, we pursued a systems immunology approach integrating high dimensional mass cytometry and cytokine responses after SARS-CoV-2 re-stimulation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from a retrospective study conducted in Australia in 2020. Results Cell populations identified by mass cytometry significantly expanding in response to spike-protein in vitro stimulation segregated the cohort in patients having ≥ 4 or ≤ 3 symptoms. Cell populations featured by patients with no more than 3 symptoms included CCR7 + T H2 cells, T H2 -polarised T FH cells, along with IgM + classical memory B cells and CXCR3 low , CD10 low classical monocytes. Notably, these responses persisted for 6 months post-exposure, in the absence of new infections. Conclusions Together, our results suggest that in previously COVID-19 naïve individuals, mild COVID-19 presentations might support the development of long-lasting immunity to SARS-CoV-2, able to contribute to protection during re-infection.

title: A novel interprofessional experience caring for post-intensive care and long COVID patients: the optimal clinic experience.
abstract: This short report describes the development of an interprofessional ambulatory care clinic with an interprofessional education program at an academic medical center providing comprehensive care to patients previously hospitalized in the intensive care unit (ICU) or with COVID-19 from May 2020 to May 2026. The OPTIMAL Clinic (lOng COVID/PosT-Icu MultidisciplinAry cLinic) was created during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, with limited staff and temporary funding. Our team consisted of clinical pharmacy and physician trainees, nurse practitioners, occupational therapists, physical therapists, pharmacists, physicians, and social workers, who collaborated strategically and synergistically to optimize patient care. Across repeated evaluations, the clinic model was associated with increased preventive care and financial sustainability, and decreased emergency department visits and unplanned hospitalizations. Our interprofessional education program achieved high ratings from trainees in preceptor support, onboarding, clinical activities, and interprofessional education. Our OPTIMAL clinic exemplifies a model for interprofessional care and education for the support of complex patients after ICU or COVID-19 hospitalizations.

title: Video-observed treatment for TB patients during COVID-19 in Senegal: efficacy, feasibility, and acceptability.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic caused disruption to TB services and negatively affected key TB control indicators. To support continuity of care and strengthen treatment adherence during the pandemic, a video-observed therapy (VOT) intervention using WhatsApp was introduced and evaluated among TB patients in Dakar, Senegal. A mixed-methods study conducted between January and March 2021 compared adherence, clinical progress, and treatment outcomes among patients receiving daily VOT and those receiving standard, facility-based directly observed therapy (DOT). Feasibility and acceptability were also explored through interviews with patients and TB clinic staff. Ninety-seven patients received VOT across five clinics, and 146 patients received DOT and formed the comparison group. Participants were predominantly male with a mean age of 32.5 years. At the end of the intensive phase, adherence was slightly higher in the VOT group compared with DOT (78% vs. 73%), and acid-fast bacillus positivity was marginally lower (14% vs. By treatment completion, cure rates were high and similar in both groups. Qualitative findings indicated that VOT was acceptable and feasible for patients and providers, though challenges included unreliable internet connectivity and concerns about privacy. Overall, VOT appears to be a practical alternative to standard DOT, particularly during public health emergencies that limit access to in-person care.

title: A conserved tyrosine in the S1/S2 loop shapes SARS-CoV-2 spike processing and host protease usage.
abstract: Both spike processing efficiency and host protease usage play critical roles in SARS-CoV-2 infection, pathogenesis, and transmission. The SARS-CoV-2 spike contains two motifs, a furin cleavage site (FCS) and an extended S1/S2 loop, which improve both cleavage efficiency and host protease usage. Disruption of these motifs significantly attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection and pathogenesis. Importantly, modifications and changes within the S1/S2 loop can also shape infection and disease outcomes following infection. In this study, we examined mass spectrometry data generated from purified virions from wild-type (WT) or mutant SARS-CoV-2 infection. We identified phosphorylation occurring at highly conserved residue Y674 and used reverse genetics to generate a mutant that ablates phosphorylation capacity in the S1/ S2 loop (Y674F). Our results show that the Y674F mutant replicated equivalently to wild-type SARS-CoV-2 in Vero cells but had attenuated replication in a human respiratory cell line. Golden Syrian hamsters infected with the Y674F mutant had equivalent weight loss, lung viral titer, and similar immune pathology to WT SARS-CoV-2. However, the mutant had reduced viral load in the nasal wash and reduced antigen staining in the large airways in the lung. Notably, loss of Y674 ablated spike processing to the S1/S2 cleavage product on virions. In addition, Y674F mutant had a diminished capacity to utilize host protease TMPRSS2 for entry. Together, these data indicates that post-translational modification of Y674 impacts SARS-CoV-2 infection of the airway by disrupting both spike processing and host protease function. These results add to data demonstrating the importance of spike S1/S2 loop modifications to SARS-CoV-2 infection, pathogenesis, and transmission.

title: Reconstructing age-specific social contact patterns across 28 EU/EEA countries during the COVID-19 pandemic: linking non-pharmaceutical interventions to social mixing, 2020–2022
abstract: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, most EU/EEA countries sequentially introduced non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) to reduce social contacts and mitigate transmission. The CoMix study captured real-time changes in social mixing, but substantial spatiotemporal gaps remain, with some countries lacking pandemic contact data. We developed a model-based framework to estimate time-varying changes in age-specific contact patterns and relate these changes to NPIs recorded in the ECDC-JRC Response Measures Database. This relationship was used to predict contacts during periods without CoMix observations. For countries without CoMix data, we reconstructed temporal age-specific mixing patterns using estimates from countries with pandemic contact data selected through a country-matching process based on socio-demographic characteristics and similarity in NPI implementation. We generated age-specific contact matrices for 28 EU/EEA countries spanning 2020-2022. Reconstructed patterns captured substantial temporal and cross-country variation in social mixing and its evolving association with NPIs across diverse European contexts. Our framework provides estimates that extend incomplete pandemic contact data across both time and countries, yielding a consistent set of age-specific contact matrices for the EU/EEA. These estimates address important gaps in empirical social-contact data and provide valuable insights into the interplay of NPIs and social mixing patterns which is of critical importance to improving epidemic modelling and policy making.

We generated age-specific contact matrices for 28 EU/EEA countries spanning 2020-2022. Reconstructed patterns captured substantial temporal and cross-country variation in social mixing and its evolving association with NPIs across diverse European contexts. Our framework provides estimates that extend incomplete pandemic contact data across both time and countries, yielding a consistent set of age-specific contact matrices for the EU/EEA. title: Proteogenomic Alterations in Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells of Psoriasis Patients Recovered from COVID-19
abstract: Abstract To address a critical gap in understanding why autoimmune disorders often worsen after COVID 19, we performed integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of peripheral blood mononuclear cells in patients with psoriasis with or without prior SARS CoV 2 infection to define proteogenomic alterations associated with post COVID exacerbations. COVID recovered patients with psoriasis exhibited a distinct immune and molecular profile characterized by upregulation of pro inflammatory cytokines and downregulation of antimicrobial peptides, alongside increased expression of genes involved in antimicrobial defense. Pathway analyses revealed concurrent activation of T cell receptor signaling and perturbations in protein and messenger RNA biogenesis, including altered ribosomal and proteasomal metabolism, ribosomal RNA expression, and NF κB signaling. These findings indicate that SARS CoV 2 infection drives immune dysregulation and cellular stress responses that contribute to psoriasis exacerbation. The identified molecular signatures provide a rationale for incorporating post COVID syndrome into existing therapeutic strategies for psoriasis.

title: The interaction effect of COVID-19 infection and hypoxia at high altitudes on the physiological functions of multiple systems- A cross-sectional study based on people at high altitudes
abstract: Abstract Backgroud: Both the low-oxygen environment at high altitudes and COVID-19 infection can independently cause cardiopulmonary dysfunction. There are multiple intersections at the pathophysiological level between the two, but their synergistic effects and long-term impacts remain unclear. Methods This study adopted a cross-sectional design and included 290 Han residents from Lhasa City, who were divided into a COVID-19 recovery group (COVID-19) and an uninfected control group(N-COVID).Demographic characteristics and psychological behavior data were collected through standardized questionnaires. CPET, muscle strength and balance tests were used to assess cardiopulmonary and muscle neuropsychological functions between the two groups. The aim was to reveal the functional recovery characteristics and potential mechanisms of COVID-19 recovered patients in high-altitude hypoxic environments. Result VO 2 peak/kg,VE/VCO 2 ,VE/VCO 2 slope and RER in COVID-19 were significantly increased ( P P 2 peak/kg [B(95%CI): 1.796 (0.292–3.301)], VE/VCO 2 slope[B(95%CI): 1.886(0.207–3.565)], RER[B (95%CI): 0.035 (0.017–0.052)], balance left/right [B(95%CI):14.869(19.807–9.932)/14.959(9-10.149-19.76)] have an independent correlation effect ( P P P P > 0.05). Conclusions During the long-term recovery from COVID-19 at high altitude, the reduction of VE/VCO 2 slope persists, and its sensitivity to recognizing cardiopulmonary dysfunction is superior to that of VO 2 peak. Meanwhile, the hypoxic environment at high altitude has a significant independent impact on VD/VT. The resulting pattern of functional dimension separation constitutes the specific pathophysiological phenotype of recovered COVID-19 patients at high altitude. Trial registration: All subjects signed the informed consent form at the time of inclusion. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee, with the approval number 2021(53).

title: Prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation combined with cognitive training reduces anxiety, daytime sleepiness, and cognitive complaints in women after COVID-19: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Persistent anxiety, disturbed sleep, and subjective cognitive complaints are frequent and often co-occur after COVID-19, especially in women, yet interventions addressing them together are limited. We examined whether adding left-prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to cognitive training reduces these symptoms in women with post-COVID cognitive complaints. METHODS In a single-centre, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial, 30 women with confirmed prior COVID-19 and self-reported cognitive decline (Mini-Mental State Examination ≥ 24; no diagnosed neurodegenerative disorder) were allocated to three groups (n = 10 each): cognitive training plus active tDCS (CT + tDCS), cognitive training plus sham tDCS (CT + sham), or cognitive training only (CT only). Active tDCS targeted the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (2 mA, 20 min; anode F3, return F7) across nine sessions over three weeks. Anxiety (Beck Anxiety Inventory), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), cognition (Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-Revised), reaction times (psychomotor speed), and prefrontal electroencephalographic (EEG) cortical arousal and frontal asymmetry were assessed at baseline and after the ninth session; there was no follow-up. All participants completed the trial (no dropout). Groups were compared using analysis of covariance adjusted for the corresponding baseline score, with non-parametric confirmation and false-discovery-rate correction. RESULTS Relative to both comparison groups, the CT + tDCS group showed significantly lower anxiety and daytime sleepiness and higher global cognition, memory, and fluency, with faster reaction times (all corrected p < .05). Cortical arousal increased and frontal asymmetry shifted toward greater relative left-frontal activation. The CT + sham and CT only groups did not differ from each other, and near-ceiling attention and visuospatial scores were unchanged. CONCLUSIONS Adding left-prefrontal tDCS to cognitive training reduced anxiety and daytime sleepiness and improved cognition and psychomotor speed in women with post-COVID cognitive complaints, with parallel changes in prefrontal EEG markers. Confirmation in larger samples is needed.

title: "Are you going to get busy living or are you going to get busy dying?" Traumatic stressors in older adult-caregiver dyads during COVID-19 social scarcity in the USA.
abstract: Abstract Background The 2022 US National Strategy to Support Caregivers emphasises the importance of understanding trauma as part of caregiving relationships. However, this focus has not been applied to understanding caregiving during social scarcity such as COVID-19 from a dyadic older adult-caregiver perspectives. Methods Drawing on joint perspectives of 11 older adult-caregiver dyads (N = 22), this qualitative thematic study explored how social scarcity impacted caregiving relationships, and whether there was evidence of traumatic stress in shared experiences. Dyads represented parent-child, relatives, and friend relationships aside from spouses. Results Three themes were identified: (1) interactional micro-injuries and micro-adaptations; (2) nested troubles: present challenges and old wounds; and (3) eudaemonic deprivation—a perception of the erosion of order, meaning and purpose. Stressors were described as continuous fear, losses, grief, loneliness, loss of meaning, and disruptive feelings of anxiety impacting caregiving relationships. Discussion Older adults demonstrated keener, sharper experiences of losses, and generally expressed self-focused distress whereas caregivers expressed generally adaptive and dyad-oriented responses. Powerlessness was a feature of traumatic stress reflected among older adults, and it was responsibility among caregivers. The study underscores the importance of trauma-informed support in caregiving at a time of involuntary and prolonged exposure to social scarcity.
journal: International journal of qualitative studies on health and well-being

title: Possible SARS‐CoV‐2 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae co‐detection during the early COVID‐19 pandemic: diagnostic challenges in a resource‐limited setting.
abstract: During the early Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, diagnostic pathways were disrupted by limited access to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) testing, evolving clinical knowledge and substantial diagnostic uncertainty. We report a case in which Mycoplasma pneumoniae ( M. pneumoniae ) and SARS-CoV-2 were both detected early in the clinical course of a previously healthy 35-year-old man in April 2020. The patient met all six Japanese clinical criteria for atypical pneumonia, and chest computed tomography demonstrated multifocal ground-glass opacities compatible with atypical pneumonia. Clarithromycin was initiated on Day 4. pneumoniae particle agglutination titre of 1 : 640 was recognized on Day 6, supporting possible M. pneumoniae infection, although serology alone cannot confirm acute disease. Later that afternoon, a positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR result was reported, prompting reframing of the working diagnosis towards COVID-19. Antimicrobial therapy was temporarily discontinued and subsequently adjusted. This case illustrates how early-pandemic diagnostic constraints, delayed availability of microbiological results and overlapping radiological findings created diagnostic complexity. Although cognitive biases such as anchoring may have contributed to the diagnostic shift, available information is insufficient to establish them as definitive causes. Instead, this case highlights the challenges of interpreting limited diagnostic data in a resource-restricted setting. As contemporary COVID-19 disease severity has attenuated and atypical bacterial infections have resurged, maintaining awareness of possible co-detection remains important for accurate clinical assessment.

title: Exploring the Evolving Role of US Hospital Chaplains During COVID-19 Through a Job Demands-Resource Theoretical Lens.
abstract: During the pandemic, the need for spiritual care grew exponentially. Although a growing body of literature has documented the experience of frontline healthcare providers such as physicians and nurses, the experiences of hospital chaplains remain largely underrepresented. In response to this gap in knowledge, this qualitative study aimed to understand how hospital chaplains (n = 12) employed at a large medical center in Southern California adapted their roles to navigate significant organizational, interpersonal, and personal challenges, through the lens of the Job Demands-Resources framework. With a 100% response rate among eligible participants, findings illustrate how chaplains drew on available resources and engaged in job crafting to care for patients and caregivers, support healthcare staff, and cultivate their own well-being. Job crafting strategies included creative adaptations to provide compassionate care to patients and caregivers; the creation of alternate safe space and embedding themselves in clinical units to better support healthcare staff; and the adoption of new self-care practices and routines, intentional boundary setting, and the cultivation of self-compassion. The findings highlight the critical yet frequently underrecognized role of chaplains in healthcare systems and underscore the need for intentional organizations' investments in chaplains as integral members of healthcare teams.

title: Vaccine responses to influenza viruses and SARS-CoV-2 under novel immunotherapies in myasthenia gravis and CIDP: a prospective observational study
abstract: Abstract Patients with myasthenia gravis (MG) and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) require long-term immunotherapy, making effective vaccination essential for infection prophylaxis. As these immunotherapies increasingly involve novel agents such as FcRn antagonists and complement inhibitors, their influence on the vaccine response needs to be assessed. Therefore, we prospectively enrolled 23 patients with MG or CIDP receiving contemporary immunotherapies who were vaccinated against influenza viruses ( n = 21; Northern Hemisphere 2025/26) or SARS-CoV-2 ( n = 12). Sera collected before and at least two weeks after vaccination were assayed for antibodies against the SARS-CoV-2 spike S1 subunit and three influenza strains. A response to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination (≥ 2-fold increase in anti-S1 IgG) was observed in 9 of 12 patients (75%; median fold-change 2.6), and influenza seroprotection rates (haemagglutination inhibition [HAI] titer ≥ 1:40) rose for all three strains reaching 86% (A/H1N1), 76% (B/Victoria), and 67% (A/H3N2). The effect of individual medications on post-vaccination titers was assessed by analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for baseline titer and diagnosis. In these exploratory models, estimates were directionally higher under ravulizumab and lower under efgartigimod and mycophenolate; none remained statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Patients receiving efgartigimod and mycophenolate concurrently had significantly lower absolute post-vaccination HAI titers for A/H1N1 (median 1:30 vs. 1:160; p = 0.0085) and A/H3N2 (median p = 0.022). These findings are consistent with lower baseline and circulating antibody levels and do not show a detectable difference in fold-change in this small exploratory cohort. Patients who failed to seroconvert to any strain were more frequently receiving FcRn antagonists, yet most retained seroprotection against at least one strain. Under FcRn antagonism, influenza titers did not parallel total serum IgG, with several patients seroconverting despite a concurrent decline in total IgG. In conclusion, most patients mounted a measurable humoral response to both vaccines despite contemporary immunotherapy.

title: Web-Based Isha Kriya Meditation and Breathwork in Long COVID: Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
abstract: Background Long COVID affects millions of adults, causing fatigue, dyspnea, cognitive symptoms, and mood disturbances. Effective treatments are limited, and many patients cannot access multidisciplinary rehabilitation because of symptom fluctuation, distance, or specialist shortages. Web-based mind-body interventions may offer accessible, scalable support alongside existing care. Objective We assessed the feasibility and efficacy of a 3-week web-based yogic breathing and meditation program for long COVID symptoms. Methods In this completed, parallel-group, 6-week waitlist-controlled, mixed methods randomized trial, adults aged 18-70 years with physician-confirmed long COVID were recruited from US clinics and self-referral and randomized 1:1 to immediate intervention or waitlist control, crossing over at week 3. The program included live webinars and video guides for daily self-practice. The primary outcome was adherence, defined as practicing at least 1 of 3 techniques on ≥4 days/week across all 3 active-intervention weeks. Secondary outcomes included perceived stressmood, quality of life, dyspnea, and somatic symptom burden, assessed at baseline, 3 weeks, and 6 weeks. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Semistructured interviews and focus groups underwent conventional content analysis and were integrated with quantitative findings via joint display. Results Of 189 randomized participants, 1 was excluded post-randomization for a protocol deviation; 188 (96 intervention, 92 waitlist) began the study. Of these, 124 reached the active intervention period. Among 58 with complete adherence data, 55% met the adherence threshold (60% intervention, 50% waitlist). Secondary analyses included 185 participants with ≥1 assessment. No adverse events were reported. Compared with waitlist control, the intervention group showed greater reductions in total mood disturbance (MD=-10; 95% CI -19 to -1.6; P=.02), negative mood (MD=-7.5; 95% CI -15 to -0.44; P=.04), fatigue (MD=-2.9; 95% CI -4.6 to -1.2; P=.001), MDP immediate perception (MD=-5.5; 95% CI -9.4 to -1.6; P=.007), MDP sensory dimension (MD=-5.1; 95% CI -8.5 to -1.7; P=.003), and somatic symptom burden (MD=-2.0; 95% CI -3.6 to -0.38; P=.02), and greater increases in positive mood (MD=2.9; 95% CI 0.66 to 5.1; P=.01) and vigor (MD=1.7; 95% CI 0.18 to 3.2; P=.03). Stress and quality of life did not differ significantly. Qualitative findings identified medical-system struggles, digital delivery, online support, and practices' effects on resilience and identity. Integration showed convergence for dyspnea and mood, divergence for stress and quality of life, and expansion through themes of medical-system experience, identity, and social connection. Conclusions This web-based yogic breathing and meditation program appears feasible and accessible for people with long COVID. By combining 3 practices in a brief protocol and integrating quantitative and qualitative evidence, this study provides novel insight into both symptom outcomes and dimensions of recovery not captured by standardized measures. Further evaluation should assess longer-term effects and integration into scalable telehealth and virtual rehabilitation pathways.

title: Wastewater-based epidemiology during New Zealand's COVID-19 elimination response: real-world public health impact and economic evaluation
abstract: ABSTRACT After more than a year without community transmission, a localised outbreak of COVID-19 occurred in Auckland, New Zealand, in August 2021. The response to this outbreak was supported by wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) with over 5,000 wastewater tests from 217 locations across New Zealand. This study provides specific real-world examples of the use of WBE to detect pathogen circulation and to provide supporting evidence that transmission was absent or limited in a community, and how this can directly influence public health actions. Evidence of community transmission via positive wastewater tests informed the escalation of public health responses, while early identification of infection in communities with no known cases enabled targeted interventions that contributed to effective control and pathogen elimination from a community. The economic benefits of these responses, quantified in millions of NZ dollars per day, highlight the value of WBE at low disease incidence and emphasise the importance of detection patterns in interpreting results and supporting communication to the public regarding infection risk. WBE can be a highly impactful and cost-effective public health tool in the response to disease incursions. Pandemic preparedness must include plans for selecting appropriate WBE sampling locations and ensuring the capacity to analyse sufficient samples rapidly.

title: COVID-19 vaccination response and challenges in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted critical vulnerabilities within public health systems worldwide, particularly in resource-limited settings where health infrastructure, vaccine access, surveillance capacity, and community engagement influenced vaccination outcomes. In Nigeria, subnational experiences varied considerably, and Bayelsa State encountered unique operational challenges related to vaccine distribution, uptake, completion of vaccination schedules, data monitoring, and equitable access. Understanding these implementation experiences is essential for strengthening future immunization programmes and pandemic preparedness strategies. This study aimed to evaluate COVID-19 vaccination coverage, vaccine distribution patterns, temporal implementation trends, priority population uptake, gender-related differences, and state-level performance in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. The study further sought to identify operational challenges and generate evidence-based lessons for improving vaccination programmes and public health emergency preparedness in similar resource-limited settings. A retrospective descriptive epidemiological analysis was conducted using routinely collected, aggregated COVID-19 vaccination surveillance data reported through the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) Daily Call-In reporting system. Data available up to 31 December 2023 were analysed. Vaccination performance indicators were assessed according to vaccine type, priority population groups, sex distribution, vaccination status, primary-series completion, and comparative state-level coverage. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, proportions, and graphical summaries, were used to characterise vaccination patterns and identify coverage gaps. AstraZeneca (48.3%) and Pfizer (29.6%) accounted for the largest proportion of administered vaccines. Vaccination coverage varied substantially across population groups, with healthcare workers achieving the highest uptake (96.2%), while the general adult population recorded the lowest coverage (44.6%). Males accounted for 54.3% of administered doses compared with 45.7% among females, indicating differences in vaccine uptake patterns. Bayelsa State achieved 61.3% completion of the primary vaccination series among the eligible population, remaining below the national target of 70%. These findings demonstrate important variations in vaccine access, uptake, and completion across population categories. COVID-19 vaccination efforts in Bayelsa State successfully protected priority groups but were constrained by operational, sociocultural, and health-system challenges. Persistent coverage gaps highlight the need for targeted interventions addressing vaccine confidence, equitable access, data quality, and programme sustainability. Strengthening gender-responsive communication strategies, improving vaccine supply-chain systems, integrating COVID-19 vaccination with routine health services, and enhancing digital surveillance platforms are recommended to improve preparedness for future public health emergencies. Effective, equitable, and data-driven vaccination strategies remain essential for reducing disease burden, strengthening health-system resilience, and protecting populations in resource-limited settings.

source_records.title: COVID-19 vaccination response and challenges in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
source_records.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted critical vulnerabilities within public health systems worldwide, particularly in resource-limited settings where health infrastructure, vaccine access, surveillance capacity, and community engagement influenced vaccination outcomes. In Nigeria, subnational experiences varied considerably, and Bayelsa State encountered unique operational challenges related to vaccine distribution, uptake, completion of vaccination schedules, data monitoring, and equitable access. Understanding these implementation experiences is essential for strengthening future immunization programmes and pandemic preparedness strategies. This study aimed to evaluate COVID-19 vaccination coverage, vaccine distribution patterns, temporal implementation trends, priority population uptake, gender-related differences, and state-level performance in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. The study further sought to identify operational challenges and generate evidence-based lessons for improving vaccination programmes and public health emergency preparedness in similar resource-limited settings. A retrospective descriptive epidemiological analysis was conducted using routinely collected, aggregated COVID-19 vaccination surveillance data reported through the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) Daily Call-In reporting system. Data available up to 31 December 2023 were analysed. Vaccination performance indicators were assessed according to vaccine type, priority population groups, sex distribution, vaccination status, primary-series completion, and comparative state-level coverage. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, proportions, and graphical summaries, were used to characterise vaccination patterns and identify coverage gaps. AstraZeneca (48.3%) and Pfizer (29.6%) accounted for the largest proportion of administered vaccines. Vaccination coverage varied substantially across population groups, with healthcare workers achieving the highest uptake (96.2%), while the general adult population recorded the lowest coverage (44.6%). Males accounted for 54.3% of administered doses compared with 45.7% among females, indicating differences in vaccine uptake patterns. Bayelsa State achieved 61.3% completion of the primary vaccination series among the eligible population, remaining below the national target of 70%. These findings demonstrate important variations in vaccine access, uptake, and completion across population categories. Persistent coverage gaps highlight the need for targeted interventions addressing vaccine confidence, equitable access, data quality, and programme sustainability. Strengthening gender-responsive communication strategies, improving vaccine supply-chain systems, integrating COVID-19 vaccination with routine health services, and enhancing digital surveillance platforms are recommended to improve preparedness for future public health emergencies. title: Beyond ACE2 downregulation: daphnetin as a multi-target agent for COVID-19 and rheumatic comorbidities.
abstract: The continuous emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., JN.1, KP.3) and the significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 in patients with rheumatic autoimmune diseases highlight an urgent unmet clinical need for dual-targeted therapeutics. Daphnetin (7,8-dihydroxycoumarin), a natural coumarin compound with a long history of clinical use in China, prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection by downregulating the viral entry receptor ACE2 through inhibition of HIF-1α and JAK2/STAT3 signaling. This review synthesizes the pleiotropic pharmacological mechanisms of daphnetin, including anti-inflammatory (NF-κB, JAK/STAT, NLRP3), antioxidant (Nrf2/Keap1), immunomodulatory (Th17/Treg balance), and mitochondrial protective pathways. These pathways are critically involved in the pathogenesis of both severe COVID-19 and rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We propose that daphnetin represents a novel "one agent, dual protection" strategy: it not only blocks viral entry by reducing ACE2 but also mitigates the hyperinflammatory and oxidative stress states that exacerbate both COVID-19 severity and rheumatic disease activity. Given its established safety, oral activity, and low cost, daphnetin is a promising candidate for clinical translation in high-risk comorbid populations. Key unresolved questions and future research directions are also discussed.

title: A Relapsing Autoimmune CNS Disorder with Dynamic Pleocytosis Following COVID-19 Vaccination
abstract: Objective To describe a challenging case of a recurrent autoimmune CNS disorder following Ad26.COV2.S COVID-19 vaccination. Background Post-vaccination inflammatory CNS syndromes are increasingly recognized but remain diagnostically challenging, particularly when clinical and laboratory findings are atypical or evolving. Disease course and optimal immunotherapy duration remain unclear. Results 45-year-old woman presented with fever and new-onset intractable headache with meningismus within one week of receiving COVID-19 vaccine. Initial CSF analysis demonstrated leukocytosis with neutrophilic predominance. MRI brain showed mild diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement. She was empirically treated for bacterial meningitis. CSF cultures and viral studies, including HSV-1/HSV-2 PCR, was negative. During her course, she developed bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, raising concern for Cogan syndrome; however, other systemic findings including interstitial keratitis were negative. She was readmitted with recurrent fever, worsening headache. Serial lumbar punctures demonstrated dynamic CSF pleocytosis, with neutrophilic predominance during febrile episodes and lymphocytic predominance when afebrile. Extensive evaluation, including CSF autoimmune encephalitis panel (including GFAP-IgG), MOG antibodies, CSF flow cytometry, PET imaging, and genetic testing for periodic fever syndromes, was unrevealing. Brain biopsy was unremarkable. Evaluation for systemic vasculitis, sarcoidosis, IgG4-related disease, and Behçet disease was negative. Over time, the patient developed persistent chronic cough of unclear etiology despite negative systemic and pulmonary evaluations, raising concern for neurogenic cough. The patient demonstrated partial clinical response to corticosteroids but experienced relapses during tapering. Mycophenolate mofetil provided limited benefit. Significant clinical and radiographic improvement was observed following initiation of rituximab. Conclusions This case highlights a relapsing autoimmune CNS disorder with CSF pleocytosis and leptomeningeal involvement following COVID-19 vaccination. The patient’s relapsing course over years and marked response to B-cell depletion support autoimmune mechanism. While autoimmune neurological events after Ad26.COV2.S vaccination have been reported, this case is notable for relapsing trajectory and highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, including uncertainty regarding optimal immunotherapy duration.

title: Psychological resilience and emotion regulation as mediators between COVID-19 fear and mental health outcomes
abstract: This cross-sectional study examined whether psychological resilience and emotion regulation difficulties mediate the relationship between COVID-19 fear and mental health outcomes among 1483 Turkish adults. Anxiety and depression served as primary outcomes given their status as the most prevalent mental health consequences of pandemic-related fear. Structural equation modeling revealed partial mediation through both pathways. When examined simultaneously, emotion regulation difficulties showed substantially stronger mediating effects (β = 0.21 for anxiety, β = 0.27 for depression) than psychological resilience (β = 0.04 for anxiety, β = 0.05 for depression). Women reported higher fear, anxiety, depression, and emotion regulation difficulties; men showed greater resilience. Married participants exhibited higher resilience and lower distress than single participants, and income reduction predicted increased depression. Emotion regulation difficulties may represent a particularly relevant intervention target for reducing pandemic-related distress, although experimental research is needed to confirm intervention effectiveness.

title: The effects of submaximal exercise on acid-base balance in people with long COVID.
abstract: Better pathophysiological understanding of long COVID (LC) is required, and disruption of acid-base regulation has been proposed as a potential mechanism underlying exercise intolerance observed in LC; however, empirical evidence remains limited. Accordingly, this study aims to systematically characterise day-to-day variation in acid-base status in individuals living with LC. Thirty people (19 female) with a confirmed diagnosis of LC or 15 healthy controls (CON; 8 female) completed three study visits. Participants completed two submaximal cardiopulmonary exercise tests (CPETs) separated by 24 h. Pre- and post-exercise fingertip capillary blood samples were collected on both CPET days for acid-base balance (pH, HCO3-, anion gap, K+, Na+, Cl- and ionized calcium (iCa2+)) and lactate. Subgroup analysis was conducted for those presenting with metabolic acidosis between LC and CON. Whole group analysis revealed no differences between LC and CON for acid-base balance (P > 0.05) or CPET variables (P > 0.05). However, a subgroup analysis determined that following CPET1, 17% (n = 5/30), and following CPET2, 33% (n = 10/30) of those with LC demonstrated metabolic acidosis, with small to large effect sizes (0.20 → 0.80) between LC and CON for pH, HCO3-, anion gap, K+, Na+, Cl-, iCa2+ and lactate. For CON, metabolic acidosis was identified for 6% (n = 1/18) on CPET day 1 and 11% (n = 2/18) on CPET day 2. Our findings suggest that some people with LC may experience acid-base balance disturbances following repeated submaximal exercise. Accordingly, a pathological subgroup is hypothesised, and these findings should provoke independent validation.
