title: Fulminant cardiogenic shock complicated by SARS-CoV-2-triggered systemic capillary leak syndrome: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Systemic capillary leak syndrome is a rare but potentially fatal condition characterised by massive plasma extravasation into the interstitial space, leading to intravascular hypovolaemia, hypoalbuminaemia, and haemoconcentration. It can be triggered by viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2. Case summary We present the case of a 62-year-old woman who developed fulminant SARS-CoV-2-triggered myocarditis and systemic capillary leak syndrome, with refractory cardiogenic and hypovolaemic shock. Treatment included venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, immunosuppression, and immunoglobulins. Progressive haemoconcentration, intravascular hypovolaemia, and coagulation impairment led to a complex haemodynamic pattern that culminated in multiple organ failure and death. Discussion This case illustrates the limitations of mechanical support in the context of systemic capillary leak syndrome, where massive third spacing with relative hypovolaemia can induce refractory venous suction and where coagulation abnormalities can lead to systemic thrombosis.

title: Changes in Depressive Symptoms Across the COVID-19 Pandemic and Recovery Periods Among Korean Adults: A Repeated Cross-Sectional Analysis of KNHANES 2018–2024
abstract: Background/Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with changes in population mental health, but whether elevated depressive symptoms persisted during subsequent recovery periods remains unclear. This study examined changes in depressive symptoms before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic among Korean adults and explored whether temporal patterns differed by sex. Methods: Data were obtained from 21,228 adults aged ≥20 years who participated in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024, representing the pre-pandemic, pandemic, early recovery, and later recovery periods, respectively. Clinically relevant depressive symptoms were defined as a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score ≥ 10. Survey-weighted analyses accounting for the complex sampling design was performed, including multivariable logistic regression and period-by-sex interaction analysis. Results: The weighted prevalence of depressive symptoms was 4.3% in 2018, increased to 5.3% in 2020, decreased to 4.7% in 2022, and was 4.3% in 2024, the same point estimate as in 2018. In the fully adjusted model, the odds of depressive symptoms were higher in 2020 than in 2018 (odds ratio [OR] = 1.316, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.056–1.641), whereas the estimates for 2022 (OR = 1.187, 95% CI: 0.945–1.490) and 2024 (OR = 1.125, 95% CI: 0.905–1.398) were not statistically significant. Weighted mean PHQ-9 scores differed across periods (p = 0.037). Sex-stratified analyses indicated greater temporal variation among men; however, the period-by-sex interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.069). Conclusions: Depressive symptoms showed modest worsening during the COVID-19 pandemic, but no statistically significant differences from 2018 were detected in 2022 or 2024. Although temporal variation appeared more pronounced among men, the period-by-sex interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.069), and the observed sex-specific differences should be interpreted with caution.

title: Neopterin and Interferon Gamma: Unveiling Their Prognostic Potential in COVID-19 with Diabetes Mellitus
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) comorbidity increases the mortality risk in COVID-19 patients. Neopterin and Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) are inflammatory markers involved in COVID-19 pathogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of neopterin and IFN-γ as predictors of mortality in COVID-19 patients with DM comorbidity. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using clinical data and serum samples from COVID-19 patients with DM hospitalized at Dr. Saiful Anwar General Hospital, Malang, Indonesia, between January 2022 and July 2022. Neopterin and IFN-γ levels were measured from serum samples. This study included 179 COVID-19 patients: 94 with DM comorbidity and 85 without. The non-survival group had significantly higher neopterin levels than the survival group (p=0.0074). title: Association of GBP2 and GBP5 expression with COVID-19 severity: a retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Host interferon responses are increasingly recognized as determinants of COVID-19 outcomes. Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are interferon-stimulated GTPases that restrict SARS-CoV-2 by interfering with furin-mediated processing of the viral spike protein; however, their relationship with clinical severity in patients has not been extensively studied. This study evaluated the association between GBP2 and GBP5 mRNA expression and clinical severity, with GBP5 as a comparator to test whether any association was gene-specific. Methods In this retrospective, cross-sectional study of archived whole-blood samples collected between November 2020 and February 2021, 150 adults with RT-PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection (37 mild, 32 moderate, 46 severe, 35 critical, classified per WHO/national criteria) and 50 SARS-CoV-2-negative controls were assayed for GBP2 and GBP5 mRNA by qRT-PCR, normalized to GAPDH (2 − ​ ΔΔCt method). Groups were compared using one-way ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc testing, with variance-robust and log2-scale sensitivity analyses; age, sex, and comorbidity were assessed by Spearman correlation and regression. Results GBP2 expression differed significantly across the five study groups (F = 288.27, p < 0.001), decreasing stepwise from mild (4.76-fold) to critical (0.60-fold) disease relative to controls. All ten pairwise comparisons were significant on the fold-change scale; on the log2 scale nine were significant with Tukey HSD (mild versus moderate, p = 0.205) and all ten with Games–Howell. GBP2 was inversely correlated with age ( r = − 0.57, p < 0.001), but clinical severity remained an independent predictor after adjustment ( p < 0.001 for each severity group). Sex and comorbidity were not independently associated, and age reached significance on the log2 scale only (conventional p = 0.045; HC3 p = 0.020). GBP5 differed far less across groups (F = 3.31, p = 0.012), with higher expression in critical patients than controls (1.35-fold vs. 1.00-fold) and no graded pattern. The crude association between low GBP2 and mortality was no longer detectable after adjusting for severity. Conclusions GBP2 expression was inversely associated with COVID-19 severity in this cohort, showing a strong graded relationship across severity strata, whereas GBP5 showed a much weaker and non-graded pattern. As only these two interferon-stimulated genes were measured, no inferences can be drawn about such genes in general. These findings describe an observed cross-sectional association, not a causal one, and warrant confirmation in prospective multicenter studies.

title: Hybrid immunity against SARS‐CoV‐2: Mechanisms, duration and global implications (Review)
abstract: Since the commencement of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID‐19) pandemic, understanding the nature and durability of immunity against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) has been central to public health strategies. Emerging evidence indicates that the combination of prior infection and vaccination, termed hybrid immunity, provides superior protection compared to infection‐ or vaccine‐induced immunity alone. The present review synthesizes currently available evidence on the mechanisms, durability and global implications of hybrid immunity, emphasizing its relevance for vaccination strategies, pandemic preparedness and health equity. The present review conducted a narrative synthesis of peer‐reviewed studies, systematic reviews and meta‐analyses published between 2020 and 2023, focusing on immunological mechanisms, epidemiological outcomes and policy implications of hybrid immunity. Mechanistically, it has been demonstrated that hybrid immunity elicits broader and more potent neutralizing antibodies, enhances memory B‐cell diversity and supports cross‐reactive T‐cell responses across variants of concern. Epidemiological evidence indicates that hybrid immunity confers the highest protection against infection, severe disease, hospitalization and mortality. Protection against reinfection wanes over time, particularly against immune‐evasive Omicron subvariants, although protection against severe outcomes remains durable for at least 6‐12 months. Booster vaccination further strengthens hybrid immunity. However, due to global disparities in vaccine access, individuals in high‐income regions disproportionately benefit from hybrid immunity, while populations in low‐ and middle‐income countries often rely on infection‐derived immunity alone. Hybrid immunity represents the most resilient form of protection against COVID‐19, combining the advantages of both natural and vaccine‐induced immunity. Its superior breadth and durability have critical implications for vaccination policies, particularly regarding booster prioritization and the development of variant‐proof vaccines. Ensuring equitable access to vaccines remains essential to maximize the protective benefits of hybrid immunity worldwide and to strengthen preparedness against future pandemics.

title: How Did COVID-19 Affect Urban Slums?
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, slum settlements received significant attention for their vulnerabilities. To mitigate risks of disease transmission and containment measures, experts called for community-driven solutions. But such approaches frequently neglect pre-existing structures of local leadership in these settlements. How did India’s slum leaders respond to the pandemic? What factors shape their success in helping residents? To answer these questions, we conducted a phone survey of 321 slum leaders in two north Indian cities during India’s stringent 2020 national lockdown. Our survey reveals striking continuities with pre-pandemic politics. Slum leaders persist in their problem-solving roles but tilt efforts toward pandemic response activities. Their effectiveness in doing so remains informed by the same factors that shape efficacy during “normal times,” notably their education and degree of embeddedness in party networks. Finally, pre-pandemic disparities in slum-level infrastructural development shape how much residents must depart from social distancing guidelines to secure essential services.

title: ‘Reaching and Teaching’: Understanding the Supercomplexity of Primary Teachers’ Work in an Area of High Social Deprivation During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the supercomplexity of primary teachers’ work in four northern English schools serving communities of high social deprivation during the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on a multiple case study, it shows how teachers’ safeguarding, pastoral and welfare roles expanded during the pandemic, requiring sustained family engagement amid overlapping social, economic and digital disadvantage and in response to shifting policy guidance. Framed by Barnett’s (2000a) notion of supercomplexity, the analysis identifies five overlapping themes: evolving definitions of vulnerability, mediating learning through homes, the emotional labour of care, rapid pedagogical and organisational adaptation and re-evaluation of educational aims beyond high-stakes accountability. While teachers demonstrated remarkable adaptability; developing hybrid provision, restructuring Early Years pedagogy and prioritising wellbeing, the moral weight of this labour remained largely unrecognised in policy. This chapter argues for teacher education and system design that centre adaptability, relational care and professional judgement, positioning teachers as co-constructors of educational meaning and essential agents in building resilience for future crises.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Widening the Gap? The Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Education for Students With Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in an English Special School
abstract: Abstract This study explores how COVID-19 restrictions impacted on the provision of education for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), from the point of view of four parents and the headteacher at a special school in the North of England. Thematic analysis of the data through Bronfenbrenner’s bioecological theory and Biesta’s domains of education contextualised the effects of school closures and policies on the people and systems that students engage with, as well as how they both interact with one another. While existing research has largely examined the impact of school closures and remote learning, this case study highlights the critical role of specialist provision in supporting families and maintaining student wellbeing. Findings reveal how the pandemic exacerbated existing inequalities and exposed the marginalisation of SEND learners within policy and practice. The study calls for a radical reframing of education through a social model of disability, advocating for inclusive environments and pedagogies. Although focused on only one special school, insights offer valuable lessons for mainstream and specialist settings alike. Wellbeing must be embedded in educational policy and practice to better support all learners moving forward.

title: Reimagining Secondary Schools as a Result of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract This chapter reports the findings of a qualitative study that set out to examine the experiences and priorities of English state-funded secondary schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. It considers how historical and contemporary policy eras have shaped the capacities of schools to respond to the challenges posed by the pandemic. Research took place within three schools with different types of governance: an inner-city new build that is part of a multi-academy trust, a Faith School and a Maintained School. It purposively recruited staff across a range of roles (senior leader, teaching and non-teaching support) to gain a complete picture of school approaches. Findings were as follows: going into the pandemic, each school identified challenges around staff recruitment, budgetary pressures, social deprivation and an increasing special educational needs and disabilities register. In the early days of school closure, schools utilised their existing pastoral structures to support children and families with varying degrees of success. As the pandemic evolved, all staff found themselves taking on new activities outside of their remit, which enabled a better understanding of the families and communities that they served. The authors conclude that in taking almost total responsibility for the welfare of pupils and their families during the pandemic, participating schools – whatever their governance – continued to resist neoliberal-driven educational policy that focuses purely on the classroom and excellent teaching. source_records.title: Reimagining Secondary Schools as a Result of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study
source_records.abstract: Abstract This chapter reports the findings of a qualitative study that set out to examine the experiences and priorities of English state-funded secondary schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. It considers how historical and contemporary policy eras have shaped the capacities of schools to respond to the challenges posed by the pandemic. Research took place within three schools with different types of governance: an inner-city new build that is part of a multi-academy trust, a Faith School and a Maintained School. It purposively recruited staff across a range of roles (senior leader, teaching and non-teaching support) to gain a complete picture of school approaches. Findings were as follows: going into the pandemic, each school identified challenges around staff recruitment, budgetary pressures, social deprivation and an increasing special educational needs and disabilities register. In the early days of school closure, schools utilised their existing pastoral structures to support children and families with varying degrees of success. As the pandemic evolved, all staff found themselves taking on new activities outside of their remit, which enabled a better understanding of the families and communities that they served. title: Epidemiología del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica: transmisión, carga viral salival y bioseguridad Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in dental practice: transmission, salivary viral load and biosafety
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la transmisión del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica, la carga viral salival y las medidas de bioseguridad. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la saliva y los aerosoles de los procedimientos odontológicos son vías relevantes de transmisión. La detección molecular del virus en saliva respalda su papel como reservorio y como muestra diagnóstica. Los colutorios antisépticos reducen el virus in vitro, pero su efecto clínico sobre la carga viral salival es limitado. El triaje, la protección personal, el control de aerosoles y la teleodontología fueron las medidas centrales. Conclusión: la bioseguridad debe mantenerse como norma permanente.

title: Efeitos da fisioterapia respiratória na reabilitação de pacientes pós-COVID-19 Effects of respiratory physiotherapy on the rehabilitation of post-COVID-19 patients Efectos de la fisioterapia respiratoria en la rehabilitación de pacientes pos-COVID-19
abstract: A COVID-19 pode deixar alterações respiratórias e funcionais persistentes, como dispneia, fadiga e fraqueza muscular, com impacto na qualidade de vida. Este estudo teve como objetivo geral verificar, por meio de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, os efeitos da fisioterapia respiratória na reabilitação de pacientes adultos com condições pós-COVID-19. A busca foi realizada nas bases PubMed, PEDro e SciELO, com estudos publicados entre 2020 e 2026, em português e inglês, e a análise incluiu apenas estudos que aplicaram um tratamento na fase pós-aguda da doença. Seis estudos compuseram a análise: três ensaios clínicos randomizados, um estudo quase-experimental com grupo controle, uma coorte prospectiva e um estudo quase-experimental sem grupo de comparação. As intervenções incluíram exercícios respiratórios, treinamento muscular inspiratório, treinamento aeróbico e de força, reabilitação pulmonar ambulatorial e telerreabilitação. Um estudo realizou dez sessões, enquanto os demais desenvolveram programas de seis a oito semanas. O aumento da distância percorrida no teste de caminhada de seis minutos foi o resultado mais frequente, e parte dos estudos registrou ganho de força muscular e redução da dispneia e da fadiga; em alguns ensaios, porém, o consumo máximo de oxigênio estimado, a qualidade de vida total e a maior parte dos parâmetros de função pulmonar não diferiram entre os grupos. Conclui-se que os estudos analisados apontam resultados positivos para determinadas intervenções, mas as diferenças entre eles impedem afirmar que exista um tratamento ideal único, e a reabilitação precisa ser individualizada.

title: Addressing loneliness and social isolation in at-risk groups during COVID-19 and beyond: a qualitative study in Switzerland
abstract: When Switzerland implemented public health measures against COVID-19, certain populations were particularly at risk of loneliness and social isolation, e.g., adolescents and young adults, older people, and migrants. This retrospective qualitative study aimed to explore stakeholders' experiences and perspectives on addressing loneliness and social isolation among these at-risk populations, with particular attention to the contextual, protective, and barrier factors shaping these experiences. It included 36 participants across six focus groups who provided social support to at-risk groups during COVID-19 in both the German- and French-speaking parts of Switzerland. The data were analysed using applied thematic analysis. Three overarching themes were developed: (1) communication and design of public health measures, (2) seizing and adapting existing resources, and (3) establishing a culture of social relationships. According to a socio-ecological framework for loneliness and social isolation during COVID-19, this study shows the interplay between the organisational and institutional levels to which participants belonged and different levels of the social system. Stakeholders perceived that their provision of social support was connected to individual initiatives, pre-existing interpersonal relationships and community support networks. Further, poor policy communication and a lack of acknowledgement of at-risk groups' social needs impacted the ability to address loneliness and social isolation. Stakeholders described opportunities to maintain social support within pandemic restrictions, noting that Swiss public health measures provided some room to meet social needs. Their accounts suggest that future preparedness should consider social relationships alongside infection prevention, pointing to specific approaches that require further safety evaluation and ethical assessment.

title: COVID-19 in the Village
abstract: Abstract This chapter examines why frontline health workers played such uneven roles in India’s rural COVID-19 response. Focusing on Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi workers, and Auxiliary Nurse Midwives, it conceptualizes frontline workers as hybrid actors positioned between local communities and the state. Drawing on interviews with workers and officials, a multistate survey, and grassroots video documentation, the chapter shows that pandemic responses rose or fell with hybrid actors’ social standing and institutional support. Many frontline health workers were doubly constrained—by weak backing from state agencies and by entrenched inequalities of caste, class, and gender—leaving them exposed, overburdened, and unable to deliver reliable care or welfare. Others were doubly empowered, combining bureaucratic authority with community trust, and so were able to mobilize resources, enforce public health measures, and extend assistance more equitably. The chapter argues that inequalities affecting frontline workers are a central but overlooked feature of crisis response and identifies the conditions under which local intermediaries might reduce, rather than reproduce, social exclusion.

title: Optimal control analysis of COVID-19 epidemic with fear effects using artificial neural networks
abstract: Mathematical modeling is effective in understanding the transmission dynamics of epidemics and designing control strategies. However, the behavioral responses of individuals during outbreaks are often overlooked. Epidemics spread mechanisms are influenced by fear, anxiety, and behavioral changes. Motivated by these challenges, a novel epidemic model incorporating fear dynamics is proposed. A theoretical analysis is conducted to analyze the model including basic reproduction number and stability analysis. Sensitivity analysis is conducted to identify the most influential epidemiological parameters affecting disease transmission. Furthermore, optimal control theory is employed to determine cost-effective intervention strategies that minimize the number of infected individuals while reducing implementation costs. The model simulation was carried through computing tool MATLAB. In addition, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) framework is employed using the PyTorch deep learning library for computational approximation and forecasting. The coefficient of determination \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$R^2$$\end{document} was found close to unity for all compartments with low values of other error metrics. This ensures the high predictive capability and approximation accuracy of the neural network framework. The simulation results reveal that combined vaccination, prevention, and quarantine strategies substantially reduce disease transmission. Sensitivity analysis reveals that transmission parameters positively influence disease spread, whereas vaccination, quarantine, and recovery rates contribute significantly to disease mitigation. The integration of the proposed hybrid mathematical–computational framework provides an efficient and reliable tool for epidemic prediction and public health decision-making in the control of infectious diseases.

title: Information disorder: their contributions to the infodemic phenomenon about Covid-19
abstract: Introduction: Informational disorder presents itself as a factual distortion of reality, causing disinformation due to the dynamics of accelerated flows of the infodemic. The Covid-19 pandemic was a tragic historical event used in the global escalation of the infodemic and its impact on information disorder. The political environment in Brazil, during the Covid-19 pandemic, was marked by rhetoric and speeches that encouraged the production and dissemination of misleading content. Objective: to establish the interrelation between the infodemic, especially from disinformation, and the behaviors adopted to face the disease, or the absence thereof, taking as corpus the statements about Covid-19 made by the then Brazilian president, Jair Messias Bolsonaro. Methodology: qualitative, exploratory and descriptive research based on bibliographic and documentary procedures, covering 2020 and 2021, in which the statements were categorized from the literature on information disorder and analyzed through Foucauldian-inspired Discourse Analysis. Results: the statements analyzed center on downplaying the severity of the disease, promoting treatment of unproven efficacy, discrediting the press, science and containment measures, and shifting responsibility, in a context in which the agency Aos Fatos recorded a daily average of 6.9 false pieces of information in 2021. Conclusions: information disorder articulated from the highest level of the Executive operated as a political practice and amplified the risks of the infodemic, although the data gathered do not allow a direct causal relationship with infection and mortality rates to be established.

title: Prevalência de fraturas de fêmur atendidas pelo SUS: uma análise de antes e durante Pandemia de SARS CoV-2
abstract: The femur is a long bone and is considered the largest bone in the human body. Femoral fractures are regarded as severe and represent a significant public health challenge due to the prolonged recovery period, generating substantial financial impacts on the healthcare system and being associated with higher mortality rates. This study aimed to analyze the prevalence of femoral fractures treated by the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS) in Brazil, before and during the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. This is a descriptive study using data from the DataSUS platform over a five-year retrospective period, from 2019 to 2023. Prevalence data by Brazilian states, sex, and age of patients were analyzed, as well as data related to the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. The groups most affected by femoral fractures were individuals aged over 80 years, women, and White individuals. The number of deaths increased with advancing age. The Southeast Region presented the highest number of hospitalizations and healthcare expenditures, while the North Region showed the lowest number of hospitalizations and healthcare expenditures during the evaluated period. From 2019 to 2022, a progressive increase in hospitalizations was observed, and in 2020 and 2021 there was a reduction in the average length of hospital stay. This study provided a detailed analysis of the impacts of the pandemic on hospitalizations due to femoral fractures within the SUS, making it possible to accurately identify changes in the epidemiological pattern of these fractures during the pandemic period.

title: The Uptake of and Access to Expanded Program for Immunization Services Among Children Aged 0 to 12 Months During the COVID-19 Pandemic in Free State Province, South Africa: A Mixed Study.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted essential health services, including routine childhood immunization. This study assessed immunization uptake and access among children aged 0-12 months and explored the effects of COVID-19 on Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) service delivery in the Free State Province, South Africa. Methods A mixed-methods exploratory study was conducted. Quantitative data were obtained from the District Health Information System (DHIS) and used to compare EPI uptake during the 12 months before and 12 months after the onset of COVID-19. Data were analyzed using Wilcoxon rank-sum and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Qualitative data were collected through unstructured interviews with provincial and district EPI and Maternal and Child Health managers, and were analyzed thematically using the World Health Organization health systems building blocks framework. Results Although immunization uptake among children under 1 year declined following the onset of COVID-19, the reductions were not statistically significant ( p > 0.05). Qualitative findings indicated that the pandemic increased pressure on the health system, adversely affecting access to and delivery of primary healthcare services, including immunization. Key challenges included staff shortages, inadequate funding, weak emergency preparedness, limitations in health information systems, and shortcomings in leadership and governance. Participants reported that these health system weaknesses existed before the pandemic but were intensified during the COVID-19 period. Conclusion Routine childhood immunization services in the Free State Province were largely maintained during the COVID-19 pandemic despite increased pressure on the health system. While the pandemic exposed and exacerbated existing health system weaknesses, it also demonstrated the resilience of immunization services. Strengthening health system preparedness, workforce capacity, information systems, and governance will be essential for sustaining immunization services during future emergencies.

Conclusion Routine childhood immunization services in the Free State Province were largely maintained during the COVID-19 pandemic despite increased pressure on the health system. While the pandemic exposed and exacerbated existing health system weaknesses, it also demonstrated the resilience of immunization services. Strengthening health system preparedness, workforce capacity, information systems, and governance will be essential for sustaining immunization services during future emergencies.

title: Riesgos laborales en profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19: revisión sistemática Occupational risks among oral health professionals during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre los riesgos laborales de los profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19 y las medidas propuestas para controlarlos. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, ensayos clínicos, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: el riesgo biológico por aerosoles, gotas y contacto estrecho fue el principal riesgo descrito, seguido de las exposiciones a sangre y punzocortantes y del riesgo psicosocial, con agotamiento profesional y percepción elevada de riesgo. Las medidas incluyeron triaje, equipos de protección, control de aerosoles y colutorios previos al procedimiento. Conclusión: la pandemia aumentó y diversificó los riesgos laborales en odontología, por lo que se requieren protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y de protección de la salud mental.

title: COVID-19 in the States
abstract: Abstract This chapter analyzes how the COVID-19 pandemic tested democratic capabilities at the subnational level. It argues that the crisis exposed not only core dimensions of state capacity but also the relational forms of power needed to secure public cooperation in highly unequal societies. It shows that national-level analyses overlook these dynamics by focusing narrowly on formal democracy and fixed bureaucratic resources, whereas the subnational level better captures how state agencies interact with civil society to coordinate high-touch health and welfare responses. It explains why state governments in India became the central actors during the pandemic and how political competition, state–society relations, and local institutions shaped state performance in health and welfare responses. These factors were key in mobilizing resources, inducing compliance, and mitigating inequalities. In doing so, the chapter demonstrates that subnational democratic capabilities are critical both for crisis response and for strengthening equitable state action more broadly.

title: FATORES DE RISCO À SAÚDE MENTAL NUMA COORTE DE IDOSOS DE CLASSE MÉDIA ALTA NO PÓS PANDEMIA DA COVID-19 MENTAL HEALTH RISK FACTORS IN A COHORT OF UPPER-MIDDLE-CLASS OLDER ADULTS IN THE POST-COVID-19 PANDEMIC PERIOD FACTORES DE RIESGO PARA LA SALUD MENTAL EN UNA COHORTE DE ADULTOS MAYORES DE CLASE MEDIA ALTA EN LA POSPANDEMIA DE LA COVID-19
abstract: Objetivo: Investigar os impactos da COVID-19 na saúde mental de idosos participantes de uma coorte populacional de classe média-alta em São Paulo, Brasil. Método: Estudo transversal descritivo realizado entre fevereiro e agosto de 2023 com 42 idosos (≥60 anos) da coorte Epidoso de São Paulo. Os dados foram coletados através de entrevista presencial com questionário estruturado contendo variáveis sociodemográficas, experiências relacionadas à COVID-19 (isolamento social, contágio, luto), sintomas de ansiedade e depressão, bem como acesso a acompanhamento médico e psicológico. A análise estatística utilizou medidas de frequência absoluta e relativa. Resultados: A amostra foi composta predominantemente por mulheres (73,8%), com média etária de 70 a 79 anos. Durante a pandemia, 90,4% relataram ansiedade e 76,2% tristeza e/ou depressão (sendo 40,5% tristeza, 21,4% depressão e 14,3% ambas), porém apenas 26,2% buscaram acompanhamento psicológico. Quanto ao isolamento social, 80,9% permaneceram isolados, sendo 38,5% por 2 anos e 42,9% vivenciaram luto de familiar. O acompanhamento médico foi mantido em 69,1% dos casos. Conclusão: A pandemia impactou significativamente a saúde mental dos idosos, evidenciando alta prevalência de ansiedade (90,4%) e de tristeza e/ou depressão (76,2%), contrastada com baixa busca por acompanhamento psicológico (26,2%), reforçando a tese de que o isolamento provocou marcante fragilidade emocional, e que as variáveis renda e escolaridade elevadas não anulam os riscos psíquicos da pandemia. Reforça-se a relevância das redes de apoio e da ampliação da assistência psicológica e de políticas públicas que fortaleçam o acesso a serviços de saúde mental para idosos, especialmente em contextos de emergências sanitárias.

title: Intellectual capital efficiency and firm performance: A bibliometric analysis across COVID 19 periods
abstract: This study maps research relevant to intellectual capital efficiency (ICE) and firm performance using 846 Scopus-indexed journal publications from 2015 to 2025.Publication and citation analysis, author and institutional productivity rankings, and a pooled keyword co-occurrence map describe the literature.Three operational periods are distinguished: pre-COVID-19 (2015 to 2019), COVID-19 onset (2020), and post-COVID-19 (2021 to 2025), with the final label referring to a publication window rather than the end of the pandemic.The periods contain 247, 98, and 501 publications, respectively; annual output increased from 36 in 2015 to 110 in 2025.The corpus accumulated 26,877 citations at extraction.Xu Jian recorded the highest reported author output, while Qingdao Agricultural University recorded the highest reported institutional output.Intellectual capital, knowledge management, and financial performance were prominent keywords.Highly cited studies illustrate financial, innovation, and organizational performance perspectives, including research on SME hotels.These patterns identify connections between efficiency measurement and knowledge deployment, but do not establish a causal effect of COVID-19 or validate ICE as a dynamic capability.The study develops a research agenda for contextual comparisons, longitudinal analysis, and sustainability measurement while acknowledging database, citation-age and network-reproducibility limitations.

title: L’IMAGINAIRE DE LA MANIPULATION DÉVOILÉ EN DEUX CRÉATIONS COMIQUES SOUS LA PANDÉMIE DE COVID-19
abstract: The subtle unveiling of the imaginary of manipulation through comic texts can contribute to a better understanding of mechanisms of social protection and mitigation in times of crisis. This article examines representations of the COVID-19 pandemic through two distinct literary works that share a common feature: the presence and creative use of pandemic-related vocabulary. The analysis focuses on Lucian Dan Teodorovici’s teenage novella “Silvestru și Marele Dictator” (2020) [Silvester and the Big Dictator] and Olivier Auroy’s “Dicorona” (2020), a “dictionnaire de mots-valises” based on portmanteau words. In Teodorovici’s novella, the pre-existing vocabulary associated with the pandemic is creatively transformed, notably through the invention of terms such as “VIM-20”, which designates the deadly virus. The resulting fictional world reconfigures the relationship between humans, animals, and the virus: while the pandemic was associated in public discourse with zoonotic transmission involving animals such as bats or pangolins, Silvestru, an intelligent tomcat belonging to a rural family living near a large city, assumes the role of savior. In “Dicorona”, Auroy similarly adopts a playful linguistic strategy, constructing portmanteau words through the combination of lexical elements derived either from rumors and fake news or from associative connections between ordinary dictionary words. Each newly coined term is accompanied by a brief explanatory narrative, contributing to a humorous reinterpretation of pandemic-related discourse. The comparative analysis draws on theoretical perspectives concerning the social imaginary, particularly the approaches developed by Cornelius Castoriadis (2005) and Dan-Gabriel Sîmbotin (2016), as well as Henri Bergson’s (1900) theory of the comic. By examining linguistic invention, humor, and fictionalization, the article argues that comic representations of the pandemic can expose and critically reconfigure the mechanisms through which fear, manipulation, and misinformation operate within the social imaginary

title: Disparities in COVID-19 challenges among people with a history of injection drug use in the RADx-UP initiative
abstract: Structural vulnerability underlies significant inequities in access to resources and outcomes in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. In particular, people who inject drugs (PWID) or people with a history of injection drug use (PWHID) face health and social challenges such as unstable housing, limited healthcare access, and increased prevalence of comorbidities, which are associated with increased risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes. Despite these vulnerabilities, there is limited research on the factors underlying COVID-19-related challenges and the specific challenges PWID/PWHID face. The RADx Underserved Populations (RADx-UP) initiative aims to address COVID-19-related disparities by improving testing in underserved populations. RADx-UP sites reported standardized data across diverse geographic, racial, and socioeconomic groups, with a particular focus on vulnerable communities such as racial minorities, PWID/PWHID, people with disabilities, and those with limited access to healthcare. Data examined in this study includes 24,808 participants from 31 RADx-UP projects across the United States (US). A total of 952 participants identified as people with a history of injection drug use by selecting “intravenous drug use” from a list of health conditions. The primary outcome was challenges experienced during COVID-19 in six domains: healthcare access, housing, food security, water access, medication access, and transportation. Participants ranked factors as being “no challenge,” a “minor challenge,” or a “major challenge.” GEE logistic regression models were used to assess the association between injection drug use and COVID-19 challenges. PWHID were significantly more likely to experience at least one COVID-19-related challenge compared to those without a history of injecting drugs (AOR = 2.00 [95% CI 1.36–2.94]). PWHID had higher prevalence of unstable housing, food insecurity, and lack of access to healthcare. Structural vulnerabilities such as insufficient access to personal protective equipment (PPE) and chronic health conditions were also associated with elevated risk of severe outcomes. Equitable public health interventions, including efforts to prioritize resource distribution to PWID/PWHID and other marginalized populations, are critical to prevent exacerbation of inequities in the context of crises.

title: Sexual and reproductive disparities by formal and informal urban residence in Kinshasa before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic threatened progress in sexual and reproductive health (SRH) across sub-Saharan Africa, with urban communities in informal settlements (slum neighborhoods) particularly at risk. In Kinshasa, disruptions to family planning and contraceptive services were noted at the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic but rebounded after lockdown restrictions were eased. However, there has been limited research on differential post-pandemic trends in SRH outcomes between slum and non-slum residents. This study uses longitudinal data from four rounds of the Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) survey in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to examine how SRH outcomes shifted across slum and non-slum neighborhoods from 2019 to 2024. We utilized mixed-effects logistic regression models to examine the influence of slum vs. non-slum neighborhood status on the odds of contraceptive and pregnancy outcomes over time. Prior to the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, seven in ten women (70.4%) were living in a slum neighborhood. Among all women, the odds of reporting one’s current or last pregnancy being unintended increased significantly from 2019/2020 to 2021/2022 (OR = 3.8) and 2024 (OR = 11.6), highlighting that pregnancies occurring during and after the pandemic were more likely to be unintended. We found no evidence of diverging trends in SRH outcomes by slum status over time. However, slum residence was significantly associated with higher need for contraception, lower contraceptive use among those in need, greater provider-dependent method use, and unintended pregnancy, before, during and after the pandemic. COVID-19 did not significantly widen reproductive health disparities between slum and non-slum residents in Kinshasa, but the analysis shows sustained inequities in contraceptive need, contraceptive coverage, and unintended pregnancy, before, during and after the pandemic. Addressing these disparities, particularly during times of budget cuts to family planning and reproductive health, requires targeted investments in counseling and contraceptive access. The COVID-19 pandemic led to disruptions in health services that threatened the ability of women in Sub-Saharan Africa to seek sexual and reproductive healthcare, such as family planning services. Those who live in informal settlements (slum neighborhoods) may be particularly harmed by disruptions related to COVID-19. In this study, we used data from the Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) Program in Kinshasa, DRC to examine changes over time in measures of reproductive health among women living in formal non-slum and slum communities. Before the pandemic, women in slum communities were less likely to be using family planning when trying to avoid pregnancy and more likely to report their pregnancies as unintended. The need for family planning to avoid pregnancy and the reporting of unintended pregnancies during and in the year after the pandemic increased for all women, with no differential trends between slum and non-slum dwellers. As a result, inequities women in slum communities faced before the pandemic​ persisted during and after the pandemic. As such, the research highlights ongoing challenges in ensuring equal access to family planning and reproductive health services in Kinshasa.

The need for family planning to avoid pregnancy and the reporting of unintended pregnancies during and in the year after the pandemic increased for all women, with no differential trends between slum and non-slum dwellers. As a result, inequities women in slum communities faced before the pandemic​ persisted during and after the pandemic. As such, the research highlights ongoing challenges in ensuring equal access to family planning and reproductive health services in Kinshasa.

title: Human-Centric Social Sensing for IoT-Enabled COVID-19 Situational Awareness: DistilBERT-Based Emergency Signal Discovery
abstract: Internet of things (IoT)-enabled public health systems need timely indicators from both device data and human-generated streams. Social media can supply upstream observations during emergencies, but noisy language complicates their validation against official surveillance. We construct daily emergency signals from Weibo posts and test whether they add leading information about official COVID-19 case counts. The analysis covers 39.6 million COVID-19-related posts in Weibo-COV 2.0 from January to April 2020. Distilled bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (DistilBERT), fine-tuned with keyword pseudo-labels, performs binary emergency screening and classifies symptom-, resource-, and policy-related subtypes. Postlevel metrics report agreement with keyword-derived pseudo-labels, not accuracy against independent human annotations; no such benchmark was available. Daily indicators are extrapolated from stratified samples of 500 posts. Their finite-sample uncertainty is reported, and alternative sample sizes represent theoretical precision bounds rather than empirical downstream stability. Validation uses stationarity tests, VAR lag selection, BH-corrected Granger predictability tests, HC1-robust OLS regressions, Johansen rank diagnostics, and a rank-one VECM sensitivity fit. A complete rerun with the stated settings reproduced all empirical outputs, while formula-derived quantities and theoretical bounds were recomputed. Binary and multiclass weighted $F1$ -scores on pseudo-labeled held-out data are 0.927 and 0.880, respectively. At a one-day lag, emergency signals improve the statistical explanation of later cases ( $F=24.68$ , adjusted $p\lt 0.001$ ); symptom signals are strongest ( $F=26.87$ ). The seven-day coefficient is 1.623 ( $p\lt 0.001$ ), and subtype decomposition raises $R^{2}$ from 0.636 to 0.665. Because the Johansen trace test rejects both rank restrictions, $\alpha =-0.2965$ (29.6%/day) remains a descriptive VECM sensitivity estimate. A keyword baseline attains higher aggregate fit ( $R^{2}=0.691$ ), so the evidence does not establish transformer dominance. DistilBERT instead contributes semantic subtype discovery with less manual rule design. The resulting IoT contribution is an interoperable analytics layer for aggregate alerts, not a new sensing device, protocol, or edge architecture.

title: Restriction of SARS-CoV-2 infectivity by SERINC5 and SERINC3, and rescue by viral countermeasure proteins
abstract: Serine Incorporator (SERINC) proteins are cellular transmembrane proteins that have various functions, such as membrane lipid biosynthesis, tumour progression and nervous system function. SERINC5 and, to a lesser extent, SERINC3 have been shown to act as viral restriction factors. Host SERINCs are taken up into virus particles during assembly and restrict subsequent infection of target cells by inhibiting viral fusion. The HIV-1 antagonist Nef inhibits SERINC5 by binding directly to SERINC5 and excluding it from HIV-1 particles via endocytosis. Other SERINC5 antagonists include GlycoGag from Murine Leukaemia Virus, S2 from Equine Infectious Anaemia Virus and, recently discovered, ORF7a from SARS-CoV-2. This study aims to confirm the status of ORF7a as a SERINC antagonist using a lentiviral pseudotype model. It was investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 lentiviral pseudotypes co-transfected with SERINC5 and SERINC3 had restricted infectivity, and whether infectivity could be rescued using ORF7a and glygoGag viral countermeasures. In addition to laboratory approaches, sequence alignments and positive selection analysis were conducted on coronavirus ORF7a to understand the evolutionary pressures on ORF7a. This study shows that SERINC5 does not restrict the infectivity of SARS-CoV-2 lentiviral pseudotypes, and we are therefore unable to conclude whether ORF7a can rescue SARS-CoV-2 infectivity. We suggest that cellular and lentiviral pseudotype variation has an impact on the reproducibility of experiments, and that optimising the production of lentiviral pseudotypes for both research and clinical applications is a key area for further investigation. Bioinformatic analysis of ORF7a provides insight into the possible roles of ORF7a in supporting SARS-CoV-2 infection by subverting host immunity, potentially playing a role in the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Metabolic Severity and Early Disease Course in Children with Newly Diagnosed Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus According to Prior SARS-CoV-2 Infection Status: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: The impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the metabolic presentation and early course of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) in children remains incompletely understood. Although an increased frequency of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) has been reported during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, it is unclear whether this reflects a direct pathogenic role of the virus or indirect effects related to healthcare access and delayed presentation. Methods: This retrospective study included children with newly diagnosed T1DM evaluated between 2021 and 2025 at a single tertiary pediatric center. Two cohorts were compared: patients with PCR-documented and serologically confirmed prior SARS-CoV-2 infection (nucleocapsid antibody-based assay) and those without. DKA severity, acid-base parameters, lipid profile, autoimmune markers, thyroid function, and metabolic indices were compared at diagnosis. HbA1c, insulin dose, and C-peptide were assessed at diagnosis and 12-month follow-up. Multivariable regression, interaction testing, sensitivity, and subgroup analyses were performed. Results: Of 134 children, 58 had confirmed prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. Median HbA1c at diagnosis was 11.02% in the COVID group versus 11.77% in the non-COVID group (p = 0.057). Insulin requirements were similar (p = 0.87). Severe DKA occurred in 39.7% versus 42.1% (p = 0.90). C-peptide levels at diagnosis and 12 months did not differ between groups. Prior SARS-CoV-2 infection was not significantly associated with HbA1c at diagnosis (β = −0.65% HbA1c, 95% CI −1.33 to 0.03; p = 0.061; additionally adjusted for DKA grade, β = −0.68%, p = 0.079). HbA1c at 12 months was similar between groups (p = 0.85); in multivariable analysis adjusted for baseline HbA1c, age, and sex, prior infection was not significantly associated with HbA1c at follow-up (adjusted β = 0.39%, 95% CI −0.06 to 0.84; p = 0.092). Conclusions: No statistically significant association was found between confirmed prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and metabolic severity at diagnosis or glycemic outcomes during the first year, although the HbA1c comparison approached significance and the sample size limited power to detect differences smaller than approximately 1.04% HbA1c. The findings do not exclude a modest effect of prior infection, and larger prospective studies are warranted.

title: Histopathology of Appendiceal Specimens From Patients With Appendicitis and Concomitant COVID-19
abstract: Background: COVID-19 is a disease caused by SARS-CoV-2, which uses angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptors to infect cells.Research suggests that gastrointestinal (GI) manifestations of COVID-19 indicate the presence of ACE2 receptors throughout the GI system, including the appendix, and has identified SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid in appendiceal specimens.Our study aimed to elucidate the relationship between appendicitis and COVID-19 through a histopathological analysis of appendixes from patients who underwent appendectomy with coexisting positive polymerase chain reaction (C+) results.We hypothesized that a strong presence of SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid would be present in appendiceal samples of C+ patients.Methods: We analyzed 34 appendiceal specimens from patients undergoing appendectomies from March 2020 to April 2022.Twenty-five specimens were from C+ patients, and nine were from C-patients; 5-μm sections of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue were subjected to C4d immunohistochemistry staining.SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid was measured using RNAscope with a probe (V-nCoV2019-S; Advanced Cell Diagnostics, Newark, CA) against COVID-19, also on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue.Results: Of the 25 C+ appendiceal specimens, three (two focally, one patchy) contained SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid (3 C+ vs. 0 C-; p = 0.553).C4d staining was variable and had no difference in intensity (p = 0.553) or quantity (p = 0.188) between COVID-19 status.There was no difference in appendiceal wall thickness between C+ and C-patients (2.28 mm C+ vs. 2.11 mm C-; p = 0.656).Conclusion: We found no differences in the presence of SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid, C4d staining, or wall thickness between C+ and C-specimens.These findings indicate minimal histopathological differences between appendixes from C+ and C-patients, suggesting that SARS-CoV-2 was not heavily involved in the pathogenesis of appendicitis.

media_mentions.content_title: Histopathology of Appendiceal Specimens From Patients With Appendicitis and Concomitant COVID-19
media_mentions.content: Abstract Background: COVID-19 is a disease caused by SARS-CoV-2, which uses angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptors to infect cells. Research suggests that gastrointestinal (GI) manifestations of COVID-19 indicate the presence of ACE2 receptors throughout the GI system, including the appendix, and has identified SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid in appendiceal specimens. Our study aimed to elucidate the relationship between appendicitis and COVID-19 through a histopathological analysis of appendixes from patients who underwent appendectomy with coexisting positive polymerase chain reaction (C+) results. We hypothesized that a strong presence of SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid would be present in appendiceal samples of C+ patients. Methods: We analyzed 34 appendiceal specimens from patients undergoing appendectomies from March 2020 to April 2022. Twenty-five specimens were from C+ patients, and nine were from C- patients; 5-μm sections of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue were subjected to C4d immunohistochemistry staining. SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid was measured using RNAscope with a probe (V-nCoV2019-S; Advanced Cell Diagnostics, Newark, CA) against COVID-19, also on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue. Results: Of the 25 C+ appendiceal specimens, three (two focally, one patchy) contained SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid (3 C+ vs. 0 C-; p = 0.553). C4d staining was variable and had no difference in intensity (p = 0.553) or quantity (p = 0.188) between COVID-19 status. There was no difference in appendiceal wall thickness between C+ and C- patients (2.28 mm C+ vs. 2.11 mm C-; p = 0.656). Conclusion: We found no differences in the presence of SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid, C4d staining, or wall thickness between C+ and C- specimens. These findings indicate minimal histopathological differences between appendixes from C+ and C- patients, suggesting that SARS-CoV-2 was not heavily involved in the pathogenesis of appendicitis. Introduction COVID-19 is a respiratory disease caused by SARS-CoV-2. For invasion of respiratory epithelial cells, SARS-CoV-2 virions utilize a spike protein that binds to the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor, which allows for subsequent internalization of the virus and propagation of viral infection [1]. While the pathogenesis of SARS-CoV-2 in respiratory tissue has been extensively researched, there is evidence that SARS-CoV-2 can invade gastrointestinal (GI) tissue [2]. The presence of ACE2 receptors throughout the GI tract suggests that tissue invasion in the GI tract is similar to that of respiratory tissue. Its ability to invade GI tissue provides a possible explanation for some of the GI manifestations of COVID-19 [3]. There have been several case studies that suggest appendicitis or an appendicitis-like syndrome is a presentation of COVID-19 [4-8]. A case study from March 2020 demonstrated SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid within the appendix of a patient who was COVID-19-positive at the time of their appendectomy, and the authors suggested that the appendicitis in that case was caused by COVID-19 [9]. Another study that assessed nine pediatric appendiceal samples taken from COVID-19-positive patients identified no SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid in their samples [10]. The pathogenesis of appendicitis is not straightforward for as common a condition as appendicitis is. A 2026 study by Gelevski et al. posits that appendicitis is a disease impacted by etiological substrate, pathological severity, and patient systemic response [11]. Understanding this hybrid severity-etiology framework is key to reconciling inconsistencies observed from patient to patient, refining risk stratification strategies, and enabling more granular correlation between appendicitis and other diseases. In the present study, we sought to elucidate a possible relationship between appendicitis and COVID-19. To do so, we performed a histopathological analysis of appendiceal specimens taken from patients diagnosed with acute appendicitis who subsequently underwent appendectomy. We hypothesized that there would be a strong presence of SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid in appendiceal tissue samples taken from those who were COVID-19-positive within 30 days of admission, supporting our hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 plays a direct role in the pathogenesis of appendicitis in the cases studied. Materials & Methods After Institutional Review Board approval, we compared appendiceal samples from patients aged 5 years or older who tested positive for COVID-19 by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with those who tested negative. These COVID-19-negative samples served as our control group. Thirty-four appendiceal specimens from patients admitted with an acute appendicitis diagnosis from March 2020 to April 2022 at our community hospital underwent histopathological analysis. Three specimens were from patients with perforated appendicitis. These patients were identified from a previous study by Harshaw et al., which examined the severity of appendicitis before and during the COVID-19 pandemic [12]. Specimens were identified from the study’s COVID-19-era, defined as patients presenting at our institution from March 11, 2020, to April 1, 2022. Twenty-five of these appendiceal specimens were from COVID-19-positive patients (defined as PCR positivity within 14 days of admission), and nine appendiceal specimens were randomly selected from COVID-19-negative patients as controls. There were 841 COVID-19-negative patients during the COVID-19-era identified by Harshaw et al. Every 84th negative patient was considered a negative control for this study. Random selection was used to obtain a diverse sample of controls in an effort to control for confounding variables. Because the COVID-19-positive patient specimens were identified from the COVID-19-positive patients in Harshaw et al., they were a sample of convenience. We used the COVID-19 (V-nCoV2019-S) probe (ACD 848568; Advanced Cell Diagnostics, Newark, CA) to detect SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid. RNAscope on 5-μm sections of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue was performed using a probe against COVID-19, along with positive (PPIB Leica RS7755) and negative (Dapb Leica RS7756) control probes for each case. Staining was done on a Leica Bond-IIITM instrument (Leica Biosystems Melbourne Pty Ltd., Australia) using the Bond RNAscope. For detection, a Brown System (Leica Microsystems DS9790; Leica Biosystems Melbourne Pty Ltd) was used. Heat-induced epitope retrieval was done for 20 minutes with ER2 solution (Leica Microsystems AR9640). All the experiments were done at room temperature. The slides were washed three times between each step with bond wash buffer or water. Each sample was subjected to complement 4d (C4d) immunohistochemistry staining, and appendiceal wall thickness was measured. Samples were then reviewed by two different pathologists, both of whom were blinded to the COVID-19 PCR status of each of the samples. Characteristics and demographics of COVID-19-positive and COVID-19-negative samples were then described by study personnel. We assessed the normality of continuous variables via a Shapiro-Wilk test. We then performed independent-samples t-tests for continuous variables and reported the data as mean (standard deviation; 95% confidence interval). For categorical variables, we conducted Fisher’s exact tests because of our limited sample size. These data were reported as n (percent of population). While we conducted these analyses to examine a potential relationship between COVID-19 and appendicitis, the descriptive statistics became more informative due to the small sample size. Analyses were performed in Stata/IC 16.0 (College Station, TX, USA). A p value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. We followed the STrengthening the Reporting of OBservational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines in structuring this article [13]. Results Histopathological analysis of these specimens showed no significant differences in appendiceal wall thickness, SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid staining, or C4d staining characteristics between appendiceal samples from COVID-19-positive and COVID-19-negative patients. Results are shown in Table 1. Figures 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B are histopathological images from one COVID-19-positive patient. C4d intensity refers to the staining density of the signal. C4d quantity refers to the distribution of the signal throughout the specimen. C4d percentage refers to the approximate percentage of the sample that contains the stain. Only three out of 25 COVID-19-positive samples contained SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid. For the COVID-19-positive group, C4d intensity was mostly strong, the quantity was mostly patchy, and the C4d percentage was mostly in the 21%-60% range. For the COVID-19-negative group, C4d intensity was always strong, mostly diffuse, and mostly in the 61%-100% range. Figures 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B are of the same specimen chosen to show the contrast between C4d and RNAscope staining. This specimen showed the most robust evidence of staining. The arrows in Figures 1B, 2B indicate areas of the appendiceal specimen that picked up the most staining in the vessels and epithelial cells. Discussion The histopathologic analysis of COVID-19-positive and COVID-19-negative appendiceal specimens yielded no significant differences in appendiceal wall thickness, SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid in appendiceal tissue, or C4d staining. This is consistent with the evidence found in the study by Jiang et al., in which all nine of their pediatric appendiceal specimens taken from COVID-19-positive patients displayed no SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid. This refutes our hypothesis and the proposed mechanism of SARS-CoV-2 infection playing a direct role in the appendicitis cases we studied. Alternative explanations for the relationship between COVID-19 and appendicitis exist. These primarily point toward the general inflammatory state generated by COVID-19 as providing the opportunity for appendicitis to occur, but not necessarily as a causative agent [14]. Our motivation to study appendiceal specimens and COVID-19 came after a case study that was done at our institution regarding the role of SARS-CoV-2 in second-trimester patients who experienced intrauterine fetal demise. Briguglio found that there was a strong concentration of C4d complement staining in the syncytiotrophoblastic layer of the placental villi in their samples. The complement activation was associated with histopathologic findings of extensive fibrin deposition and villous infarction, suggesting a role of immune-mediated vascular injury in adverse fetal outcomes. They suggested that because previous research has demonstrated that pregnant women have higher levels of ACE2 receptors in the placenta, this provides the entry point for SARS-CoV-2 [15]. This case study highlights the vascular insult SARS-CoV-2 can inflict on ACE2-abundant tissues. This case study, in conjunction with the previously aforementioned studies that investigated the relationship between COVID-19 and the appendix, provided much of the inspiration for our study. Similar vascular pathology has been studied in the GI tract, with an association between ischemic colitis and COVID-19. In a case study performed by Uhlenhopp et al., two patients developed left-sided colitis after being diagnosed with COVID-19. Both imaging and endoscopy confirmed nonocclusive ischemia and thrombotic events, suggesting that the underlying pathophysiology was secondary to the hypercoagulable state induced by the viral infection [16]. In this study, we had no significant presence of viral nucleic acid (only three of 25 specimens) in appendiceal tissue, and C4d staining showed no significant difference between COVID-19-positive and COVID-19-negative patients. These results reinforce the idea that SARS-CoV-2 may not directly affect GI tissue in all cases but may exacerbate underlying vulnerabilities in vascular integrity through complement activation and endothelial injury. This aligns with the broader observation that COVID-19 is a multisystem inflammatory disease, which is capable of triggering pathology through immune-mediated responses rather than direct virus-induced cell damage. Limitations of our study include our relatively small sample size and small control group. Including more samples from multiple centers could grant a more powered analysis through which more definitive and generalizable findings could be drawn. Also, the samples were taken from March 2020 to April 2022. This time frame contained numerous variants of SARS-CoV-2 with different levels of virulence, creating the possibility for variable effects on the GI tract. While C4d staining was used to identify the degree of host-mediated damage caused by the SARS-CoV-2 infection, there are also limitations to using the C4d stain. It is a recognized marker for complement activation and has diagnostic utility in transplant pathology in identifying antibody-mediated rejection, but it is not the most specific tool for evaluating COVID-19. C4d staining has limitations as a biomarker due to its lack of specificity, as accumulation of the C4d protein can occur in a wide range of conditions. The presence of C4d indicates that the complement pathway has been activated but does not clarify the underlying cause or distinguish between different inflammatory triggers [17]. Conclusions In this exploratory and descriptive analysis, histopathological differences between appendiceal specimens from COVID-19-positive and COVID-19-negative patients with acute appendicitis were minimal, suggesting that direct SARS-CoV-2 infection of appendix specimen may not be heavily involved with the pathogenesis of appendicitis in the patients studied. Because of the small sample size in this study, significant associations were not established; however, this does not necessarily indicate an absence of biological relevance, especially when considering descriptive findings. From a clinical standpoint, these results should be considered with caution, and more studies should be done to further investigate this work. title: Personal Courage Moderates the Association between Neuroticism and Anxiety and Depression Symptom Trajectories from Pre-Covid-19 to Covid-19
abstract: More research is needed on the mental health effects of the coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) on the average individual. In addition, little is known about what factors contribute to effects, specifically anxiety and depression symptoms. Prior studies conducted by Zinbarg et al. (2023) and Reynolds et al. (in preparation) found that the factors of personal courage and neuroticism significantly and predicted anxiety and depression symptoms during the transition period from pre-COVID-19 to the COVID-19 pandemic when tested in isolation from each other. Unexpectedly, neuroticism predicted smaller increases in transdiagnostic symptom factors Anhedonia Apprehension and General Distress. Conversely, neuroticism predicted larger increases in the Fears factor. Personal courage, measured as persistence despite fear, predicted smaller increases in General Distress and Fears. Unexpectedly, personal courage predicted larger increases in the Anhedonia Apprehension factor. Post-hoc explanations suggest neuroticism may have operated through social avoidance prior to the pandemic, leaving individuals higher on neuroticism with less positive affect to lose under shelter-in-place measures. Personal courage may have operated through social approach. Given both factors may have operated along the same approach/avoidance pathway, personal courage may override the avoidant tendencies in neuroticism among individuals high on both factors. Moreover, individuals high on neuroticism who also engage in continuous exposure to their subjective fears through personal courage may experience lessened fear over time and weakened effects of neuroticism. We expect the current study to find that personal courage moderates the relationship between neuroticism and transdiagnostic symptom factors, such that higher levels of personal courage weaken the neuroticism-symptom factor relationship for each factor during the COVID-19 transition period.

title: The marginal propensity to consume and household savings during the COVID-19 pandemic: evidence from Thailand and Vietnam
abstract: Using household surveys from Thailand and Vietnam during the COVID-19 pandemic, we find that the marginal propensity to consume is significantly higher for positive income shocks than for negative ones. Moreover, we find that households’ savings positions play a crucial role, as the effects are especially pronounced for households that experienced a decline in savings. This result contradicts predictions from the life-cycle permanent income model with borrowing constraints as well as empirical evidence from industrialised countries. However, our finding is consistent with Kahneman and Tversky’s prospect theory, according to which the combination of income uncertainty and loss aversion may contribute to stronger reported responses to positive shocks.

title: Depression, anxiety, stress, and intolerance of uncertainty during the COVID-19 pandemic by considering the impact of pre-existing mental health issues
abstract: This research was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study aims to investigate self-reported mental health issues in a public sample, including depression, anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty about the future. A public sample (N = 313) was obtained through social media, and collected using an online survey. Participants completed a series of demographic questions including disclosure about previous mental health issues, the depression anxiety stress scale (DASS) and the intolerance uncertainty scale (IUS). There was a strong positive relationship between elements of the DASS and IUS. Having previous mental health issues were strongly associated with higher scores across all measures. Evidence is provided to support the notion that additional stress, anxiety and fear is experienced by people with pre-existing mental health issues during unprecedented times. This research offers a unique insight into the mental health of the general public during a global pandemic.

title: COVID-19 diagnosis using a decision tree algorithm
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a respiratory infection for which chest X-ray (CXR) imaging can provide an accessible screening modality. This study investigates an interpretable computer-aided screening pipeline for distinguishing COVID-19-positive from normal CXR images. Methods: The pipeline combines Otsu-based lung segmentation, morphological refinement, seven Hu invariant shape moments, training-fold z-score normalization, and a class-weighted Decision Tree. A cohort of 2,600 CXR images (1,000 COVID-19-positive and 1,600 normal) was evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation. The retained experimental record reports 98.6% accuracy, 97.8% precision, 98.6% recall (sensitivity), and 98.2% F1-score. The pooled confusion matrix shows TP=986, FN=14, FP=22, and TN=1578, corresponding to 98.6% accuracy and 97.8% precision. ROC/AUC analysis yielded AUC = 0.987 ± 0.004 under the image-level evaluation protocol. Conclusion: The findings indicate that a low-dimensional, shape-based descriptor combined with an interpretable Decision Tree can discriminate COVID-19-positive from normal CXR images under the present internal image-level protocol. Because the cohort was not partitioned at the patient or source level and no independent external cohort was retained in the study record, the results are considered preliminary proof-of-concept evidence rather than clinically validated diagnostic performance.

title: Patrones espaciales de la violencia familiar en México durante el confinamiento por COVID-19 Spatial patterns of family violence in Mexico during the COVID-19 lockdown
abstract: This article analyzes family violence in Mexico during the COVID-19 lockdown from a geographical perspective, using autocorrelation and regression models to identify sociodemographic and social disadvantage factors associated with its territorial distribution. The results show that family violence was not randomly distributed but rather concentrated in clusters of municipalities with high rates in the north, northwest and central-west regions of the country, and with low rates in the south and southeast. Some variables commonly associated with violence –such as insufficient income, economic dependency, income gaps, and educational lag– showed effects contrary to expectations, suggesting that, in the context of lockdown, poverty and inequality operated differently than in non-extraordinary periods. In contrast, urbanization, demographic feminization, and a higher proportion of female-headed households were associated with an increase in family violence. The findings confirm the multicausal nature of the phenomenon and highlight the importance of considering spatial dependence to understand its territorial distribution.

title: Long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection on diabetes: A metabolomics study of systemic metabolism
abstract: This thesis examines how previous COVID-19 relates to diabetes by analysing blood sugar, fats, particles that carry fats and cholesterol, and other blood measures. The study analyses blood samples from adults in Mauritius and finds a more pronounced pattern of unhealthy blood fats in people with diabetes who previously had COVID-19. This pattern may be linked to artery-blockage risk. Over about one year, new-onset diabetes is more common in people with previous COVID-19 and is accompanied by changes in blood fats. The study suggests closer monitoring of blood sugar and heart health after COVID-19, especially in people with diabetes.

title: Economic resilience in low-income African communities: Assessing post-COVID-19 ramifications and indigenous mitigation strategies
abstract: Background: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic had significant economic consequences for South Africans, prompting the government to implement contingency plans to manage and mitigate its effects. These strategies required strict compliance from the population, particularly in low-income communities. Aim: This study aimed to provide an in-depth account of the economic ramifications of COVID-19 and the outcomes of government-imposed mitigation measures on compliance within low-income communities. Setting: The study was conducted in informal settlements located around Johannesburg and Cape Town, South Africa. Methods: A qualitative case study approach was adopted. Data were collected through individual and group interviews with residents of the selected informal settlements. Thematic analysis was used to identify key themes related to government strategies and their economic outcomes. Results: The study identified two main themes: (1) government strategies to prevent contagion and ensure compliance, which included lockdown, social distancing and economic relief initiatives and (2) economic ramifications, where residents experienced substantial economic hardship because of restrictions, including loss of income, food insecurity and limited access to essential services, which in turn affected their ability to comply with public health measures. Conclusion: The findings highlight the complex interplay between government pandemic-control strategies and the economic realities faced by low-income communities. Economic hardship significantly affected compliance with COVID-19 mitigation measures. Contribution: This study contributes to a deeper understanding of how pandemic mitigation strategies influence vulnerable populations, providing valuable insights for policymakers to design more effective and equitable public health interventions in times of crisis.
