title: The impact of tax compliance governance on the corporate financial performance during the COVID-19 crisis
abstract: This study examines how tax compliance governance affects the financial performance of listed companies in Morocco during the challenging COVID-19 crisis period. Building on the recognition that tax compliance extends well beyond traditional control mechanisms and is shaped by broader institutional and behavioral factors (Alm, 2019), alongside evidence that responsible corporate practices can strengthen relationships with key stakeholders (Freeman et al., 2010), we approached the tax compliance seal as a governance mechanism with the potential to generate tangible financial benefits. Using panel data from 2013 to 2021, we conducted a linear regression analysis, completed with robustness tests to evaluate model specification and ensure estimate reliability. The results show a significant positive relationship between the tax compliance seal and firms’ financial performance, although its effects vary by performance indicator and time period. These results suggest that effective tax compliance governance can strengthen financial resilience and market capitalization during times of economic uncertainty.

title: Miocardite aguda em pacientes com COVID-19: uma revisão de literatura
abstract: Introdução: A COVID-19 é uma doença infecciosa altamente contagiosa que pode causar repercussões graves em diversos órgãos e sistemas, incluindo o sistema cardiovascular, o qual é acometido de maneira direta e indireta pelo vírus, uma das principais manifestações se dá pela miocardite aguda a qual acomete, em graus variados de intensidade, cerca de 20-30% dos pacientes hospitalizados pela COVID-19. Objetivo: Diante disso a presente revisão bibliográfica objetiva reunir e sintetizar de maneira clara e objetiva as informações já adquiridas em estudos e relatos de caso envolvendo a miocardite infecciosa pelo sars-cov-2. Método: A consulta eletrônica de dados foi conduzida nas seguintes bases: scielo, lilacs, Google acadêmico e pubmed. Os descritores utilizados: COVID-19, myocarditis, sars-cov-2, heart failure. Foram estabelecidos critérios de inclusão: literaturas referentes aos anos de 2020 e 2021 correspondentes aos descritores, e de exclusão: literaturas que não responderam integralmente aos descritores utilizados. Resultado: Foram encontrados 14 artigos, nos quais todos se enquadraram nos critérios de escolha, apresentando a miocardite causada pelo sars-cov-2 como uma das complicações mais prevalentes em pacientes hospitalizados. Consideração/Conclusão: A miocardite aguda causada pela COVID-19 acomete mais gravemente os pacientes com doenças cardiovasculares prévias, os quais em 41% desenvolvem miocardite fulminante, manifestação que atinge mortalidade de até 70%.

source_records.abstract: Introdução: A COVID-19 é uma doença infecciosa altamente contagiosa que pode causar repercussões graves em diversos órgãos e sistemas, incluindo o sistema cardiovascular, o qual é acometido de maneira direta e indireta pelo vírus, uma das principais manifestações se dá pela miocardite aguda a qual acomete, em graus variados de intensidade, cerca de 20-30% dos pacientes hospitalizados pela COVID-19. Objetivo: Diante disso a presente revisão bibliográfica objetiva reunir e sintetizar de maneira clara e objetiva as informações já adquiridas em estudos e relatos de caso envolvendo a miocardite infecciosa pelo sars-cov-2. Método: A consulta eletrônica de dados foi conduzida nas seguintes bases: scielo, lilacs, Google acadêmico e pubmed. Os descritores utilizados: COVID-19, myocarditis, sars-cov-2, heart failure. Foram estabelecidos critérios de inclusão: literaturas referentes aos anos de 2020 e 2021 correspondentes aos descritores, e de exclusão: literaturas que não responderam integralmente aos descritores utilizados. Resultado: Foram encontrados 14 artigos, nos quais todos se enquadraram nos critérios de escolha, apresentando a miocardite causada pelo sars-cov-2 como uma das complicações mais prevalentes em pacientes hospitalizados. Consideração/Conclusão: A miocardite aguda causada pela COVID-19 acomete mais gravemente os pacientes com doenças cardiovasculares prévias, os quais em 41% desenvolvem miocardite fulminante, manifestação que atinge mortalidade de até 70%.

title: Maternal Exposure to Ambient Ozone and Birthweight Reduction During COVID-19 Epidemic in East China: A Sex- and Window-Specific Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Low birthweight (LBW) remains a major global public health challenge, with long-term consequences for neonatal survival and chronic disease risk. Maternal exposure to ambient ozone (O3) has been implicated in fetal growth restriction, but evidence remains inconsistent. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 14,381 term singleton live births in Zhejiang Province, East China, during the COVID-19 lockdown and quarantine period. Maternal O3 exposure during each trimester and the entire pregnancy was estimated using data from nearest atmospheric monitoring stations, with refined time-activity patterns accounting for home and workplace locations. Results: In multivariable linear regression adjusted for the pre-specified covariates, maternal O3 exposure averaged over the entire pregnancy was inversely associated with birthweight (pooled estimate across sex- and residence-stratified models: β = −2.1 g per μg/m3, 95% CI: −3.6 to −0.5; stratum-specific β ranged from −2.24 to −0.92). An interquartile range (IQR) of approximately 10–15 μg/m3 in entire-pregnancy O3 exposure increase was associated with an estimated birthweight reduction of about 20–33 g; the range reflected the combination of stratum-specific β estimates and stratum-specific IQRs. The explained variance was small as indicated by R2, showing that O3 was not a powerful individual-level predictor of birthweight; the precisely estimated β nonetheless reflected a systematic shift in the population distribution of birthweight. Conclusions: Maternal O3 exposure during pregnancy was associated with reduced birthweight in a sex- and window-specific manner. The third trimester was more stronger association period for female fetuses, whereas cumulative exposure across mid-to-whole pregnancy was more critical for males. Maternal nutritional intake is a plausible modifiable factor that may attenuate susceptibility, but the present study did not measure diet, food insecurity, or psychological stress. Future studies should incorporate dietary assessment and biomarkers to test this hypothesis.

title: Mortality prediction scores for pediatric poisonings before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic: analysis of the virtual pediatric systems intensive care unit database
abstract: Drug overdoses are one of the leading causes of pediatric hospitalizations. Mortality from pediatric drug overdoses increased during the COVID-19 pandemic. To better understand this trend, this study tracked national Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) admissions for pediatric overdoses across the periods before, during, and after the pandemic. We hypothesized that pediatric patients admitted to the PICU for drug overdoses involving opioids, non-opioid analgesics, anti-depressants, anti-convulsants, stimulants, alcohols, or cannabis during the PICU during the COVID-19 pandemic would have a higher probability of mortality, measured by Pediatric Index of Mortality (PIM-3) and Pediatric Risk of Mortality (PRISM-III), compared to before and after the pandemic. This is a multi-center, retrospective cohort of de-identified patients aged 2–21-years admitted to the PICU between January 2019 to June 2023 using the Virtual Pediatric Systems (VPS) database. Patients were included using VPS “Star” and ICD-9 codes associated with poisoning admissions involving common drug classes. Admissions were categorized into three specified time-periods: pre-COVID, peak-COVID, and post-COVID. Primary outcomes included demographics, daily admissions for poisonings by drug class, and probability of mortality measured by PIM-3 and PRISM-III. Secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay. This study included 35125 poisoning admissions (13,699 males and 21,424 females) with approximately 31.0, 19.0, and 17.4 poisoning admissions per day in pre-COVID, peak-COVID, and post-COVID periods respectively ( p < 0.05). Demographics had statistically significant differences across COVID time periods for race/ethnicity, age, and sex ( p < 0.05) with white patients between 12 and 21 years comprising the most admissions over the time period. The median probability of mortality measured by PIM-3 decreased over the time period (0.73% to 0.71% to 0.66%) while PRISM remained unchanged throughout the study (0.34%). The average hospital length of stay across all drug classes increased across time periods (4.07 to 4.51 to 5.40 days; p < 0.05). Although the probability of mortality decreased over time, the hospital length of stay increased, indicating an ongoing healthcare burden among pediatric patients admitted to the PICU with drug poisonings. These findings highlight the continued need for hospital resources for patients with acute poisoning.

title: Health Emergencies and Democratic Erosion: Did the COVID-19 Pandemic Help Autocratization?
abstract: Abstract Emergencies are often thought to provide a great opportunity for authoritarian leaders to deepen and consolidate their grip on power. The COVID-19 pandemic, the deadliest peacetime threat to human welfare in one hundred years, provided a dramatic test case for the resilience of constitutional structures. The response to it entailed an unprecedented degree of state intervention in the lives of citizens, spanning a range of coercive, mandatory policies such as restrictions on movement and gatherings, imposition of face masks, extensive state interference with the market through eviction and dismissal bans, as well as state provision through public programs such as income support, tax relief, and public health and vaccination provision. All such measures can be justified by reference to the public health threat. Yet the manner in which they are designed and implemented, their duration, and oversight of them can all be manipulated by power-hungry autocrats seeking to increase their powers. This chapter draws on that wealth of data and analysis collected in the Lex-Atlas: Covid-19 project, which compared over fifty countries’ responses to the pandemic, to assess whether the COVID-19 pandemic window of opportunity was effectively used by autocratizers, a point all too salient during the global “third wave of autocratization.” The key message is that constitutional structures proved fairly resilient across the dataset, but also that there were distinct dangers of backsliding in hybrid democracies.

title: ASPECTO GENÉTICO E MICROBIOLÓGICO DA VACINA DE RNA NO MECANISMO DE IMUNIZAÇÃO E NA EFETIVIDADE CONTRA A COVID-19 FRENTE À VARIANTE GAMA (P.1): O CONTEXTO DO AMAZONAS DURANTE A PANDEMIA
abstract: Esta revisão integrativa descreve o desenho e o mecanismo de ação das vacinas de RNA mensageiro (RNAm) e analisa como a variabilidade genética do SARS-CoV-2 (coronavírus da síndrome respiratória aguda grave 2) influenciou o escape imunológico e a efetividade dessas vacinas no contexto epidemiológico do Amazonas, com destaque para a variante Gama (P.1). A busca ocorreu nas bases PubMed e SciELO, complementada pelo Google Scholar, com publicações de 2020 a 2026, e os estudos foram organizados em eixos temáticos e analisados de forma qualitativa e descritiva. A Gama reuniu 17 mutações, entre elas K417T, E484K e N501Y no domínio de ligação ao receptor da proteína Spike, e foi estimada, conforme o modelo, como 1,7 a 2,4 ou cerca de 2,6 vezes mais transmissível que as linhagens anteriores; reinfecções foram documentadas em Manaus. Soros de vacinados com RNAm apresentaram redução dos títulos neutralizantes contra a Gama, com manutenção de neutralização significativa, e a reatividade de células T foi pouco afetada. Fora do Brasil, estudos canadenses estimaram a efetividade de uma dose de RNAm contra a Gama entre 61% e 89%. No Brasil, a vacinação durante a onda Gama baseou-se sobretudo em CoronaVac e ChAdOx1, e o RNAm foi empregado principalmente como reforço, com alta efetividade em dados nacionais. Conclui-se que compreender a evolução genética do SARS-CoV-2 e seus efeitos sobre a resposta imunológica orienta a vacinação e a vigilância epidemiológica, e que estudos locais sobre a efetividade das vacinas de RNAm ainda precisam ser realizados no Amazonas.

title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. Findings: Sustainability performance (ESG scores) significantly enhanced stock resilience during the pandemic. However, this protective effect dissipated post-pandemic. Results confirm a statistically significant improvement in overall resilience following the crisis, as investors redirected their focus toward traditional financial fundamentals such as profitability and leverage. Conclusion: Sustainability performance acts as situational crisis insurance. Its risk-mitigation value is highly salient during systemic uncertainty but diminishes under stable market conditions. Novelty/Originality of this article: Unlike prior single-phase studies in developed economies, this research provides longitudinal evidence on the dynamic, state-dependent nature of sustainability performance across crisis and recovery phases within Southeast Asia’s early-stage ESG landscape.

title: Lecciones de las pandemias de influenza y de COVID-19 para la odontología: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar las lecciones de los brotes históricos de influenza y de la pandemia de COVID-19 aplicables a la atención odontológica. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas y narrativas, ensayos clínicos y documentos de análisis histórico. Resultados: la pandemia de 1918 mostró el valor de proteger al personal sanitario y la de 2009, el de los diagnósticos moleculares y del uso planificado de los antivirales. En odontología, la COVID-19 obligó a controlar los aerosoles, reforzar la bioseguridad, priorizar la atención urgente, evaluar colutorios antisépticos y atender el agotamiento profesional. Conclusión: la preparación odontológica exige protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y planes de continuidad asistencial.

title: Auditor switching under COVID-19 pandemic: evidence from China
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether and how the COVID-19 pandemic altered firms’ auditor switching behavior. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on crisis management theory, the authors analyze a panel data set of Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms from 2016 to 2023 using a propensity score matching–difference-in-differences (PSM–DiD) approach. Findings Pandemic exposure significantly increased auditor switching likelihood. This effect was attenuated by slack resources but amplified when the incumbent auditor was a large audit firm, suggesting that crisis-induced switching reflects strategic adaptation shaped by internal resource endowments and external relational constraints. Practical implications Managers may leverage auditor switching as a crisis adaptation strategy, though such decisions carry audit quality risks. Regulators should monitor elevated switching rates during crises as potential indicators of governance stress. Originality/value This paper contributes to the literature by empirically investigating auditor switching as a strategic crisis response. By integrating crisis management theory with established auditor switching perspectives, it complements the “auditor-side” COVID-19 literature with a “client-side” perspective and identifies boundary conditions governing firms’ crisis responses.

title: Sub‐State Nationalism and the Pandemic: Everyday Constitutional Reasoning and Welsh Political Autonomy During Covid‐19
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines the relationship between Covid‐19 attitudes and Welsh national sentiment, focusing on how the pandemic shaped public evaluations of Welsh autonomy within the United Kingdom's devolved governance structure. Drawing on survey and qualitative interview data, it shows that Covid‐19 did not simply shift support for greater autonomy and independence but was associated with changes in how constitutional preferences are expressed and justified. Favourable evaluations of the Welsh Government's pandemic response and preventative health measures are linked to support for greater autonomy. The relationship with Welsh independence, however, remains ambiguous. Some Covid‐sceptic individuals with political mistrust expressed support for independence, highlighting the complexity of the relationship between public policy, health measures and sub‐state nationalism. The findings illustrate how public health crises can reconfigure the mode of nationalist reasoning, shifting it towards everyday assessments of competence, care and governance. More broadly, the study advances minority nationalism theory by showing how crisis conditions alter the evaluative frameworks through which constitutional preferences are formed and articulated.

title: The relationship between the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and Polish teachers' mental health and work ability
abstract: Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic has had serious negative socioeconomic consequences and has led to changes in day-to-day functioning and work organization. The outbreak and subsequent school closures abruptly compelled teachers to switch from classroom instruction to distance education, requiring rapid adaptation to new digital technologies with insufficient support. These unexpected transformations may have affected teachers’ stress levels and, consequently, their mental health and work ability. The purpose of the study was to examine the relationship between challenges at work during the pandemic, subjectively perceived work ability, and the general functioning of teachers of primary and secondary schools. Material and Methods: The study included 370 primary and secondary school teachers from the Łódź Voivodship, Poland. Data were collected online from October 2022 to May 2023, after in-person teaching had resumed. Participants completed an occupational stressor checklist, the single-item Work Ability Score (WAS) derived from the Work Ability Index , the General Functioning Questionnaire , 58 items (GFQ-58), and questions on pandemic-re-lated concerns and threats. Factor structure and associations were examined using factor analyses, non-parametric tests, and binary logistic regression. Results: Work-related stress was associated with lower self-rated work ability and poorer general psychological functioning. Relational and communication difficulties were associated with higher odds of poor or moderate work ability (OR = 1.73, 95% CI: 1.17–2.55). Insufficient organizational and training support, technological barriers and rapid work changes, personal concerns, and an acute COVID-19 infection course were independently associated with higher odds of an elevated GFQ-58 score. Conclusions: The study allowed for the identification of key pandemic-related psychosocial stressors and their associations with teachers’ work ability and general psychological functioning. These findings highlight the importance of organizational support and preparedness during periods of rapid change, while the effectiveness of specific interventions requires further evaluation. Int J Occup Med Environ Health.

title: The relationship between Twitter uncertainty measures and stock market returns during the COVID-19 crisis
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore how uncertainty captured through social media, particularly Twitter, affects global stock markets during the COVID-19 crisis. It focuses on whether the Twitter economic uncertainty (TEU) and Twitter Market Uncertainty (TMU) indices contain information that helps explain market behaviour in periods of stress. Design/methodology/approach The analysis relies on daily data from January 2007 to May 2023. This paper combines linear and nonlinear Granger causality tests (Diks and Panchenko, 2006) with the BDS nonlinearity test, and a Dynamic Conditional Correlation-Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (DCC-GARCH) connectedness framework is used (Gabauer, 2020) to capture the dynamic transmission of volatility between Twitter-based sentiment indicators and 13 international financial markets. Findings The results highlight strong nonlinear causal effects from Twitter-based uncertainty measures to market returns. TEU and TMU indices appear to drive fluctuations in stock returns, particularly during episodes of heightened uncertainty. The DCC-GARCH analysis shows that TEU-ENG and TEU-USA act as net transmitters of volatility to markets such as Japan, Ukraine, China, Germany and even Bitcoin. Research limitations/implications As the study focuses mainly on the COVID-19 crisis, future research could extend the analysis to other stress periods or explore alternative sentiment measures such as the volatility index. Practical implications The findings suggest that social media sentiment can serve as a timely indicator for risk managers and investors, complementing traditional uncertainty measures. Social implications The results highlight how collective behaviour on social networks can amplify uncertainty and market reactions, underscoring the need for responsible communication and better public understanding of financial information online. Originality/value This study offers fresh evidence on how Twitter-based uncertainty indices interact with market dynamics, combining behavioral–finance insights with nonlinear econometric techniques.

title: Purchased resilience in the food industry: how COVID-19 deferred structural vulnerability in Italian agri-food SMEs (2019–2023)
abstract: To examine whether SMEs in Italian food and beverage processing were disproportionately affected by COVID-19, and by what means short-run outcomes were sustained, developing purchased resilience: performance maintained through external resources whose cost is deferred. Accounting panel for 2,661 Unionalimentari-affiliated SMEs (2019–2023) against 199 enterprises of 250 or more employees. Fixed-effects estimates of differential changes in profitability and leverage, plus a test of whether leverage accumulated under the support schemes predicts later performance. Profitability shows no detectable differential shift between size classes (ROE β = −0.262; ROI β = −0.082; both n.s.). Leverage diverged: SMEs deleveraged more slowly (β = +2.061, p = 0.022), widening an eighteen-point pre-existing gap. Unit labour costs rose 16.6% for micro-enterprises against 6.6% for large firms, and firms accumulating more leverage recorded weaker 2022 ROI (−0.184, p < 0.001). With one pre-treatment year, parallel trends cannot be verified; estimates are differential changes, not causal effects. The groups differ in more than size, and 2023 coverage reaches 56.0% of 2019 reporters. Crisis instruments delivered as debt require an exit design. The change in the debt ratio over that period is observable in filed accounts and could screen firms for post-crisis measures. Introduces purchased resilience as a construct distinct from absorptive, adaptive and financial resilience, with firm-level evidence linking leverage divergence to later performance in the context of broad crisis-support mechanisms.

title: COVID-19 as a Compound Hazard: Emergency Managers Experiences in Compound Disaster Management
abstract: The health impacts of the coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) have been widely documented; however, less is known about the impacts of the COVID-19 response on emergency managers who were part of the COVID-19 response while continuing with their everyday disaster job, too. Interviews were conducted in late 2021 with state emergency management planners from 21 states to discuss their experience handling COVID-19 and other disasters concurrently. The 158 disasters declared during the COVID-19 pandemic give us a unique view of compound hazard events that include a long-duration hazard with a large geographic footprint. Experiences from emergency managers serving during COVID-19 were able to shine a light on activities and policies that helped and hindered their efforts to serve their communities most effectively. Common issues encountered were related to coordination, lack of training in roles, a need for more resources in rural areas, more planning for long duration events, and mental health resources.

title: Prevalence of Musculoskeletal Symptoms in Post-COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Background: Coronavirus disease 2019 can affect several body systems, and musculoskeletal symptoms may persist after recovery from the acute infection. Pain and other musculoskeletal complaints can create additional challenges during the post-COVID-19 recovery period. Objective: To determine the frequency and distribution of musculoskeletal symptoms among post-COVID-19 patients. Methodology: This observational cross-sectional study was conducted from June to September 2021 after ethical approval from the Lyallpur Institute of Management Sciences, using purposive sampling to recruit 120 individuals with previous COVID-19 infection, of whom 70 met the eligibility criteria. Participants were aged 30 to 55 years, had recovered from COVID-19 with a negative test, reported musculoskeletal symptoms, and had manual muscle testing grades 1–3, while smokers, those with autoimmune conditions, those >55 years, and participants still positive or under quarantine were excluded. Data were collected through a demographic form, self-developed screening questionnaire, 0–5 verbal pain scale, Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire, and Standardised Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire, administered through face-to-face interviews. The Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire assessed overall musculoskeletal health (0–56), while the Nordic Questionnaire identified symptoms across different anatomical regions. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, and appropriate measures for numerical variables, were used to summarize demographic characteristics, pain intensity, Musculoskeletal Health Questionnaire scores, and musculoskeletal symptoms. Results: Of the 70 participants, 50 (71.4%) reported very severe pain, 14 (20%) reported the worst possible pain, and 6 (8.6%) reported severe pain. Neck and shoulder symptoms were reported by all participants (100%), followed by upper-back symptoms (98.6%) and lower-back symptoms (94.3%). Knee symptoms were reported by 81.4% of participants, while ankle, elbow, and wrist symptoms were reported by 68.6%, 57.1%, and 54.3%, respectively. Hip symptoms were reported by 42.9% of participants. Conclusion: Musculoskeletal symptoms were frequently reported among the post-COVID-19 patients included in this study, particularly in the neck, shoulder, upper-back, and lower-back regions. These findings highlight the importance of assessing musculoskeletal complaints during post-COVID-19 follow-up. Larger prospective studies incorporating objective functional assessments are needed to determine symptom progression and rehabilitation needs.
journal: Healer Journal of Biomedical and Health Sciences

title: Self-Reported COVID-19 Diagnosis and Workplace Preparedness Indicators Among Primary Healthcare Workers in King Sabatha Dalindyebo, South Africa
abstract: Background/Objectives: Primary healthcare (PHC) workers played a central role in the COVID-19 response, yet evidence on self-reported COVID-19 diagnosis and workplace preparedness in resource-constrained PHC settings remains limited. This study assessed the frequency and distribution of self-reported COVID-19 diagnosis among PHC workers in King Sabatha Dalindyebo, South Africa, and examined its associations with occupational category and selected workplace preparedness indicators. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 268 PHC workers in King Sabatha Dalindyebo sub-district, Eastern Cape Province, South Africa, from January 2022 to April 2022. A structured self-administered questionnaire measured demographic and occupational characteristics, COVID-19 history, and individual preventive behaviours and workplace preparedness indicators. The primary outcome was self-reported COVID-19 diagnosis during 2020–2022. Descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were used. The principal model included age and occupational role; an extended model additionally included sex and selected preparedness indicators (PPE use, COVID-19 policy availability, workplace risk assessment and N95 fit testing). Results: Of 266 participants with valid outcome data, 103 (38.7%) reported a COVID-19 diagnosis. Age ≥ 46 years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10–3.16) and professional nurse/facility manager status (aOR 2.73, 95% CI 1.61–4.61) were independently associated with diagnosis in the principal model. In the extended model (n = 263; 101 reported diagnoses), the associations persisted (age ≥ 46 years: aOR 1.83, 95% CI 1.06–3.19; nurse/facility manager: aOR 3.22, 95% CI 1.84–5.64), whereas self-reported consistent PPE use, policy availability, workplace risk assessment, and N95 fit testing were not statistically significantly associated after adjustment with reported diagnosis. The corresponding occupational-category adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) were 1.82 (principal model) and 1.98 (extended model). Conclusions: Self-reported COVID-19 diagnosis was common among PHC workers in this South African setting and was associated with older age and professional nurse/facility manager status. The measured preventive behaviour and workplace preparedness indicators were not statistically significantly associated with diagnosis in the extended model. However, the cross-sectional design, uncertain temporality and reliance on self-reported measures limit interpretation. These findings support further role-sensitive occupational surveillance and prospective evaluation of infection-prevention implementation in PHC settings.

title: ВЛИЯНИЕ МИКРОНИЗИРОВАННОГО ПРОГЕСТЕРОНА НА ПЕРИНАТАЛЬНЫЕ ИСХОДЫ ЖЕНЩИН, ПЕРЕНЕСШИХ SARS-COV-2 ИНФЕКЦИЮ ВО ВРЕМЯ БЕРЕМЕННОСТИ
abstract: В период пандемии новой коронавирусной инфекции актуальным стал вопрос о поиске лекарственных препаратов, способных улучшить перинатальные исходы женщин и оказать благоприятное влияние на ранний неонатальный период у новорожденных. Цель исследования - оценить связь применения микронизированного прогестерона с перинатальными исходами у женщин, перенёсших COVID-19 в период гестации. Проведен ретроспективный анализ 165 историй течения беременности, родов и историй развития новорожденных, находившихся под наблюдением в 2020-2023 гг. Контрольную группу составили беременные женщины (n=30), которые во время гестации вирусной инфекцией SARS-CОV-2 не болели. title: Fractional-Order Hybrid SIR Forecasting of COVID-19 in Bangladesh and the United States: Memory Effects and Out-of-Sample Evaluation
abstract: Fractional-order epidemic models are often justified by memory, yet whether memory improves forecasts is rarely tested out of sample. We extend a hybrid SIR framework, in which a daily transmission rate is reconstructed from reported cases and then forecast, to Caputo fractional order $\alpha\in(0,1]$. We prove well-posedness, conservation, positivity and a linearized threshold at disease-free states, and derive a Gr\"unwald-Letnikov reconstruction that reduces exactly to the integer-order one at $\alpha=1$. Our main theoretical result shows that for $\alpha<1$ the influence of the unknown initial infectious count vanishes, but no faster than $t^{-\alpha}$; after 332 daily steps it is about $4.4\times10^{8}$ times larger at $\alpha=0.9$ than at $\alpha=1$. In out-of-sample forecasting over 27 weekly origins, the effect of memory depends on the setting. In Bangladesh the integer order gives the lowest error for linear and constant-rate forecasts in 47 of 48 settings. In the United States, where reported cases reached about 18% of the population, a fractional order lowers the linear forecaster's error in all 12 comparisons in 2021 but raises the constant-rate forecaster's, with no difference significant after Holm adjustment. Against standard baselines, the SIR-based linear forecaster was more accurate than the classical SIR model and a neural network without SIR structure, and competitive with ARIMA: in the United States the fractional linear forecaster had the lowest error of all methods (seven-day MAPE 7.54% against 9.14% for ARIMA), whereas in Bangladesh ARIMA had the lowest MAPE, with no significant difference from ARIMA in either country. The choice of a fractional order should rest on out-of-sample evidence rather than in-sample fit.

title: A panel-trained neural integer-valued autoregressive network for multi-country COVID-19 mortality forecasting, with an analysis of Poisson–Weighted Sujatha innovations
abstract: Integer-valued autoregressive (INAR) models are a standard framework for count time series, but their innovation law is usually fixed in advance and their thinning probability is usually constant. We study a three-parameter Poisson–Weighted Sujatha (PWS) count distribution, obtained by Poisson-mixing a weighted Sujatha density with a free rate λ. With λ = 1 it coincides with the Poisson-weighted Sujatha law of Shanker and Shukla; our additions are the rate parameter, proofs, and an analysis of the likelihood. The pmf is a three-component Negative Binomial mixture; we derive moments, limiting relations to the Poisson, Negative Binomial and Poisson–Sujatha laws, and, for the continuous mixing density, exact conditions for a monotone hazard rate and mean residual life: they hold for c ≥1/27 but not for all θ>0 when c is small. The model is strictly identifiable but (θ, λ) are practically unidentified along a likelihood ridge (Fisher information for logθ decays like θ −2 ), whereas the mean, variance and p = θ/(θ+λ) are estimated with decreasing mean squared error. On three COVID-19 series the Negative Binomial has the best AIC and BIC: every PWS component (for c ≥0) is a Negative Binomial with shape at least one, while the series require shape below one, so ĉ lies on the boundary c = 0. We embed PWS in a GRU-driven INAR network with time-varying thinning and innovation parameters (NS-INAR), trained on a panel by an exact convolution likelihood, and evaluate it on weekly COVID-19 mortality in 83 countries under a protocol in which country selection, tuning and training use only pre-test information. The network reduces the aggregate negative log score of a static per-country INAR(1)-NB by 23.2% (95% bootstrap CI [14.1 to 32.2]), but the held-out window is one of collapsed counts, and a persistence forecast with a Negative Binomial law does at least as well; INGARCH-NB and DeepAR-style networks are comparable; seasonal inputs do not help; and PWS innovations beat Negative Binomial innovations in one network design but not under per-series scaling. We therefore attribute the improvement to panel-trained, time-varying parameterisation, not to the PWS law, and restrict our conclusions to one disease, one data source and one forecast window.
journal: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics

title: Firm Performance and Corporate Donations in Nigeria: A Covid-19 Pandemic Analysis
abstract: This study empirically investigated the relationship between firm performance and corporate donations before, during and after covid-19 pandemic period. In order to determine the relationship between firm performance and corporate donations, firm performance was proxy suing return on assets (ROA), return on equity (ROE) and share price (SP) while corporate donations on the other hand was measured using the ratio of donations and total assets. Three hypotheses were formulated to guide the investigation and the statistical test of parameter estimates was conducted using panel regression model operated with STATA 14. Ex Post Facto design was adopted and data for the study were obtained from the published annual financial reports of listed deposit money banks on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) spanning from 2012-2022. The results of the study show that there is no difference in the direction of the effect of return on equity on corporate donation which is positive in the pre covid and in the post covid though both coefficients do not appear to be statistically significant. Also, there is also no difference in the direction of the effect of SP on corporate donation which is negative in the pre covid and in the post covid though both coefficients do not appear to be statistically significant 5% while there is a difference in the direction of the effect of ROA on corporate donation which is negative and significant in the pre covid and then positive and also significant in the post covid. The study therefore concludes that return on assets, return on equity and share price does not determine corporate donations of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. In lieu of the findings of the study, the study recommends that corporate financial performance is a key determinant of corporate donations and the study recommends the need for tax authorities such as the FIRS to implement tax incentives for corporate donations that account for changes in profitability and financial performance. Tax incentives can encourage companies to maintain or increase donations regardless of short-term financial fluctuations

title: ОТДАЛЁННЫЕ НЕВРОЛОГИЧЕСКИЕ ИСХОДЫ ПОСЛЕ COVID-19: КОНТРОЛЬНОЕ ИССЛЕДОВАНИЕ ПАЦИЕНТОВ С НЕВРОЛОГИЧЕСКИМИ ПРОЯВЛЕНИЯМИ
abstract: Изучена 6-летняя динамика отдалённых неврологических исходов у 108 пациентов, госпитализированных с COVID-19 и неврологическими проявлениями в 2020 году. Сохраняющиеся неврологические симптомы выявлялись у 73,1% обследованных. Наиболее частыми отдалёнными проявлениями стали повышенная утомляемость (39,8%) и когнитивные нарушения (31,5%). Тяжёлое и критическое течение острого COVID-19 ассоциировалось с более чем трёхкратным увеличением шансов развития стойких когнитивных нарушений (OR 3,13; 95% CI 1,21–8,08; p=0,015) и длительной утомляемости (OR 2,80; 95% CI 1,18–6,62; p=0,017). Полученные результаты подчёркивают необходимость долгосрочного неврологического наблюдения пациентов после тяжёлого COVID-19.

title: FORMATIVE PROCESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS IN NURSING IN THE CONTEXT OF COVID-19
abstract: Objective: to report the experience of remote teaching in an academic master’s degree course during the covid-19 pandemic. Methods: this is a descriptive study, experience report type, experienced from October to December 2020 in a mandatory subject of the Postgraduate Program in Nursing of a Public University in the state of Pará. Results: The educational activities took place synchronously and asynchronous, from virtual classes and texts for reading, all of that was possible by the use of educational technological strategies in the experienced pandemic scenario. Remote teaching required students and teachers to adapt to the new classroom routine in their homes, adapting the study environment and appropriate equipment for this context. Even with the challenges faced, the establishment of the remote learning process added skills among those involved, improvement of tools and digital transformation of the conventional classroom. Conclusion: remote teaching was efficient and provided opportunities for pedagogical mediations, promoting collaborative learning among students. It also revealed the need for training for those involved in the process.
authors: Marília de Fátima Vieira de Oliveira

title: Impacto de la COVID-19 en los servicios y las políticas de salud de América Latina
abstract: Objetivo: analizar el impacto de la COVID-19 en los servicios de salud pública de América Latina y las políticas adoptadas. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la pandemia interrumpió los servicios esenciales de rutina, incluidas la atención materna y odontológica, y amplió vulnerabilidades previas de sistemas fragmentados y desiguales. Las respuestas incluyeron la reorganización de servicios, la telesalud, la protección de las cadenas de suministro, medidas no farmacológicas y planes de vacunación con prioridades distintas. title: DEVELOPMENT STABILITY OF CHINESE PROVINCES BEFORE AND AFTER THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC: AN I-DISTANCE APPROACH
abstract: Regional inequality among China’s thirty-one provinces is a central concern for economic policy, yet how the COVID-19 shock reshaped their development remains unclear. This study applies the Ivanovic I-distance method to rank the provinces on nine per-capita socio-economic indicators spanning income, consumption, living standards and innovation, comparing the pre-pandemic year 2019 with the post-pandemic year 2022. The I-distance, which weights variables through their partial correlations, suits this small-sample, strongly correlated setting and yields an interpretable composite. The results reveal a pronounced stability: the development hierarchy is almost perfectly preserved across the shock, with a Spearman rank correlation of 0.95 and a Kendall coefficient of 0.85, while Ward clustering reassigns only three of the thirty-one provinces. Behind this stability lie localized asymmetries: several inland provinces rise by up to six places, while economic prosperity diverges from per-capita public provision. Disposable income and consumption dominate the ranking, with a leading contribution of 0.92, whereas educational capacity contributes least. The correlation of the 2022 ordering with independently sourced 2023 income data is 0.85. The pandemic thus perturbed but did not restructure China’s regional development order.

title: Agency of Rohingya Refugees in Bangladesh during the Covid-19 Pandemic
abstract: This article examines the everyday agency exercised by Rohingya refugees with reference to their collective responses during the unprecedented COVID-19 pandemic to demonstrate the refugees’ capacity for collective action and well-being. The article is structured into five sections. The first section theorises refugee agency with reference to the relevant scholarly literature. The second section contextualises the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar district. The third section states the methodology adopted for the study, which is premised on in-depth interviews, observation and informal participant observation in the Rohingya refugee camps. The fourth section highlights the challenges faced by the refugees during the pandemic, while the ensuing fifth section critically analyses the nature of agency of Rohingya refugees during as well as in the aftermath of the pandemic, foregrounding particularly its implications for their everyday life. The concluding section summarises the findings of the article.

title: Impacto de la pandemia del Covid-19 en la salud materno-perinatal en el Hospital I Antonio Skrabonja Antoncich - Pisco de la red asistencial Ica Essalud. 2019-2021
abstract: La pandemia de COVID-19 pudo comprometer la continuidad de la atención obstétrica y neonatal. El objetivo fue comparar los resultados maternos y perinatales antes y durante la pandemia en el Hospital I Antonio Skrabonja Antoncich de Pisco, Perú. La metodología utilizada fue el estudio observacional analítico de cohorte retrospectiva, basado en registros de 1 409 puérperas con gestación única y sus neonatos. Se compararon marzo de 2019 a febrero de 2020 (n=769) y marzo de 2020 a febrero de 2021 (n=640). Se utilizaron frecuencias, odds ratios (OR), intervalos de confianza del 95% y los análisis de chi-cuadrado y regresión logística consignados en la tesis. Para mortalidad perinatal se efectuó una comprobación adicional mediante la prueba exacta bilateral de Fisher a partir de los recuentos publicados. Los resultados arrojaron que las complicaciones maternas aumentaron de 60,7% a 84,4% (OR=3,492; IC95%: 2,698–4,519) y las perinatales de 42,0% a 82,0% (OR=6,304; IC95%: 4,922–8,073). Se observaron mayores frecuencias de preeclampsia, infección urinaria materna, hemorragia posparto, ictericia, infección urinaria neonatal y sepsis neonatal. La cesárea presentó frecuencias similares (44,9% y 44,5%; p=0,901). No se registraron muertes maternas. Hubo una muerte perinatal antes y seis durante la pandemia; la prueba exacta de Fisher produjo p=0,051. La ganancia ponderal gestacional ≤11 kg se asoció con complicaciones maternas durante la pandemia (OR ajustado=2,009; IC95%: 1,135–3,556). Se concluye que el periodo pandémico se asoció con una mayor frecuencia de complicaciones maternas y perinatales en esta población hospitalaria. El diseño retrospectivo y las limitaciones del registro impiden atribuir causalidad o separar los efectos de la infección de los cambios en la atención sanitaria.

title: Long-COVID: Ultrasensitive multiplex protein biomarker profiling reveals subclinical neuroinflammatory and innate immune dysregulation without correlation to symptom severity
abstract: Routine laboratory tests are consistently normal in long-COVID, yet patients suffer persistent and debilitating symptoms. Whether subclinical inflammatory and neurological dysregulation underlies this discordance remains unclear. Ultra-sensitive multiplex proteomics may detect low-abundance biomolecular signals invisible to conventional methods, and alternative mechanisms such as central sensitization may be operative. In this single-centre, age- and sex-matched case–control study, plasma from 48 Long-COVID patients and 48 recovered controls was analysed using the NULISAseqTM CNS Disease Panel 120, quantifying 123 biomolecules with attomolar sensitivity. The median interval from SARS-CoV-2 infection was 65.5 weeks in patients and 72.5 weeks in controls. Differentially expressed proteins were identified using Mann–Whitney U test with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Principal Component Analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis, and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) were used to characterize biological subgroups and activated pathways. Despite no separation between patients and controls on conventional PCA, 19 proteins were significantly dysregulated, with CCL22, IL-6R, and CST3 being prominently upregulated. IPA revealed activation of the Pathogen-Induced Cytokine Storm, Neuroinflammation, and IL-10 Signaling pathways. Hierarchical clustering identified two biologically distinct patient subgroups—one characterized by metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial dysfunction, the other by neuroinflammatory pathway activation—yet neither cluster differed in fatigue, depression, cognitive symptoms, or any other patient-reported outcome measure. Long-COVID harbors subclinical innate immune activation and neuroinflammatory dysregulation detectable only at attomolar sensitivity, with no direct mapping to clinical symptom profiles. This biological-clinical dissociation suggests that additional mechanisms—including central sensitization or epigenetic dysregulation—may translate peripheral immune signals into the symptom burden experienced by patients.

title: Percepção da geração de resíduos sólidos e de hábitos durante a pandemia de COVID-19 na microrregião de Varginha em Minas Gerais
abstract: Este estudo teve como objetivo descrever a percepção sobre a geração de resíduos sólidos domiciliares, as mudanças nos hábitos de consumo e as práticas ambientais durante a pandemia de COVID-19 entre participantes da microrregião de Varginha, Minas Gerais. Realizou-se um levantamento descritivo, com aplicação de questionário online entre 5 de agosto e 23 de novembro de 2021. Participaram 431 respondentes, recrutados por adesão voluntária, sem seleção probabilística. Os resultados foram analisados por frequências absolutas e relativas. Dos participantes, 70,07% relataram perceber aumento na geração de resíduos, 65,89% informaram crises de ansiedade e 54,76% afirmaram ter passado a pedir muita comida em casa. Quanto aos aspectos ambientais, 49,42% declararam separar os resíduos domiciliares, 97,45% manifestaram preocupação com questões ambientais e 22,51% desconheciam a destinação final dos resíduos. Os achados descrevem percepções e práticas autodeclaradas, sem comprovar aumento efetivo da quantidade de resíduos ou relações causais entre ansiedade, alimentação e geração de resíduos. A participação voluntária e exclusivamente online limita a generalização dos resultados para a população regional. O levantamento aponta temas para ações de informação e educação ambiental e para pesquisas que combinem questionários com mensuração direta dos resíduos.
authors: Rosângela Francisca de Paula Vitor Marques

title: Comunicação e Educação em Saúde: O jornal Maré de Notícias significando a covid-19 e educando para a saúde durante os primeiros meses de pandemia no Brasil
abstract: A saúde é assunto frequente nos jornais, alertando ora as novidades da medicina, ora os perigos de não aderir a um estilo de vida saudável - entre outros temas que orbitam a área da saúde. Durante a pandemia e a infodemia do novo coronavírus (2019-nCoV), tal temática teve destaque no jornalismo nacional, buscando ensinar formas de ser, estar e se proteger. O presente trabalho utiliza a perspectiva teórica dos Estudos Culturais em Educação para discutir o currículo cultural do jornalismo em saúde, ao produzir e reverberar significados quanto à saúde e à pandemia, durante os primeiros meses (de março a setembro), após a declaração de Emergência em Saúde Pública de Importância Nacional (ESPIN). O objetivo deste trabalho é analisar quais os sentidos produzidos e relacionados à saúde e quais as ações veiculadas para o enfrentamento desta pandemia, em 7 matérias principais e suas respectivas chamadas na capa, nas edições mensais março à setembro do jornal comunitário Maré de Notícias. O delineamento teórico metodológico consiste na análise cultural, alicerçada no entendimento do jornal como uma sala de aula (Schmidt, 1999) e a Maré como um território necropolítico (Mbembe, 2018). Entende-se que o jornal enfatizou em seu currículo ações de resistência, tanto contra um vírus, quanto às dificuldades deste momento singular na comunidade da Maré, possibilitando uma narrativa, ‘de dentro’. Neste sentido, os significados deste currículo direcionam-se aos moradores da Maré e suas vivências. A Saúde é diagramada no jornal como estratégia de resiliência frente à emergência da educação e saúde contextualizada.
journal: Revista Latino Americana de Estudos em Cultura e Sociedade

title: Associated factors for the quality of nasopharyngeal swab collection: a large-scale COVID-19 screening in Beijing
abstract: Nasopharyngeal swab (NPS) sampling is the primary method for SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid testing and is widely used in large-scale screening, but factors related to the quality of NPS collection have not been systematically investigated. We analysed a self-reported database of personnel who performed NPS collection during large-scale COVID-19 screening in Beijing, China (2022). Three participants younger than 18 years were excluded, leaving 1,483 participants from 827 sampling sites. Two outcomes were specified a priori : a knowledge-based measure (both guideline-based items on sampling site and depth answered correctly) and a self-rated measure (fully standardised vs. all other responses). Associations were estimated by multivariable logistic regression in a single fully adjusted model and re-estimated using generalized estimating equations and cluster-robust standard errors to allow for clustering; precision was assessed against the number of events per variable. Overall, 1,422 participants (95.9%) answered both knowledge items correctly and 974 (65.7%) rated their practice as fully standardised. Only 61 participants (4.1%) answered a knowledge item incorrectly (about 6.8 events per variable), so estimates for that outcome are imprecise and reported as exploratory. Previous sampling experience was the only characteristic that remained significant after correction for multiple testing (OR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.52–6.70). For the self-rated outcome, previous experience (OR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.33–3.32), longer engagement in sampling (OR = 1.03 per month, 95% CI: 1.02–1.04), site emergency management measures (OR = 3.11, 95% CI: 2.12–4.55) and a nursing background (OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.10–1.91) were associated with higher odds of reporting fully standardised practice. Estimates were unchanged after accounting for clustering. Previous sampling experience, duration of engagement, professional background and site-level emergency management measures were associated with self-reported NPS collection quality. The knowledge-based analysis rested on only 61 lower-quality responses, so its estimates are imprecise and exploratory rather than a basis for quantifying effects. Because both outcomes were self-reported and the design was cross-sectional, these findings describe associations rather than causal effects and cannot establish that training, experience or site management improve collection quality. Within these constraints, they may inform training and site-management strategies for future large-scale screening.

title: The Influence of Professional Skepticism, Auditor Knowledge and Client Pressure on Audit Quality during the Covid-19 Pandemic (an Empirical Study of Public Accounting Firms in East Jakarta Registered with IAPI)
abstract: Purpose – This study examines the effect of professional skepticism, auditor knowledge and client pressure on audit quality among auditors working in public accounting firms in East Jakarta during the Covid-19 pandemic, a period in which audit engagements were conducted predominantly under remote and physically restricted conditions. Design/methodology/approach – Primary data were collected through a self-administered questionnaire distributed to auditors employed by public accounting firms in East Jakarta that are registered with the Indonesian Institute of Certified Public Accountants (IAPI). Purposive sampling was applied using three inclusion criteria: current employment in an East Jakarta public accounting firm, a minimum of one year of audit experience, and a minimum undergraduate (S1) qualification. Of the 103 questionnaires returned, 76 satisfied the criteria and were complete, and these were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.0. Findings – Professional skepticism and client pressure exert a statistically significant influence on audit quality (t = 4.215, p = 0.000 and t = 3.051, p = 0.002 respectively), whereas auditor knowledge does not (t = 1.140, p = 0.255). Professional skepticism yields the largest path coefficient in the model, indicating that during a period of crisis and remote auditing an auditor's attitudinal disposition contributes more to audit quality than technical knowledge considered in isolation. Originality/value – The study integrates agency theory and attribution theory into a single behavioural auditing framework in which an internal attribution (professional skepticism), a competence-based resource (auditor knowledge) and an external attribution (client pressure) are modelled simultaneously, and it tests that framework on primary data obtained from practising auditors while remote auditing was a necessity rather than a choice. In doing so it extends the behavioural auditing literature from stable engagement settings to crisis settings. Practical implications – The findings suggest that audit firms responding to disruption should invest in reinforcing skeptical judgement and in structural safeguards against client influence, rather than relying on technical training alone.

Professional skepticism yields the largest path coefficient in the model, indicating that during a period of crisis and remote auditing an auditor's attitudinal disposition contributes more to audit quality than technical knowledge considered in isolation. Originality/value – The study integrates agency theory and attribution theory into a single behavioural auditing framework in which an internal attribution (professional skepticism), a competence-based resource (auditor knowledge) and an external attribution (client pressure) are modelled simultaneously, and it tests that framework on primary data obtained from practising auditors while remote auditing was a necessity rather than a choice. In doing so it extends the behavioural auditing literature from stable engagement settings to crisis settings. Practical implications – The findings suggest that audit firms responding to disruption should invest in reinforcing skeptical judgement and in structural safeguards against client influence, rather than relying on technical training alone.

title: IMPACTOS DA PANDEMIA DA COVID-19 NO PROCESSO DE TRABALHO DE ENFERMEIROS DA ATENÇÃO PRIMÁRIA À SAÚDE DE BELÉM DO PARÁ
abstract: Objetivou-se identificar como se desenvolveu a organização do processo de trabalho dos enfermeiros da Atenção Primária à Saúde (APS) frente à pandemia da covid-19. Trata-se de uma pesquisa descritiva e exploratória, com abordagem qualitativa. Os participantes desse estudo foram 31 enfermeiros alocados na APS do município de Belém-PA. Utilizou-se o software IRAMUTEQ para análise dos discursos, com o dendrograma da Classificação Hierárquica Descendente. Evidenciou-se quatro classes que revelam os significados atribuídos às mudanças no processo de trabalho em decorrência da pandemia da covid-19; o papel da APS em cenários de emergência sanitária; a atuação do enfermeiro na APS em resposta à situação da pandemia da covid-19 e as estratégias utilizadas para manutenção dos serviços. Conclui-se que, apesar dos desafios enfrentados durante a pandemia, os enfermeiros na APS demonstraram notáveis estratégias de adaptação e uma resiliência significativa diante de um contexto complexo e desafiador, evidenciando a multifacetada dinâmica de seu papel.

title: CUIDADOS DE ENFERMAGEM AO IDOSO COM SEQUELAS RESPIRATÓRIAS DA COVID-19 LONGA: REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA
abstract: Este artigo buscou analisar os cuidados de enfermagem destinados a idosos com sequelas respiratórias decorrentes da COVID-19 longa. Para isso, realizou-se uma revisão integrativa da literatura nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE e SciELO, em setembro de 2026, considerando artigos originais publicados entre 2020 e 2026, nos idiomas português e inglês. Após a aplicação dos critérios de inclusão e exclusão, 15 estudos compuseram a amostra, cujos achados foram analisados de forma descritiva e temática. Os resultados evidenciaram dispneia, tosse persistente, alterações pulmonares e redução da tolerância aos esforços, associadas ao comprometimento da funcionalidade, da autonomia e da qualidade de vida. Quanto à enfermagem, destacaram-se a avaliação clínica, o acompanhamento dos sintomas, a educação em saúde, a orientação ao paciente e à família e a articulação multiprofissional. Também foram identificadas dificuldades relacionadas à fragmentação da assistência, à capacitação profissional e à ausência de protocolos específicos. Concluiu-se que o acompanhamento de enfermagem deve integrar a avaliação das manifestações respiratórias às necessidades funcionais e de apoio da pessoa idosa, favorecendo um cuidado contínuo e individualizado.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

title: Análise da completude das fichas de notificação de SRAG por COVID-19 em João Pessoa, 2020-2021
abstract: Objetivou-se analisar a completude das fichas de notificação de SRAG por COVID-19 em João Pessoa, no período de 2020 a 2021. Trata-se de um estudo transversal, descritivo e quantitativo, realizado a partir de 1.316 notificações. Os escores utilizados para avaliar a completude foram: excelente (> 95,0%), bom (90,0% - 95,0%), regular (80,0% - 90,0%), ruim (50,0% - 80,0%) e muito ruim (<50,0%). Os resultados mostraram alta completude nas variáveis sociodemográficas, exceto escolaridade, classificada como “ruim”. A maioria das variáveis de sinais e sintomas apresentou completude “excelente”, enquanto as de comorbidades e fatores de risco foram classificadas entre “ruim” e “muito ruim”. As variáveis referentes à confirmação da doença e à evolução apresentaram, em sua maioria, qualidade “boa” e “excelente”. De forma geral, a análise dos anos de 2020 e 2021 evidenciou padrões semelhantes de completude, indicando consistência no registro, mas também persistência de fragilidades em determinadas variáveis.
authors: Vitória Polliany de Oliveira Silva Nascimento

title: Negotiating the Transition from High School to Higher Education in South Africa Under the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The literature has long explored the transition from high school to higher education through diverse empirical and theoretical lenses. The significance of this chapter is that the author uses the unprecedented COVID-19 challenges in South Africa to contribute to the contemporary and contextual understanding of the transition from high school to university. The chapter aims to problematise the transition from traditional contact teaching to online models, which schools and higher education institutions adopted during the COVID-19 lockdown. The transition not only disrupted education but also exposed and deepened socio-economic and cultural inequalities. Framed by Nancy Fraser’s social justice and Kimberlé Crenshaw’s intersectionality theories, in-depth face-to-face and online interviews revealed that overlooking the complex interplay of social structures during transitions can perpetuate existing injustices. The results highlight the interplay between technological change and pre-existing disparities. They further underscore the necessity for a more inclusive and equitable educational approach which addresses the socio-economic and technological inequalities among learners and students.

title: DESIGUALDADES REGIONAIS NA RECUPERAÇÃO DA ASSISTÊNCIA HOSPITALAR ÀS DOENÇAS CARDIOVASCULARES NO BRASIL APÓS A PANDEMIA DE COVID-19: ESTUDO ECOLÓGICO DE SÉRIE TEMPORAL, 2015–2025
abstract: As doenças cardiovasculares permanecem como a principal causa de morbimortalidade no Brasil, e a pandemia de COVID-19 provocou importantes alterações na organização da assistência hospitalar, com possíveis repercussões persistentes sobre o acesso aos serviços e os desfechos clínicos. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as desigualdades regionais na recuperação da assistência hospitalar às doenças cardiovasculares no Brasil após a pandemia de COVID-19. Trata-se de um estudo ecológico de série temporal, utilizando dados secundários do Sistema de Informações Hospitalares do Sistema Único de Saúde (SIH/SUS), do Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade (SIM) e do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), abrangendo o período de 2015 a 2025. Foram analisadas taxas de internação, mortalidade hospitalar, letalidade, tempo médio de permanência, custos e indicadores de recuperação assistencial, empregando análises descritivas, teste de Mann-Kendall, regressão de Prais-Winsten e testes não paramétricos para comparação entre regiões. Observou-se redução expressiva das internações durante o período pandêmico, seguida de recuperação parcial nos anos subsequentes, acompanhada por aumento da letalidade hospitalar. A recuperação ocorreu de forma heterogênea entre as macrorregiões brasileiras, sendo mais lenta nas regiões Norte e Nordeste e mais consistente nas regiões Sul e Sudeste, evidenciando desigualdades na capacidade de reorganização dos serviços especializados. Os achados demonstram que os efeitos indiretos da pandemia persistiram mesmo após a retomada da assistência, reforçando a necessidade de políticas públicas voltadas ao fortalecimento das redes de atenção cardiovascular, à redução das desigualdades regionais e ao aprimoramento da capacidade de resposta do Sistema Único de Saúde.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

title: INFORMAÇÃO E SAÚDE NA COVID-19: GESTÃO EM DUAS UNIVERSIDADES LUSÓFONAS
abstract: This article presents a qualitative study in two Lusophone universities, one Brazilian and one Portuguese, that articulates information, health and telematic services, institutional flows and responses adopted during the social isolation period of the COVID-19 pandemic. The objective was to understand how information technology services were structured and adapted to meet the informational needs of faculty, students and staff in a health crisis context. The investigation was developed based on structured observation of institutional websites and portals, complemented by semi-structured interviews with managers responsible for the information systems of the universities analyzed. The data were interpreted using the Critical Incident Technique, considering the dimensions of people, processes and technologies. The results indicate that both institutions faced system overload, reorganization of informational flows and the need for technical and emotional training of teams. The Portuguese institution showed greater resilience due to prior digital experience, while the Brazilian institution had to accelerate process digitalization and expand the use of collaborative platforms and community guidance. It is concluded that the organization of health information ecosystems contributed significantly to ensure institutional continuity, supporting health communication and consolidating digital practices incorporated after the pandemic period.
authors: Rita de Cássia Silva dos Santos

title: Altered herpesvirus-specific immune response is associated with long COVID
abstract: Long COVID is associated with persistent immune dysregulation, but whether immunity to latent viruses is also altered remains unclear. We profiled herpesvirus-specific antibodies and T-cell responses in people with long COVID and recovered convalescent controls at 4, 8, and 24 months after SAR-CoV-2 infection. Overall antibody reactivity and abundance against cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) responder frequencies and circulating B-cell subsets were broadly preserved, but early antibody avidity and virus-specific CD4 T cell response magnitude were reduced. Neither virus nucleic acid was detected in plasma or stool at 4 or 8 months. Here, we show that long COVID is associated with selective, time-dependent alteration of herpesvirus-specific immune memory, including relatively preserved or enhanced CD8 responses and greater representation of selected herpesvirus-associated T-cell receptor clonotypes. Together, these findings indicate altered herpesvirus-specific antibody quality despite broadly preserved antibody abundance. Lower EBV avidity was associated with poorer quality of life and unrecovered status.

title: Beyond Metastatic Lymphadenopathy in Breast Cancer: Approach to Axillary Masses.
abstract: The axilla is a pyramid-shaped space containing tissues of various origins including adipose, neural, vascular, cutaneous, myogenic, and lymphatic structures. Axillary masses are typically identified when patients present with palpable areas of concern or during imaging for breast cancer screening or staging. Breast imagers frequently encounter axillary masses while evaluating the axillary region at mammography and US. While reactive lymphadenopathy represents the most common cause of axillary lymph node enlargement, lymph node metastasis from breast cancer is a common cause of axillary masses requiring clinical evaluation. Recent immunization, particularly COVID-19 vaccination, is an important cause of unilateral axillary lymphadenopathy. Additional causes beyond metastatic lymphadenopathy must be considered in the differential diagnosis, including benign and malignant entities arising from accessory breast tissue, adipocytic, neurogenic, vascular, infectious, traumatic, and cutaneous origins. Understanding axillary anatomy is essential for developing a comprehensive differential diagnosis and determining appropriate management strategies. Systematic assessment of characteristic imaging and clinical findings, combined with thorough correlation with patient history and symptoms, enables accurate diagnosis. US serves as the primary imaging modality for mass assessment and biopsy guidance. Depending on the differential diagnosis, mammography, CT, and MRI provide supplementary information to better define mass origin and extent. Definitive diagnosis often requires histopathologic analysis. A systematic approach ensures accurate diagnosis and optimal management of axillary masses. © The Author(s), 2026. title: Impact of obesity on vaccine effectiveness against respiratory viral infections: from immunological mechanisms to clinical outcomes
abstract: Obesity is a major global health challenge associated with chronic low-grade inflammation, immune dysregulation, and increased susceptibility to severe respiratory viral infections. As obesity prevalence continues to rise, understanding its impact on vaccine-induced immunity has become increasingly important. This narrative review examines current evidence on the effects of obesity on vaccine immunogenicity, immune durability, and clinical effectiveness against influenza and coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Studies demonstrate that obesity has little effect on early humoral responses following influenza vaccination, whereas findings for COVID-19 vaccines are more heterogeneous and influenced by vaccine platform, obesity severity, prior infection, metabolic health, and follow-up duration. However, longitudinal evidence from both influenza and COVID-19 vaccine studies suggests that obesity, particularly severe obesity, is associated with accelerated antibody waning, reduced neutralizing activity, impaired memory B-cell and antigen-specific T-cell responses, and increased breakthrough infections despite initially adequate antibody titres. These alterations are driven by chronic inflammatory signaling, adipokine imbalance, impaired antigen presentation, germinal center dysfunction, accelerated B-cell senescence, T-cell metabolic inflexibility, insulin resistance, and dysregulated immunometabolism. Importantly, influenza and COVID-19 vaccines remain highly effective in reducing severe disease, hospitalization, and mortality among individuals with obesity, supporting continued vaccination in this population. Collectively, the available evidence indicates that conventional serological measures alone are insufficient to evaluate vaccine performance in obesity. Future studies should integrate assessments of antibody durability, neutralizing capacity, cellular immunity, and immune memory while considering obesity severity and metabolic phenotype as well as vaccine platform, vaccination stage, previous infection, and the timing of immune assessment to guide optimized vaccination strategies and booster schedules.

title: Systemic and oral adverse effects of semaglutide reported in randomized controlled trials: a scoping review.
abstract: To map the systemic and oral adverse events (AEs) of semaglutide reported in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). This scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Only english-language and RCTs were considered. A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from 2019 until 2025. Of 630 identified records (300 in PubMed, 312 in Scopus, and 18 in Web of Science), 12 studies were included after screening. The review identified systemic AEs of semaglutide, primarily gastrointestinal events like nausea (12 studies) and diarrhea (11 studies). Less frequent effects included pancreatitis (5 studies), hepatobiliary (3 studies) and gallbladder disease (3 studies), dental caries (1 study) and dry mouth (1 study). Subcutaneous administration predominating (7 studies), followed by oral (3) and mixed routes (2), over treatment durations of 21-68 weeks and 4-9 weeks of follow-up. Additionally, systemic events such as nasopharyngitis (5 studies), COVID-19 (5 studies), and metabolic or nutrition-related disorders were reported in all 12 studies. Importantly, none of the included studies directly investigated oral or dental outcomes. Semaglutide demonstrated an overall favorable safety profile in the included randomized controlled trials, with adverse events predominantly gastrointestinal. However, the RCTs did not provide direct evidence regarding oral health outcomes. Therefore, the available evidence is insufficient to draw conclusions about oral adverse events associated with semaglutide, highlighting the need for randomized clinical trials specifically designed to assess oral health outcomes in patients receiving GLP-1 receptor agonists.

title: Beta-Amino Alcohols as Key Frameworks in Drug Discovery: A Review of Medicinal Applications and Biological Profiles.
abstract: Beta-Amino alcohols, as pivotal frameworks in organic and medicinal chemistry, play a prominent role in drug design and development. This comprehensive review evaluates the therapeutic potential of β-amino alcohols, highlighting their significance in the management of a broad spectrum of human pathologies, including cancer, bacterial infections, malaria, and viral diseases. Furthermore, the efficacy of these molecules in cardiovascular, respiratory, and ocular disorders is assessed. Alongside their therapeutic applications, the epoxide ring-opening process, the primary and most established synthetic pathway for constructing β-amino alcohol cores, is critically discussed and integrated with structure activity relationship (SAR) insights to demonstrate how specific chemical modifications dictate pharmacological potency. The consolidated findings reveal that β-amino alcohols exert their therapeutic effects through diverse molecular mechanisms. These pathways encompass the suppression of malignant cell proliferation, potent bactericidal activity against resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains, inhibition of Plasmodium species in malaria, targeting the main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 for COVID-19 therapeutics, and functioning as dual-binding cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease management. Additionally, these derivatives have been reported to modulate adrenergic receptors, highlighting their potential relevance to cardiovascular, respiratory, and ocular therapeutic research, including conditions such as hypertension, asthma, and glaucoma. Overall, this review provides an up-to-date analysis of β-amino alcohol-based therapeutic applications and offers a new perspective on the potential role of these compounds in modern medicinal chemistry, which may contribute to the rational design of novel drug candidates.

title: Molecular profiling of repeated self-sampled blood reveals dynamic immune phenotypes in young adults
abstract: Abstract Although population-based studies of circulating blood proteins have provided profound insight into human biology, transient changes to time-dependent exposures often remain elusive. Here, we perform a longitudinal dried blood spot (DBS) self-sampling study in 808 young adults (aged 24–27, 64% females) from the Swedish Barn [Children], Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm Epidemiology cohort. In total, we collected ~2400 samples from 2020 to 2022. Each sample was profiled for SARS-CoV-2 serological, anti-interferon autoantibodies (AAbs), and 365 inflammation-related proteins. We subsequently linked these samples to registry-confirmed infection and vaccination exposures, physiological traits, genetic variation, and blood counts. We show that data-driven seroclustering captures the response to both infection and vaccination exposures, while stable AAbs against interferon receptors IFNAR1 and IFNGR2 associate with the duration of self-reported COVID-19 symptoms. Genome-wide mapping reveals 664 protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) across 65 proteins, with cis -pQTLs associated proteins showing greater longitudinal stability. Paired pre- and post-exposure samples indicate temporal changes in protein levels after infection (LAP3) and vaccination (TIMP3). This multi-molecular epidemiological profiling of self-sampled blood captures dynamic immune trajectories and shorter-term variability in a population of young adults.

title: [Gender and age characteristics of cases of disability during the pandemic of coronavirus infection in Moscow].
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been a global stress factor for population health in most countries, including Russia. The high prevalence and economic burden of diseases make it important to study the regional characteristics of population morbidity among different population groups. The aim of this study was to identify the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on temporary disability cases among residents of Moscow by gender and age, based on data from a primary healthcare organization. The assessment was based on data from 2019 to 2024. The dynamics of the total number of disability cases from 2019 to 2024, as well as their distribution by gender and age categories, were analyzed. The «disability coefficient» was calculated for the entire attached population and for specific gender and age groups. The average duration of days of disability due to respiratory diseases during the study period was also evaluated. It can be stated that the female part of the working population was more likely to apply for disability leaves, and the 35-49 age group had the highest number of temporary disability cases. There were no significant differences in the duration of temporary disability cases between men and women.
