title: Safety and ragional differences of Isatuximab- pomalidomide-dexamethasone combination in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: an external validation using FAERS and Lecheng real-world database
abstract: Abstract Isatuximab approved by FDA in 2020 for the treatment of relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM), although ICARIA-MM trial established its efficacy, leaving gap in different regional healthcare systems and reporting methodologies. This study investigated the AE profile of Isatuximab combined with pomalidomide-dexamethasone (Isa-Pd), focusing on safety of Isa-Pd, and regional differences between Lecheng and French in FAERS (FR). Lecheng data (2022Q3–2024Q2) were extracted from a prospective observational real-world study in China (IsaFiRsT), while FAERS reports (2020Q1–2025Q4) were obtained from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database. AE terms were standardized using MedDRA, and data mining used ROR, PRR, BCPNN, and MGPS algorithms. Our study divided into 2 parts: 1. Analysis all Isa-Pd-related data in FAERS and Lecheng. Comparing the database of French in FAERS with Lecheng to get regional differences. A total of 507 AE reports were analyzed, with 200 reports from Lecheng and FR used for regional comparison. Strong overall signals included infections and infestations, blood/lymphatic system disorders, investigations, and cardiac disorders. Beyond known hematological toxicities, this study identified unexpected risk signals, including cardiac failure, hypertension, hypokalemia, and Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, which are not fully characterized in current prescribing information. No specific fatal risk was attributed to Isa-Pd. Regional differences were observed between Lecheng and FR: Lecheng group had more males (Lecheng 62.5% vs FR 48.21%), and lderly patients(≥65 years: Lecheng 70.45% vs FR 58.93%). AEs reported group show difference, all data in Lecheng by physicians, and FR data reported almost equally by pharmacist (56.25%) and physician (42.86%). Lecheng shows frequent hospitalization (100%) in outcome, while FR showed a broader outcome spectrum (hospitalization 53.57%, Life-Threatening 12.50%, death 4.5%). Onset was shorter in Lecheng (Median Lecheng 9.50 vs FR 13.50), Lecheng AE signals concentrated in Investigations (Neutrophil count decreased, ROR=172.21; Platelet count decreased, ROR=22.75). FR group AE signals distributed across Blood and lymphatic system disorders (Lymphopenia, ROR=58.15; Neutropenia, ROR=31.76), Infections and infestations (COVID-19, ROR=12.11), and Vascular disorders (Hypertension, ROR=18.28). These regional differences may be related to population variations, regional management, and distinct post-AE medication regimens. Crucially, by introducing a prospective local real-world cohort (Lecheng) as an external validation for FAERS, this study overcomes the inherent under-reporting biases of spontaneous systems. It comprehensively characterizes the Isa-Pd safety profile, uncovers unexpected risks, and provides robust pharmacological evidence for individualized safety monitoring and risk mitigation.

title: An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antibody design
abstract: The capacity of an antibody to recognize and bind an antigen with high specificity and strength (i.e., its binding affinity) is a key determinant in the design and optimization of neutralizing antibodies against pathogenic targets. Here we introduce Ab-Affinity, a fine-tuned protein language model (PLM) that predicts the binding affinity of an antibody against a target peptide within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Cross-validation results shows that that Ab-Affinity outperforms other PLM-based affinity predictors when evaluated on a held-out validation and independent test sets. When integrated with a genetic algorithm and simulated annealing for sequence diversification and fitness optimization, Ab-Affinity enables the generation of candidate antibodies exhibiting over 100-fold improvement in predicted binding affinity relative to its parental (natural) antibody. More broadly, antibodies designed with Ab-Affinity attain higher predicted binding affinities than those produced by alternative mutational strategies, yielding synthetic antibodies with favorable predicted biophysical characteristics. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations for the strongest synthetic candidates indicate enhanced interactions and increased stability with the target peptide epitope within the spike protein. Experimental validation in vitro for a top-ranked candidate reveals an apparent increase in binding relative to its parental antibody. All model weights, source code, and analysis pipelines are publicly released to allow full reproducibility.

title: An Engineered Thio‐Amino Polymer Achieves Potent, Safe, and Broad Cell Type Delivery in the Lung Mapped by Spatial Transcriptomics
abstract: Efficient delivery of nucleic acids to the lung has the potential to impact future respiratory treatments. Current formulations exhibit significant limitations, including insufficient potency, single-cell delivery characterizations, efficacy demonstrations in disease models, and toxicology assessments. Here we describe polymer 81 (P81), which, when used with hypotonic solvents, is 34.1- to 77.8-fold more potent than previous polymers with various cargos for lung transfection by nebulized mRNA. Through the exploration of multiple routes of administration, P81 demonstrated a wide of range of cell-type delivery, including bronchial airway epithelial cells, tracheal basal stem cells, and 54% of all cells in the distal lung, assessed via single-cell spatial transcriptomics. Robust expression of mRNA-encoded antibodies in the lung by P81 enabled quantification of target protein and successful suppression of SARS-CoV-2 infection. The toxicology assessments of multiple doses of P81 polyplexes via nebulization in rodents were unremarkable. Overall, P81 represents a step forward for inhaled nucleic acid delivery to the respiratory tract, positioning itself as an efficient, safe, and translatable delivery formulation.

title: Lipoplex Nanoparticle-Based RNA Delivery to 3D Melanoma Spheroids.
abstract: Lipoplex nanoparticle-based vaccination technologies have shown tremendous efficiency for in vivo transfection during the COVID-19 pandemic and also hold promise for treating melanoma. While pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics need careful in vivo and clinical testing, other parameters of drug performance can be assessed with in vitro systems as well. Spheroids composed of more than one cell type can serve to assess drug penetration, cell-type specificity, and transfection efficiency at an early stage of drug development.

title: Incidence, shedding, and transmission of common respiratory viruses: data from a prospective, longitudinal, household cohort study in the Gambia from March 2021-June 2022.
abstract: Background Respiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet little is known about their incidence, risk factors, and transmission dynamics in community settings. We aimed to compare the epidemiology of multiple respiratory viruses within households in the Gambia. Methods We conducted a prospective household cohort study in a peri-urban region of the Gambia. Households with ≥5 members, including at least one adult and one child, were enrolled and followed for one year. Upper respiratory tract swabs were collected weekly, regardless of symptoms, and tested by RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, seasonal coronaviruses, human rhinovirus (HRV), influenza A/B, RSV A/B, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, and adenovirus. We estimated incidence, symptomatic fraction, shedding duration, and household secondary attack rates (SARs), and explored associations with virus type and demographic variables. Findings From 2 March 2021 to 13 June 2022, 349 participants from 52 households completed 14,421 scheduled and 129 unscheduled visits. Respiratory viruses were detected in 11.1% of visits (n = 1611), representing 1423 infection episodes. HRV was most common, infecting 86.5% of participants (2.4 infections per person-year). Children aged Interpretation A large burden of asymptomatic infections underlies the circulation of respiratory viruses within households, with key differences in incidence, shedding and transmission across viral species. Funding This study was funded through a UK Research and Innovation grant.

title: A coronavirus protease activates sensory neurons via TRPA1 to drive sneeze, cough, and pain.
abstract: Sneezing, coughing, and pain are common symptoms of respiratory viral infection. These responses are initiated by airway-innervating nociceptors that detect noxious stimuli, but how SARS-CoV-2 activates these neurons remains unclear. Here, we show that the coronavirus papain-like protease (PLpro) directly activates airway-innervating nociceptors in mice and human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived nociceptors. PLpro triggers sneezing, coughing, acute pain, and calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) release in the airways. Both the proteolytic activity of PLpro and the host ion channel transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) are required for neuronal activation and sneezing. Infection with the mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 or the murine coronavirus MHV-A59 also induces sneezing in mice, and MHV-A59-evoked sneezing is TRPA1-dependent. SARS-CoV-2 infection of the trigeminal ganglia altered transcriptional programs associated with nociception, including upregulation of the TRPA1-CGRP signaling pathway activated by PLpro. Together, these findings reveal a direct mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 triggers pain and airway reflexes and identify PLpro and TRPA1 as potential therapeutic targets for COVID-19.

source_records.abstract: Sneezing, coughing, and pain are common symptoms of respiratory viral infection. These responses are initiated by airway-innervating nociceptors that detect noxious stimuli, but how SARS-CoV-2 activates these neurons remains unclear. title: Discrimination of ranges of closely related RNA targets using CRISPR-based detection assay developed using machine learning-based optimization
abstract: Abstract Early detection and identification of pathogen strains are crucial for mitigating infectious disease threats, including those posed by closely related zoonotic variants. A key limitation of current molecular detection approaches is their narrow focus on individual targets, which can delay recognition of outbreaks caused by closely related but non-identical pathogens. Here we report a two-channel CRISPR/Cas13a detection assay capable of discriminating between SARS-CoV-2 and a panel of twelve closely related zoonotic sarbecoviruses using a compact duplex assay format. Guide RNA sets with tunable specificity were designed using a two-stage machine learning pipeline: initial candidate filtering with a pre-existing RuleFit model, followed by retraining on 382 sarbecovirus-specific in vitro data points to refine the mismatch threshold from 4 to 6 mismatches for target exclusion. The optimized assay achieved proof-of-concept three-way classification of synthetic RNA targets into: (1) SARS-CoV-2, (2) the closest known near-neighbor BANAL-236, and (3) remaining zoonotic near-neighbors, with a limit of detection of 15–150 fM for synthetic RNA targets. This approach provides a practical framework for surveillance-oriented detection that identifies not only a specific pathogen but also its closest relatives, provided that system-specific validation and model retraining are included for new target systems.

title: Modeling and simulation methods used in the maritime industry: evolution, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. The study demonstrates that M&S techniques enable safer, more efficient, and more environmentally sustainable operations, validated by scientific standards. The COVID-19 pandemic served as a critical catalyst, consolidating the strategic value of M&S as a central component of maritime resilience and innovation. This research traces the evolution of M&S adoption from 2010 to 2025, identifying four dominant research directions: maritime simulators, computational fluid dynamics (CFD)/finite element analysis (FEA), digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based methods. The analysis reveals that while traditional approaches dominated the 2010-2020 period, emerging technologies—particularly digital twins and AI-based methods—have accelerated exponentially since 2020, reflecting the maritime industry's accelerated digitalization. Forward projections through 2035 indicate that AI-based methodologies will experience the highest growth rate at approximately 329%, followed by digital twins at 147%, underscoring the fundamental transformation of maritime research and practice. The integration of these advanced modeling approaches offers optimal equilibrium between physical precision and computational efficiency for addressing complex maritime challenges.

title: Cas13d-mediated viral RNA degradation leads to potent antiviral control against both positive and negative sense RNA viruses
abstract: Respiratory viral infections continue to pose a substantial global health challenge, with a pressing need for effective treatment options. The rapid mutation rate of RNA viruses presents a significant risk of escape from existing treatments. Here, we harness the rapid adaptability and high sequence specificity of the RNA-targeting CRISPR-Cas13 nuclease technology to target and cleave the genome of different RNA viruses, disrupting replication and impairing propagation. We identified potent CRISPR-RfxCas13d/crRNA (Cas13d/crRNA) combinations that can efficiently restrict viral replication in both pre- and post-viral exposure treatment settings. In vitro treatment with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) co-encapsulating Cas13d mRNA and crRNAs targeting coding and non-coding regions of positive-sense (+) RNA coronaviruses including SARS-CoV-2 effectively inhibited viral replication. In addition, both pre- and post-viral exposure treatments with the LNP-Cas13d/crRNA against the negative-sense (−) RNA Nipah virus resulted in 99% restriction of this highly pathogenic virus. Hence, the Cas13d/crRNA antiviral method holds promise as a potential therapeutic approach against severe viral infections caused by both (+) and (−) RNA viruses. Furthermore, the multi-locus targeting of viruses by Cas13d could offer a possibility to prevent virus breakthrough and increase the therapeutic arsenal against many emerging RNA viruses in the future.

title: Dual mechanisms of ribonucleases in pathogen-host interactions
abstract: Abstract Ribonucleases (RNases) are fundamental regulators of RNA metabolism that function as both virulence determinants and host defense effectors. During infection, pathogens exploit RNase activities to ensure replication fidelity, reprogram host gene expression, and evade immune surveillance, whereas hosts deploy RNase arsenal to restrict pathogen proliferation and amplify antimicrobial signaling. Despite extensive characterization of individual enzymes, an integrated mechanistic framework spanning viral and bacterial systems remains elusive, and the therapeutic potential of targeting conserved RNA processing pathways is underexplored. Here, we systematically describe RNase-mediated mechanisms across representative pathogens, including severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, influenza A virus, Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa . Viral strategies that ensure genome integrity, degrade immunostimulatory RNAs, and silence host immune gene expression are outlined, along with bacterial systems wherein RNases coordinate virulence gene expression, metabolic adaptation, and the transition between acute and chronic infection states. Host countermeasures, ranging from membrane disruption and RNA decay pathways to ribotoxic stress responses, are further explored. By revealing the convergent evolutionary principles of RNA metabolism hijacking and the double-edged nature of shared enzymatic pathways, this review highlights the spatiotemporal precision of RNA processing as a potential therapeutic target for combating antimicrobial resistance and emerging viral variants.

title: A central hub model for remote delivery of multisite clinical trial interventions.
abstract: Digital health technologies enable remote delivery of clinical interventions, creating opportunities to redesign multisite trials. Traditional trials require participating sites to deliver interventions independently, potentially increasing implementation variability and operational complexity. Centralized models instead allow local recruitment and assessments while coordinating intervention delivery through one hub. We describe the feasibility of this model in RECOVER-NEURO, an NIH-funded, five-arm phase 2 randomized trial overseen by the Duke Clinical Research Institute. The trial enrolled 328 participants across 22 US sites with cognitive symptoms associated with long COVID. Sites conducted recruitment, consent, and clinical assessments, while an NYU Langone Health hub managed study kit preparation and distribution, device programming, onboarding, remote supervision, adherence monitoring, and equipment recovery. Participants were randomized to BrainHQ cognitive training alone; BrainHQ plus cognitive rehabilitation (PASC-CoRE), delivered via telehealth by Mount Sinai and Emory University investigators; BrainHQ plus active transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS); BrainHQ plus sham tDCS; or non-adaptive computer-based puzzles and games as an active comparator. Interventions were delivered remotely over 10 weeks using home-based study kits. Participants completed a mean of 44.0 ± 10.9 sessions over 68.8 ± 11.3 days. Of 320 participants who received intervention, 260 (81.3%) were consistently adherent. The hub initiated intervention within 13.5 ± 6.1 days of first participant contact, supported up to 168 concurrently active participants, and achieved a 96.9% equipment return rate. The intervention phase was completed in 375 days. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of centralized remote delivery of digital and device-based interventions in a large multisite trial and may inform future decentralized or hybrid clinical trials. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05965739.

title: A Structured Decision-Support Framework for Technology Adoption to Advance Airport Sustainability and Resilience
abstract: Airports face challenges in integrating sustainability and resilience into their long-term operational plans due to climate change, regulatory mandates, financial constraints, and disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic. While technology adoption plays a key role in addressing these issues, many airports lack structured strategies for evaluating, selecting, and implementing sustainability and resilience-focused innovations. Technology is often adopted reactively, driven by crises or regulatory compliance, rather than through proactive, strategic planning. This study introduces an empirically supported decision-support framework that combines established technology adoption models, sustainability and resilience assessment logic, and airport-specific implementation needs into a structured process for sustainable and resilient technology adoption. The framework synthesizes engineering-based maturity assessment, strategic planning, cross-disciplinary implementation, and Envision-based sustainability and resilience criteria, providing a tool that merges engineering judgment with organizational, regulatory, and environmental considerations. It equips airport decision-makers with a practical methodology for aligning technological innovation with operational performance, sustainability objectives, and long-term adaptability. The framework was empirically supported through expert input and statistical analyses of survey responses representing 27 commercial airports across the United States. An illustrative case study demonstrates an application of the framework by translating strategic sustainability and resilience goals into actionable implementation steps. This study contributes to the body of knowledge by presenting an evidence-based decision-support methodology that bridges the gap among strategic commitments and implementation, supports decarbonization, operational resilience, and infrastructure sustainability, while providing practical guidance for planners, sustainability leaders, and policymakers.

title: Functional Recovery and Healthcare Seeking Among Adults with Persistent Post-COVID Symptoms in Astana, Kazakhstan
abstract: Background: Recovery of everyday functioning and medical care seeking are complementary dimensions of persistent symptoms after COVID-19. We examined their relationship among adults surveyed in Astana, Kazakhstan. Methods: A secondary analysis was conducted using a cross-sectional web survey collected from 1 May 2025 to 1 February 2026. Of 408 respondents, 318 adults met eligibility criteria, 258 provided a definite symptom-persistence response, and 74 reported symptoms lasting more than 12 weeks. Functional responses were cross-tabulated with healthcare seeking. Proportions were summarized with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and exploratory associations with unadjusted prevalence ratios (PRs). Results: Among the 74 participants, 31 (41.9%) reported at least moderate quality-of-life impact and 37 (50.0%) had sought medical care. Incomplete activity recovery was reported by 38 of 69 participants with a definite response (55.1%). Care seeking was more frequent with incomplete than complete recovery (24/38 versus 11/31; 63.2% versus 35.5%; PR 1.78, 95% CI 1.04-3.03). Fourteen of 38 participants with incomplete recovery had not sought care (36.8%, 95% CI 23.4-52.7), as had 14 of 31 with at least moderate quality-of-life impact (45.2%, 95% CI 29.2-62.2). Conclusion: Persistent post-COVID symptoms were frequently accompanied by incomplete functional recovery. Although care seeking was more common among participants with incomplete recovery, over one-third of this group had not sought help. Assessing return to usual activity alongside symptom persistence can support a more complete appraisal of post-COVID burden in primary care.

title: Visual discrimination down to the analytical limit of detection in colorimetric lateral flow biosensors via streamlined image processing.
abstract: For point-of-care diagnostics, the visual limit of detection (LOD) is a critical parameter directly affecting diagnostic accuracy, as clinical decisions rely heavily on naked-eye classification. Improving visual detection while maintaining operational simplicity is highly advantageous for clinical testing. Here, colorimetric lateral flow biosensors for SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein (N-protein) and Streptococcus pyogenes antigen (Strep-A) were employed as models. The effect of N-protein concentration was studied in the range of 0-300 pM. The analytical LOD, determined both by longitudinal intensity profiling with subsequent test zone peak area integration, and by fixed region-of-interest analysis, was approximately 2 pM, whereas the visual LOD was 10-15 times higher (about 20-30 pM). Similar results were obtained for Strep-A. Within this concentration gap, human visual perception fails to resolve the colorimetric signal, leading to false-negative readouts despite the analyte level exceeding the analytical LOD. We demonstrate that a streamlined workflow based on histogram equalization of sensing membrane digital images reliably resolves subvisual, true analytical signals, effectively bridging the gap between the visual and analytical LOD. By redistributing pixel intensities via a cumulative distribution function, this process amplifies subtle reflectance intensity differences that remain imperceptible to the human eye. Robustness studies confirm that this resolution enhancement remains effective across both uncompressed TIFF and compressed JPEG formats, with compressed blank controls (0 pM) remaining free from non-specific signals. Because it operates exclusively on digital records without modifying the physical sensor architecture, this accessible, data-validated strategy can be combined with chemical signal-amplification methods to achieve synergistic performance improvement effects.

The analytical LOD, determined both by longitudinal intensity profiling with subsequent test zone peak area integration, and by fixed region-of-interest analysis, was approximately 2 pM, whereas the visual LOD was 10-15 times higher (about 20-30 pM). Similar results were obtained for Strep-A. Within this concentration gap, human visual perception fails to resolve the colorimetric signal, leading to false-negative readouts despite the analyte level exceeding the analytical LOD. We demonstrate that a streamlined workflow based on histogram equalization of sensing membrane digital images reliably resolves subvisual, true analytical signals, effectively bridging the gap between the visual and analytical LOD. By redistributing pixel intensities via a cumulative distribution function, this process amplifies subtle reflectance intensity differences that remain imperceptible to the human eye. Robustness studies confirm that this resolution enhancement remains effective across both uncompressed TIFF and compressed JPEG formats, with compressed blank controls (0 pM) remaining free from non-specific signals. Because it operates exclusively on digital records without modifying the physical sensor architecture, this accessible, data-validated strategy can be combined with chemical signal-amplification methods to achieve synergistic performance improvement effects.

title: Synthesis of ADP‐Ribose Mimetics as Potent Inhibitors for the Coronavirus Hydrolase Mac1
abstract: ABSTRACT We describe the design and synthesis of α‐azido‐4‐thioribose and α‐epoxycarbaribose‐based adenosine diphosphate ribose (ADP‐ribose) analogs as potent inhibitors of the SARS‐CoV‐2 macrodomain Mac1. The α‐epoxycarbaribose was designed to emulate the structure of the distal ribose of ADPr, which adopts an E 3 conformation during hydrolysis and release from the target protein. In addition, a sulfonyl carbamate linker and the remdesivir‐inspired nucleobase GS‐441524 were incorporated into our designs to increase inhibitor lipophilicity and potency, respectively. The α‐epoxycarbaribose GS‐441524 pyrophosphate was identified as the most potent Mac1 inhibitor to date, exhibiting low‐nanomolar affinity. Replacing pyrophosphate with the less polar sulfonyl carbamate linker yielded an inhibitor with an IC50 of 19 nM. Analysis of co‐crystal structures of Mac1 and its inhibitors showed that the epoxide is intact and revealed that the sulfonyl carbamate linker positions itself to mimic pyrophosphate binding.

title: Genomics in Action: Zambia’s Path Toward Integrated Pathogen Surveillance
abstract: Genomic surveillance is increasingly central to public health, and the Africa CDC calls on African Union Member States to integrate genomics into national health systems. This editorial reflects on the 2nd Zambia Genomics Symposium, held on 27 and 28 August 2026 under the theme of integrating AI and One Health for enhanced pathogen surveillance, and considers where Zambia's surveillance system stands. Zambia has strengthened sequencing capacity, trained a growing cadre of molecular biologists and bioinformaticians, and formed the Zambia Genomic Sequencing Consortium. Local research now spans wastewater surveillance, antimicrobial resistance, viral genomics, and the microbiome, including work on hypervirulent and multidrug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and on SARS-CoV-2 variants. The authors argue that the defining challenge is not generating evidence but translating it into routine surveillance, policy, and frontline action, held back by concentrated sequencing capacity, a stretched bioinformatics workforce, and maturing data governance. They call on government to prioritise genomic surveillance with dedicated budgets and clear governance, on universities to embed genomics and bioinformatics early in curricula, on partners to align funding with national priorities, and on scientists to keep publishing and collaborating.

title: Univariate Time Series Forecasting of ED Admissions and Hospital Discharges with Prophet and Azure Databricks MLflow.
abstract: Goal Bed capacity is a key limitation for patient throughput at high trauma-level hospitals. By leveraging existing operational data and incorporating relatively simple quantitative methodology, future bed balancing can be predicted primarily via forecasting of incoming ED admissions and hospital discharges. These predictions can inform a number of key decisions related to bed planning, potentially enhancing provider satisfaction and mitigating negative patient outcomes. Methods Univariate time series forecasting with the Prophet procedure was applied to generate daily forecasts of admissions and discharges over a 28-day period at Vanderbilt University Adult Hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, the largest facility within the Vanderbilt University Medical Center system. Models for ED admissions and hospital discharges were each developed independently as custom-built and Automated Machine Learning (AutoML)-produced models, respectively. Principal findings Both models performed well in terms of accurately producing 28-day forecasts, compared to naive alternatives, and were expected to improve as historical data become more available. Although these models were limited by a lack of consistent data availability due to the emergency response during the COVID-19 pandemic years, they were effective in improving the accuracy of bed balancing estimates by hospital operations staff with relative ease, regarding model development and operational application. Practical applications Although simple, univariate models benefit from relatively trivial data requirements and adequate time to implement operationally. This cost-effective approach provides an effective solution for health systems seeking to support bed-planning efforts.

title: Total Shared Knowledge: An Actionable Measure Linking Patient Safety Culture and Safety Outcomes Data.
abstract: Goal Patient safety culture is vital for improving healthcare outcomes, but its practical application faces theoretical and empirical challenges. This study proposes total shared knowledge (TSK) among staff as a novel, actionable measure for patient safety culture that healthcare leaders can use to enhance team dynamics and performance. Grounded in an adaptive culture framework, this study examined TSK's relationship with safety outcomes across 42 inpatient units in five hospitals (N = 1,363 staff). Methods This study employed a mixed-design approach, incorporating both longitudinal and cross-sectional data. TSK was quantified using 12 composites from the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality Hospital Survey on Patient Safety Culture collected in late 2018. This was matched with 2 years of monthly safety outcomes data from a hospital event-reporting system (January 2018-December 2019, minimizing potential COVID-19 bias). Negative binomial regression was used to model the relationship of TSK and safety outcomes, and a mixed-effects location scale analysis was used to model within-and-between unit variation in safety outcomes. Principal findings Findings show that higher TSK is significantly associated with fewer reported safety events (β = -0.37, p = .0031). Specifically, a one-composite increase in TSK was linked to a reduction of approximately 5.1 safety events per unit per month. Furthermore, greater TSK was associated with reduced variability in outcomes (τ = -0.51, p = .007), with a one-standard-deviation increase in TSK leading to a 47% decrease in within-unit variation, suggesting improved predictability. Practical applications These results highlight the strategic value of leveraging safety culture data to guide team-specific interventions and allocate organizational resources more effectively. By reframing safety culture as shared knowledge, this study offers healthcare managers a theory-informed, data-driven approach to significantly enhance organizational safety performance and predictability.

title: ARE-Wochenbericht des RKI KW45
abstract: Die Aktivität akuter respiratorischer Erkrankungen (ARE) in der Bevölkerung ist in der 45. KW im Vergleich zur Vorwoche gestiegen und befindet sich auf einem moderaten Niveau. Im ambulanten Bereich ist die Zahl der Arztbesuche wegen ARE in der 45. KW im Vergleich zur Vorwoche stabil geblieben und lag weiterhin auf einem moderaten Niveau. Im Nationalen Referenzzentrum (NRZ) für Influenzaviren wurden in der 45. KW 2026 in insgesamt 67 der 126 eingesandten Sentinelproben respiratorische Viren identifiziert, darunter hauptsächlich Rhino-/Enteroviren (33 %), gefolgt von Influenzaviren (A und B) (10 %). Zudem wurden unter anderem SARS-CoV-2 (3 %) und Respiratorische Synzytialviren (RSV; 1 %) in der 45. Im stationären Bereich ist die Inzidenz schwerer akuter respiratorischer Infektionen (SARI) unter Berücksichtigung von erwarteten weiteren SARI-Diagnosen (Nowcasting) in der 45. KW 2026 weiterhin stabil geblieben und lag auf einem niedrigen Niveau. Es erhielten jeweils 4 % der SARI-Patientinnen eine COVID-19- bzw. Der Anteil der RSV-Diagnosen lag unter 1 %. In der virologischen SARI-Surveillance des NRZ für Influenzaviren wurden in der 45. KW 2026 hauptsächlich Rhino-/Enteroviren nachgewiesen. Die Zahl der an das RKI gemäß IfSG übermittelten Fälle mit Influenzavirusinfektion ist in der 45. Meldewoche (MW) 2026 im Vergleich zur 44. MW erneut gestiegen. Die Influenza-Fallzahlen zeigten einen ähnlichen Verlauf wie im letzten Jahr um diese Zeit. Die COVID-19-Fallzahlen sind im Vergleich zur Vorwoche ebenfalls angestiegen, es wurden bisher deutlich weniger Fälle im Vergleich zur Vorsaison übermittelt. Die Zahl der RSV-Infektionen blieb in der 45. MW weiterhin niedrig. Die rekombinante SARS-CoV-2-Variante XFG wurde in der 43. KW 2026 erneut am häufigsten unter den zirkulierenden SARS-CoV-2-Linien detektiert. Die im Abwasser gemessene SARS-CoV-2-Last blieb weiterhin deutlich unter den Werten aus dem Vorjahr zu dieser Zeit, stieg jedoch in den letzten Monaten allmählich an. Auch die Influenzaviruslast ist in den letzten Wochen leicht gestiegen. Die RSV-Last im Abwasser blieb weiter niedrig.

title: Standardized Annotation of Quantitative Proteomics Datasets Using SDRF-Proteomics.
abstract: Proteomics datasets require detailed and standardized metadata annotation to ensure reproducibility, reusability, and alignment with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles. This chapter presents a practical, hands-on workflow for annotating a label-free proteomics dataset using the Sample and Data Relationship Format for Proteomics (SDRF-Proteomics), a HUPO-PSI and EuBIC-MS standard that has been adopted by major proteomics data repositories. We demonstrate the process on a COVID-19 nasal-swab dataset (PXD020394), showing how to derive sample and assay metadata from the study files, encode them in SDRF with the lesSDRF web application, and validate the result. Although the worked example is label-free, the approach can be generalized to other quantification strategies.

title: Targeted sequencing-based analysis of respiratory pathogen profiles in Shenzhen, China
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are caused by diverse viral, bacterial, and fungal pathogens and remain a major public health burden worldwide. Rapid and accurate identification of respiratory pathogens is important for clinical diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance. Shenzhen is a highly populated metropolitan city characterized by substantial population mobility and intensive domestic and international travel, which may influence the regional circulation patterns of respiratory pathogens. However, sequencing-based epidemiological data regarding respiratory pathogens in Shenzhen remain limited. Methods Clinical specimens from 392 patients with suspected RTIs who underwent targeted sequencing at Longgang District People’s Hospital of Shenzhen between 2023 and 2025 were analyzed using a respiratory pathogen targeted sequencing panel. Clinical information was retrospectively collected. Microorganism detection profiles, co-detection patterns, age-associated detection frequencies, and associations with clinical manifestations were analyzed. Results Among the 392 enrolled patients, at least one panel-targeted respiratory microorganism was detected in 273/392 samples (69.6%), whereas 119/392 samples (30.4%) were negative. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) was the most frequently detected microorganism, followed by influenza A(H1N1) virus, Klebsiella pneumoniae , Epstein-Barr virus, Haemophilus influenzae , and Streptococcus pneumoniae . Among the 273 positive samples, 195/273 (71.4%) showed single-microorganism detection, whereas 78/273 (28.6%) showed multiple-microorganism detection. Cough and fever were the most frequently observed symptoms across most microorganism groups. In addition, Bordetella pertussis and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were more frequently detected in younger patients, whereas Klebsiella pneumoniae , Aspergillus , and Epstein-Barr virus were more commonly detected in elderly individuals. The clinical relevance of some detected microorganisms should be interpreted cautiously, as their detection does not necessarily indicate active infection or etiological causality. Conclusion Targeted sequencing detected a diverse range of respiratory microorganisms in patients with suspected RTIs and provided regional data on their detection patterns in Shenzhen, China. These findings may contribute to respiratory pathogen surveillance, although individual sequencing results should be interpreted together with clinical and microbiological information when assessing etiological relevance.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) are caused by diverse viral, bacterial, and fungal pathogens and remain a major public health burden worldwide. Rapid and accurate identification of respiratory pathogens is important for clinical diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance. Shenzhen is a highly populated metropolitan city characterized by substantial population mobility and intensive domestic and international travel, which may influence the regional circulation patterns of respiratory pathogens. However, sequencing-based epidemiological data regarding respiratory pathogens in Shenzhen remain limited. Methods Clinical specimens from 392 patients with suspected RTIs who underwent targeted sequencing at Longgang District People’s Hospital of Shenzhen between 2023 and 2025 were analyzed using a respiratory pathogen targeted sequencing panel. Clinical information was retrospectively collected. Microorganism detection profiles, co-detection patterns, age-associated detection frequencies, and associations with clinical manifestations were analyzed. Results Among the 392 enrolled patients, at least one panel-targeted respiratory microorganism was detected in 273/392 samples (69.6%), whereas 119/392 samples (30.4%) were negative. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) was the most frequently detected microorganism, followed by influenza A(H1N1) virus, Klebsiella pneumoniae , Epstein-Barr virus, Haemophilus influenzae , and Streptococcus pneumoniae . Among the 273 positive samples, 195/273 (71.4%) showed single-microorganism detection, whereas 78/273 (28.6%) showed multiple-microorganism detection. Cough and fever were the most frequently observed symptoms across most microorganism groups. In addition, Bordetella pertussis and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were more frequently detected in younger patients, whereas Klebsiella pneumoniae , Aspergillus , and Epstein-Barr virus were more commonly detected in elderly individuals. The clinical relevance of some detected microorganisms should be interpreted cautiously, as their detection does not necessarily indicate active infection or etiological causality. Conclusion Targeted sequencing detected a diverse range of respiratory microorganisms in patients with suspected RTIs and provided regional data on their detection patterns in Shenzhen, China. These findings may contribute to respiratory pathogen surveillance, although individual sequencing results should be interpreted together with clinical and microbiological information when assessing etiological relevance.

title: 12 | Modelling and artificial intelligence to support vaccination planning, vaccine research and public guidance
abstract: Vaccination contributes to infection prevention and antimicrobial resistance control. Translating evidence into vaccination strategies requires tools to explore alternative scenarios, identify research priorities and communicate recommendations. We present three complementary approaches addressing these needs. Materials and Methods. SIVax is an age-structured mechanistic framework for generating synthetic influenza epidemic curves, epidemiological calibration and evaluation of alternative vaccination scenarios, informed by 16 pre-COVID-19 Italian surveillance seasons. A compartmental model of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), calibrated to Italian ECDC infection estimates for 2016-2020, explores hypothetical vaccine characteristics and transmission conditions. VaccinIAmoci is a conversational artificial intelligence system grounded in Italian institutional vaccination guidance and constrained to vaccination-related queries. Two domain experts independently evaluated its responses to 180 queries against a generic-prompt baseline. SIVax enabled exploration of how campaign timing and age-specific coverage could influence influenza incidence, while making calibration uncertainty and scenario assumptions explicit. The MRSA model provided conditional vaccine performance benchmarks, highlighting the importance of protection against acquisition and the constraints imposed by external reservoirs. VaccinIAmoci improved response accuracy and rejection of off-topic requests compared with the generic prompt, although residual errors concerned pregnancy and travel health. These findings illustrate distinct uses of modelling and artificial intelligence in vaccination planning, vaccine research and public communication. These approaches can make complex evidence more accessible for scenario analysis, research prioritisation and vaccination guidance. Their value depends on transparent assumptions, explicit uncertainty and appropriate validation. Model outputs represent conditional scenarios rather than forecasts or deployment thresholds, while chatbot performance requires real-world evaluation before conclusions can be drawn about vaccination uptake or health outcomes.

title: At the Interface: How Bat, Swine, and Bovine Reservoir Networks Shape Coronavirus Emergence in Human Populations
abstract: ABSTRACT Coronavirus emergence at the human–animal interface is shaped by interactions among ecological, evolutionary, molecular, and anthropogenic processes rather than by isolated spillover events. This review synthesizes evidence from three interconnected systems involving bats, swine, and cattle, integrating viral evolution, host susceptibility, production ecology, and human exposure into a comparative framework for zoonotic risk. The literature through 2026 was reviewed. Bats maintain extensive alpha ‐ and betacoronavirus diversity through long‐term host–virus associations, geographic structuring, and recombination. Swine can amplify diverse coronaviruses because of their susceptibility to multiple viral lineages, frequent viral co‐circulation, and dense transmission networks in intensive production systems. Bovine coronavirus represents a distinct but under‐surveilled system: it is globally distributed, evolutionarily related to human coronavirus OC43, and associated with occupational exposure among livestock workers. Across these systems, host switching depends on the combined effects of spike protein–receptor compatibility, host protease availability, cellular permissiveness, and immune evasion; no single molecular trait reliably predicts zoonotic emergence. Land‐use change, livestock intensification, wildlife trade, and global production networks further increase spillover opportunities by altering contact patterns and pathogen movement. Major surveillance gaps remain at livestock–wildlife–human interfaces, particularly in longitudinal serology, genomic sampling, and the integration of animal, human, environmental, and supply chain data. Key priorities include standardized occupational serosurveillance, genomic and metagenomic monitoring of high‐risk livestock systems, investigation of unexplained human febrile illness, and spatially explicit One Health early‐warning systems. Integrating reservoir dynamics, viral evolution, production ecology, and human exposure can improve early detection and strengthen preparedness for future zoonotic coronavirus emergence.

title: MSF-PSD: multi-scale features based panoptic segmentation and detection framework for lung disease classification
abstract: Complex anatomical variations and heterogeneous pathological patterns make it difficult to accurately segment lung images from Computed Tomography (CT) scans, especially in lungs affected by COVID-19. Conventional segmentation techniques often struggle to capture Panoptic Segmentation information and fine-grained structures across diverse clinical datasets. This study suggests a novel Multi-Scale Feature-based Panoptic Segmentation and Detection (MSF-PSD) framework for simultaneous lesion boundary detection and lung disease classification. To improve multi-scale feature representation, the suggested framework incorporates an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) and uses EfficientNet-B7 as its foundation. For hierarchical feature fusion, a Region Proposal Network (RPN) and Region of Interest (RoI) refinement with Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) are used after a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN). An end-to-end panoptic detection pipeline is made possible by three parallel prediction heads that carry out category classification, bounding box regression, and mask segmentation. The COVIDx-CT and SARS-CoV-2 datasets are preprocessed using Gaussian filtering and CLAHE to increase structural visibility. Supercomputing resources are utilised to guarantee scalable training and effective inference because multi-head learning and parallel feature extraction have high computational demands. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) localises discriminative pathological regions and improves model interpretability. MSF-PSD achieves 98.4% accuracy, 97.12% precision, 94.2% recall and 93.33% F1-score, demonstrating its efficacy and clinical potential for dependable automated COVID-19 screening and lung disease assessment.

title: 11 | Surveillance of communicable diseases and antimicrobial resistance through wastewater-based epidemiology: experiences in the Sicilian Region
abstract: Wastewater-Based Epidemiology (WBE) is an innovative public health surveillance approach that analyses wastewater to monitor infectious agents and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants at population level. In Sicily, WBE has progressively developed through poliovirus surveillance and expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, creating opportunities for integrated environmental surveillance. Materials and Methods. The Sicilian surveillance network included multiple sampling sites, including Palermo, Catania, Messina, Siracusa, Trapani and Ragusa, linked to laboratories participating in the surveillance system coordinated by the Italian National Institute of Health (ISS). SARS-CoV-2 monitoring involved collaboration among universities, healthcare institutions, laboratories and water service providers, within the framework of European Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/472. Further activities included participation in 2023 National Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (CCM) project investigating respiratory viruses in wastewater. Preliminary correlations between wastewater measurements and clinical surveillance indicators were assessed for respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and influenza viruses. The regional network was also considered for extension to AMR surveillance, in line with the Italian National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2022–2025 (PNCAR). During the COVID-19 pandemic, the regional network covered approximately 29.6% of Sicily’s population. Preliminary findings from CCM project involving the University of Palermo showed positive correlations between wastewater and clinical surveillance indicators for hRSV/A (r=0.513; p 0.05). The regional network reportedly covers 1,482,120 population equivalents, representing 29.6% of the regional population, and could provide a basis for monitoring antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). The Sicilian experience highlights WBE’s potential as an integrated regional surveillance infrastructure for infectious diseases and AMR determinants. Positive correlations for selected respiratory viruses support further evaluation of wastewater monitoring as a complement to clinical surveillance, although predictive performance and temporal relationships require validation. Future priorities include standardised procedures, sustained monitoring, quality assurance and integration of environmental, clinical and epidemiological data. Detection of ARGs should be interpreted cautiously, as it does not independently establish viable resistant pathogens or clinically expressed resistance.

title: Performance evaluation of face mask: from textile filtration determination to air leakage minimization
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic emphasized the critical role of face masks in preventing the transmission of respiratory viruses, especially in medical settings. Respiratory viruses, including SARS, influenza, and adenoviruses are primarily transmitted through the respiratory pathways, making face masks the primary barrier for protection. This study aims to evaluate and compare the filtration efficiency and pressure differentials of different face masks to contribute to the development of a comprehensive test bench for medical textiles. Unlike prior fit-testing approaches that assess mask fit only as a wearing condition, this study introduces a test bench that independently quantifies nasal and oral air leakage under controlled sealing configurations, providing a reproducible platform for evaluating custom sealing accessories. The design of a sealing device is also evaluated to assess the effectiveness of a physical external sealer. The study focuses on designing and evaluating accessory seals for face masks to determine air loss percentages in areas where the mask is not in complete contact with the face. The creation of a test bench for textiles in medical use is intended to contribute valuable insights into mask performance, addressing both filtration efficiency and pressure differentials. The study evaluates different face masks including N95, surgical, and newly developed fabrics. Results revealed that N95 masks consistently demonstrate superior filtration efficiency and acceptable pressure differentials across specific flow rates. Thus, understanding face mask efficacies is crucial for optimizing mask designs, contributing to the advancement of protective measures against respiratory diseases.

title: Development of a whole workflow for multiplexed diagnosis of viral respiratory infections
abstract: Abstract Endemic cold waves caused by SARS-CoV-2, Influenza and RSV challenge global health systems by co-circulation in the population. This requires appropriate pre-analytical workflows that obtain valid multi-virus diagnostic test results and ensure the reliability of downstream molecular analyses. Various pre-analytical parameters like specimen stabilization, virus infectivity inactivation and nasal sprays as interfering substances were examined. The BD transport swab system including the UVT medium was able to stabilize the nucleic acid copy numbers of the tested viruses at 37 °C for up to 96 h, even when supplemented with the virus inactivating reagent transport medium additive-P (TMA-P). Viruses infectivity were inactivated by TMA-P, TMA-D and benzalkoniumchloride (BAC). However, only BAC is usable in combination with the QIAprep& high-throughput system. Furthermore, TMA-P and BAC are compatible with sequencing. Additionally, external substances like nasal sprays used prior to sample collection may interfere with test results. The BD system supplemented with inactivating substances reduce the biosafety requirements for transport and analysis while ensuring valid test results including sequencing. The use of the direct PCR QIAprep& system in combination with the multi-target detection assays minimizes the specimens processing time. Overall, a rapid and reliable detection workflow of respiratory viruses was developed for clinically relevant pre-analytical scenarios.

title: Real-World Safety of Upadacitinib in Adults and Adolescents With Atopic Dermatitis: 12-Month Analysis of the Multicountry Observational AD-VISE Study
abstract: Introduction: Upadacitinib (UPA) is an oral selective Janus kinase inhibitor approved for the treatment of atopic dermatitis (AD) in adolescents and adults. Multiple clinical trials have reported on the efficacy and safety of UPA for the treatment of AD. AD-VISE is a real-world drug utilization cohort study of UPA in adolescent and adult patients with AD. Previously reported effectiveness analyses from the AD-VISE study have shown similar trends to those reported in clinical trials. Here we present the first real-world safety data through 12 months of treatment with UPA from the AD-VISE study. Methods: AD-VISE is an ongoing observational, prospective, multi-country study primarily evaluating the effectiveness of UPA (15 and 30 mg) in adults and adolescents with AD over a period of 2 years. Herein, we report the 12-month safety analysis, patients were followed until the earliest of one-year of UPA exposure or the UPA discontinuation date plus 30 days (data cutoff: Oct 17, 2025). Adverse events (AEs) are reported as number and percentage of patients experiencing an AE (n, %), and exposure adjusted event rate (events [E] per 100 patient-years [PYs]) for patients receiving any dose of UPA. The possibility of an AE being related to UPA was assessed by the investigators. Results: This analysis included 861 patients and a total of 757.4 PYs of exposure to UPA. A total of 441 (51.2%; 171.0 E/100PYs) patients experienced at least one AE, with 284 (33.0%; 74.1 E/100PYs) patients experiencing at least one AE with reasonable possibility of being related to UPA. Serious and severe AEs were experienced by 33 (3.8%; 6.7 E/100 PYs) and 30 (3.5%; 5.8 E/100 PYs) patients, respectively. AEs leading to discontinuation of UPA were experienced by 38 (4.4%; 8.3 E/100 PYs) patients. Serious AEs with a reasonable possibility of being UPA related were experienced by 10 (1.2%; 2.5 E/100 PYs) patients. No deaths or cases of malignancy excluding non-melanoma skin cancer were reported (n = 0; E = 0). Nineteen patients experienced at least one herpes zoster event (2.2%; 2.8 E/100 PYs). Cases of lymphoma, major adverse cardiovascular events, and venous thromboembolism were each reported once (each n = 1, 0.1%; 0.1 E/100 PYs). The most commonly reported AEs (occurring in ≥ 2% of patients, by preferred term) were acne (n = 94, 10.9%), upper respiratory tract infection (n = 61, 7.1%), continued or worsening of atopic dermatitis (n = 60, 7.0.%), COVID-19 (n = 58, 6.7%), herpes simplex (n = 23, 2.7%), headache (n = 22, 2.6%), nasopharyngitis (n = 21, 2.4%), and folliculitis (n = 18, 2.1%). Conclusion: These results of the real-world safety of UPA in patients with AD are consistent with the previously established UPA long-term safety profile in patients with AD in clinical trials.

A total of 441 (51.2%; 171.0 E/100PYs) patients experienced at least one AE, with 284 (33.0%; 74.1 E/100PYs) patients experiencing at least one AE with reasonable possibility of being related to UPA. Serious and severe AEs were experienced by 33 (3.8%; 6.7 E/100 PYs) and 30 (3.5%; 5.8 E/100 PYs) patients, respectively. AEs leading to discontinuation of UPA were experienced by 38 (4.4%; 8.3 E/100 PYs) patients. Serious AEs with a reasonable possibility of being UPA related were experienced by 10 (1.2%; 2.5 E/100 PYs) patients. No deaths or cases of malignancy excluding non-melanoma skin cancer were reported (n = 0; E = 0). Nineteen patients experienced at least one herpes zoster event (2.2%; 2.8 E/100 PYs). Cases of lymphoma, major adverse cardiovascular events, and venous thromboembolism were each reported once (each n = 1, 0.1%; 0.1 E/100 PYs). The most commonly reported AEs (occurring in ≥ 2% of patients, by preferred term) were acne (n = 94, 10.9%), upper respiratory tract infection (n = 61, 7.1%), continued or worsening of atopic dermatitis (n = 60, 7.0.%), COVID-19 (n = 58, 6.7%), herpes simplex (n = 23, 2.7%), headache (n = 22, 2.6%), nasopharyngitis (n = 21, 2.4%), and folliculitis (n = 18, 2.1%). Conclusion: These results of the real-world safety of UPA in patients with AD are consistent with the previously established UPA long-term safety profile in patients with AD in clinical trials.

title: Infectious Disease Horizon in Emerging Infectious Diseases
abstract: Emerging infectious diseases often spread freely before an outbreak is detected, yet the duration of this free-transmission period and the infection size accumulated during this period are difficult to quantify. These quantities directly affect forecasts of subsequent transmission dynamics, estimates of infection size, and decisions regarding prevention and control measures. In this study, we propose and compute the infectious disease horizon (IDH)-the time span from when an infectious disease begins spreading to when it is first detected-and examine its antecedents and consequences. First, based on the SEAIR free-transmission model, we derive transmission characteristics, including the generation interval, the serial interval, the basic reproduction number, and the effective reproduction number, and describe the incidence using a renewal equation. Second, by considering two detection routes, we further obtain the distribution and mean of the IDH under different detection settings and quantify the infection size at the time of outbreak detection. Third, intervention measures are incorporated to derive a post-detection transmission model with generally distributed stage durations, followed by the derivation of the corresponding model under exponentially distributed stage durations and the determination of the final infection size. Finally, under the exponential-distribution assumption, the model is applied to the COVID-19 outbreak in Xi'an. The unified framework developed in this study provides a theoretical basis for evaluating early surveillance capacity for emerging infectious diseases, optimizing testing strategies, and determining the intensity of prevention and control measures after outbreak detection.

title: When Text Complements the Return Path: A Strong Baseline for Behavioral Equity-Peer Retrieval
abstract: Which representation better identifies firms that will co-move with a public company next quarter after Fama–French five-factor (FF5) adjustment: what the firm says or how it has traded? We compare Form 10-K Item 1 excerpts of up to 8,000 characters available before each ranking date, represented by four frozen dense encoders and term-frequency–inverse-document-frequency (TF-IDF), with a date-indexed, unit-normalized path of standardized residual returns that has no learned retrieval parameters. Inner products between paths equal sample residual correlations. Across six modern tests (2024–2026), the path reaches normalized discounted cumulative gain at five (NDCG@5) of 0.336, versus 0.300 for TF-IDF and 0.279 for the best dense encoder; in these configurations, TF-IDF beats all four dense encoders. In a census of 1,301,691 firm pairs from one transition, filing similarity is only weakly aligned with same- or next-period residual co-movement (pairwise Spearman ρS approximately 0.049 or lower; the return path reaches 0.103 in the next period). Text nevertheless helps when return history is short: an 80%-return/20%-TF-IDF percentile-rank blend, selected on twelve earlier 2020–2024 transitions and then frozen, reaches 0.373 and improves on the path in all six tests, but adds no gain with four periods of return history, where the path alone reaches 0.430. Two nonlinear diagnostics selected under their respective historical-only protocols also fail to beat their corresponding frozen blends. Across 19 transitions spanning 2020–2026, the path beats TF-IDF in 18 of 19; the sole reversal is the transition out of the COVID-19 crash window. We propose the return path as a minimum baseline for learned behavioral-peer retrieval. The study uses a retrospectively assembled U.S. security panel, requires recent returns, and does not test valuation peers or trading outcomes.

title: Fibromyalgia Care Under Compounding National Crises in Lebanon: A Six-Year Longitudinal Study of Healthcare Utilization and Continuity
abstract: Background/Objectives: Fibromyalgia is a chronic, symptom-defined condition whose recognition and management depend on sustained access to care. Recorded utilization during crises may therefore reflect disrupted access, diagnostic recognition, and longitudinal engagement rather than disease burden. Since 2019, Lebanon has experienced overlapping financial deterioration, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut port explosion, and armed conflict. We characterized recorded fibromyalgia utilization and continuity across these six years. Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed all outpatient encounters with fibromyalgia as the primary diagnosis in electronic health records of the American University of Beirut Medical Center, January 2019–December 2024. Monthly encounter volume was the primary utilization outcome. Recorded continuity was evaluated as time from each patient’s index encounter to a subsequent fibromyalgia-coded encounter, with 180-day return as the principal standardized comparison across cohorts. Results: We identified 4969 encounters from 3237 patients (87.5% female; mean age, 46.7 years). Monthly encounter volume fell around the 2019 financial and banking disruption and remained below the preceding nine-month level (84.3 vs. 66.8 encounters/month; rate ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.61–0.94), with a further exploratory reduction in mid-2024. The 180-day probability of a subsequent encounter declined from 22.8% in the 2019 cohort to 15.6% in 2024 (hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.45–0.76); lower return rates emerged from the 2022 cohort onward. Conclusions: Recorded fibromyalgia utilization and recorded return for subsequent fibromyalgia-coded care within the same institution changed at different times during Lebanon’s compounding crises. These findings describe recorded care, not disease occurrence: recovering patient numbers may coexist with persistently lower recorded return within the institution, so aggregate utilization alone may incompletely describe recovery for continuity-dependent chronic conditions.

title: Long-Term Safety of Baricitinib in Pediatric Patients With Atopic Dermatitis Aged 2 to <18 Years With Up to 5.2 Years of Exposure
abstract: Introduction: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease that frequently begins in childhood and can significantly impact quality of life. Baricitinib, an oral selective Janus kinase inhibitor, has demonstrated efficacy and an acceptable safety profile in pediatric patients with moderate-to-severe AD in short- and intermediate-term analyses.1,2 However, comprehensive long-term safety data remain limited. This final analysis of BREEZE-AD-PEDS reports long-term safety data from pediatric patients treated with baricitinib for up to 5.2 years. Methods: BREEZE-AD-PEDS (NCT03952559) was a phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study. The study design included a long-term extension treatment period to evaluate longer-term safety in baricitinib-treated pediatric patients (aged 2 to <18 years) with moderate-to-severe AD. Safety analyses were conducted in the All-BARI population (all patients who received ≥1 dose of baricitinib) and the Extended BARI population (patients randomly assigned to placebo or to 1-mg, 2-mg, or 4-mg baricitinib dose equivalents in the double-blind period who received ≥1 dose of study treatment; censored at transition to open-label baricitinib for non-responders or patients who lost response). Safety outcomes were summarized descriptively and included treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), adverse events of special interest (AESI), laboratory abnormalities, and growth parameters. Incidence rates (IRs) are reported per 100 patient-years at risk. Results: A total of 474 pediatric patients were exposed to baricitinib, corresponding to 1424.5 patient-years of exposure. Median and maximum duration of exposure to baricitinib were 3.3 and 5.2 years, respectively. The majority of patients experienced TEAEs that were mild-moderate in severity. The most frequently reported TEAEs included COVID-19 (IR 8.4), nasopharyngitis (IR 7.2), and upper respiratory tract infection (IR 5.1). Acne occurred exclusively as mild or moderate events (IR 3.7 and 1.0 respectively); no severe acne cases occurred. SAEs and study drug discontinuations due to adverse events occurred at IRs of 3.8 and 1.4, respectively. In All-BARI, 8 patients reported infections that led to study drug discontinuation (IR 0.6). The IR for serious infections was 1.5 (n = 21). Herpes zoster was reported in 14 patients (IR 1.0). No dose-related trends were observed for TEAEs, discontinuations, serious infections, or herpes zoster in Extended BARI (median exposure 17-40 weeks by dose, versus 173 weeks in All-BARI); dose-related increases in total and LDL cholesterol were observed. No deaths, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolic events, arterial thrombotic events, malignancies, tuberculosis, or gastrointestinal perforations were reported. Growth parameters, including height, weight, and BMI percentiles, remained broadly consistent with the expected trajectory for a pediatric population throughout the study. The difference between chronological age and radiographic bone age remained consistent through Week 220, with no clinically meaningful changes observed. Conclusion: In this final analysis of the BREEZE-AD-PEDS study, encompassing 1424.5 patient-years and up to 5.2 years of exposure, baricitinib’s long-term safety profile in children remained consistent with previous reports,1,2 with no new safety signals identified. No clinically meaningful impact on growth or bone maturation was observed through Week 220, supporting the long-term use of baricitinib in pediatric patients with moderate-to-severe AD who require systemic therapy.
journal: SKIN The Journal of Cutaneous Medicine

title: SPATIAL DISPARITIES IN CULTURAL TOURISM: A MULTIDIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS OF MUSEUM ATTENDANCE DYNAMICS IN BULGARIA
abstract: This study aims to identify and analyse spatial disparities and structural stratification of regional museum activity in Bulgaria over a 13-year period (2012-2024). The primary objective is to evaluate the stability, growth trajectory, and resilience of regional cultural supply models in response to external and macroeconomic shifts, specifically the COVID-19 pandemic. A multidimensional statistical analysis was applied to panel data from the National Statistical Institute and the Institute for Market Economics, encompassing all 28 administrative districts in Bulgaria. Quartile grouping (based on visits per 1000 inhabitants) was utilized to differentiate clusters, while long-term dynamics and crisis resilience were assessed through specific indicators: Coefficient of Variation (CV), Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), Sensitivity Index (SI), and Recovery Index (RI). Through this approach, the districts were categorized into three distinct performance tiers: Highlevel (Leaders), Mid-level, and Low-level. The analysis reveals significant structural imbalances and high systemic volatility across all clusters, indicating a critical dependence on incidental tourist flows. A “scale paradox” was identified, whereby districts with moderate attendance volumes and a developed local product demonstrate considerably higher post-crisis adaptability compared to traditional leaders. Although all groups exhibit coefficients of variation exceeding 40%, the Mid-level segment achieves the highest annual growth (4.95%) and positive recovery (17.15%), outperforming the top-tier districts, which record slower growth (1.62%) and negative post-pandemic recovery (-12.08%). Empirical profiles highlight stable cores (Veliko Tarnovo, Gabrovo), strategic event legacies (Plovdiv), and nature-integrated recovery (Smolyan), contrasting with transitdependent declines (Vidin). The high structural volatility underscores an urgent need for a conceptual shift in regional cultural policies. Strategic management should pivot towards active audience development and integrated regional tourism products, linking public subsidies to institutional flexibility and proven post-crisis resilience rather than merely static volumes.
journal: Geo Journal of Tourism and Geosites

title: Reimagining Literacy Recovery: Lived Experiences of Junior High School English Teachers Implementing the ARAL Program in Developing Academic Reading and Writing Competencies
abstract: The persistent decline in learners' literacy proficiency has become one of the most pressing educational concerns worldwide, particularly following the learning disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. In the Philippines, the implementation of the Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program institutionalized through Republic Act No. 12028 represents the government's strategic response to addressing learning loss by strengthening foundational competencies, including academic reading and writing. While existing studies have extensively evaluated learners' literacy performance and intervention outcomes, limited attention has been given to the lived experiences of Junior High School English teachers of Bontoc District who serve as primary implementers of literacy recovery initiatives. Their perspectives are critical in understanding how national educational policies are translated into classroom practices that foster academic literacy among diverse learners. This phenomenological study aims to explore the lived experiences of Junior High School English teachers in implementing the ARAL Program to develop students' academic reading and writing competencies. Guided by Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA), the study seeks to understand how teachers perceive their instructional roles, instructional innovations, implementation challenges, coping mechanisms, and professional meanings derived from literacy intervention. Participants will consist of purposively selected Junior High School English teachers actively implementing the ARAL Program in public secondary schools. Data will be gathered through in-depth semi-structured interviews and analyzed using the interpretative procedures of Smith, Flowers, and Larkin. The study is expected to generate rich thematic descriptions that explain how teachers facilitate literacy recovery through differentiated instruction, reflective practice, collaborative engagement, and learner-centered pedagogies. Findings will contribute to the growing body of knowledge on literacy intervention, English language education, teacher professional development, and educational policy while providing evidence-based recommendations for strengthening the implementation of the ARAL Program in Philippine secondary schools.
journal: International Journal of Education, Literacies and Curriculum Studies

title: Temporal trends in cause-specific mortality in French Guiana, 2001–2023: an analysis of age-standardized mortality rates compared with mainland France and neighboring countries
abstract: French Guiana is a French overseas territory with a young, rapidly growing population, a high burden of tropical infectious diseases, and an accelerating transition toward non-communicable diseases. This study describes temporal trends in age-standardized mortality rates across 17 cause-of-death categories over 2001–2023, compares trajectories with mainland France, and contextualizes findings within the regional South American environment. Age-standardized mortality rates trends were assessed using the Mann–Kendall test. Territorial divergence was evaluated via difference-in-slopes z-tests. Regional comparisons used WHO World Standard Population rates against GBD 2023 estimates for four North Brazilian border states and Suriname. Significant declines were observed for infectious diseases (4.4%/year men, −3.9%/year women), circulatory diseases (−2.0%/year men, −2.5%/year women), perinatal conditions, and male cancer mortality. Significant improvements were concentrated in 2001–2017; post-2017 trends were generally non-significant. Against mainland France, six causes showed significantly divergent trends: perinatal mortality declined toward the national rate; respiratory mortality crossed from below to above the national level; and cancer and circulatory mortality declined more slowly. Subcause analysis identified AIDS/HIV (−8.5%/year, 81% reduction) and alcohol-related disorders (−7.5%/year, now below the national rate) as the most marked improvements. Metabolic disease mortality (rate ratio 2.44 × in 2023) remained persistently elevated. Regionally, French Guiana had substantially lower mortality than neighbors for most causes, while exceeding North Brazilian cancer rates, likely reflecting better ascertainment. French Guiana has made substantial mortality gains, particularly for HIV/AIDS, perinatal conditions, and cardiovascular disease, and compares favorably with its South American neighbors. However, its transition remains incomplete: diabetes mortality is widening relative to mainland France, respiratory mortality has crossed to above-national levels, and the 2017 social crisis followed by the COVID-19 crisis appears to have interrupted progress.

French Guiana has made substantial mortality gains, particularly for HIV/AIDS, perinatal conditions, and cardiovascular disease, and compares favorably with its South American neighbors. However, its transition remains incomplete: diabetes mortality is widening relative to mainland France, respiratory mortality has crossed to above-national levels, and the 2017 social crisis followed by the COVID-19 crisis appears to have interrupted progress.

title: Corporate Crisis and Disaster Management in the Digital Era: Building Organisational Resilience through Digital Transformation
abstract: Corporate crises are increasingly shaped by interconnected digital infrastructures, global supply chains, cloud services, artificial intelligence and data-intensive business models. This conceptual article examines how digital transformation is changing the character and management of corporate crises. It develops an integrated Digital Crisis Resilience Framework (DCRF). Drawing on crisis management, organisational resilience, dynamic capabilities, stakeholder and socio-technical systems theories, the article conceptualises resilience as a continuous strategic capability rather than a reactive emergency function. The DCRF integrates eight capabilities across the crisis lifecycle. Comparative analysis of the NotPetya/Maersk, SolarWinds, COVID-19, Colonial Pipeline and CrowdStrike cases illuminates the Digital Resilience Paradox: digitalisation can simultaneously strengthen adaptive capacity and increase systemic vulnerability. A five-level Digital Crisis Resilience Maturity Model, research propositions and an implementation roadmap are proposed. The article contributes by integrating fragmented research streams and extending crisis resilience from the firm level to the wider digital ecosystem.
journal: British journal of computer, networking and information technology
