title: Q-VIRA: Alignment-free viral mutation triage with a variational quantum circuit
abstract: The "Day Zero" Bottleneck: The core problem Q-VIRA addresses is not identifying mutations, but prioritizing them for wet-lab characterization. Because deep mutational scanning (DMS) takes two to six weeks per variant, labs face a severe triage bottleneck. Q-VIRA targets the specific "day zero" scenario of a novel pathogen. In this regime, state-of-the-art alignment models (like EVmutation or GEMME) fail because the virus lacks the deep evolutionary sequence history required for multiple-sequence alignments. Meanwhile, massive Protein Language Models (PLMs) like Meta's ESM carry upwards of 650 million parameters but fail to provide the sharply calibrated, ranked shortlists that a lab technician actually needs to decide which mutation to test first. Quantum Architecture & Parameter Efficiency: Rather than brute-forcing the problem with millions of parameters, Q-VIRA utilizes a data-reuploading Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) with dense encoding (embedding two features per qubit on the RY and RZ axes). By mapping just four to six alignment-free classical descriptors (such as side-chain volume, BLOSUM62 scores, and AlphaFold-predicted residue burial) into a high-dimensional quantum Hilbert space, the circuit creates a highly expressive non-linear decision boundary. The resulting footprint is microscopic: the SARS-CoV-2 specialist model requires only 41 parameters on 2 qubits, while the cross-virus generalist model spans 12 viral organisms using only 63 parameters on 3 qubits. The authors explicitly state they are not claiming quantum speedup; rather, they claim extreme parameter efficiency and verifiability, matching or beating classical neural networks at half the parameter count. Optimizing for the Wet Lab: A major contribution of the preprint is shifting the evaluation metric away from raw AUC to focus on practical lab utility. The authors introduce the "clean prefix"—the number of correct top-ranked mutations the model predicts before making its first false positive. Because Q-VIRA produces the tightest calibration gap in the study (0.045), its clean prefix reaches 22. This is 2.4x deeper than the best classical baseline (an SVM that managed a prefix of 9), meaning a lab can work almost two and a half times further down the triage list before wasting a bench slot on a false positive. Rigorous, Leakage-Free Methodology The preprint heavily emphasizes an "honesty-first" methodology. Many machine learning models in biology achieve inflated >0.90 AUCs through random data splits, which allow the model to memorize a site during training and "predict" it during testing. Q-VIRA strictly forbids this by using site-grouped splits for the specialist model and protein-grouped splits for the generalist model, guaranteeing the model is evaluated exclusively on structures it has never seen—perfectly simulating a novel virus deployment. Head-to-Head Outcomes: Under these strict constraints, the 63-parameter Q-VIRA circuit outperforms every variant of Meta’s ESM family on the alignment-free task, achieving a +0.125 mean AUC advantage over the 3.25-billion-parameter ESM-1v ensemble on four held-out proteins. The paper honestly concedes that alignment-based methods still win when sequence data is abundant, but firmly positions Q-VIRA as the superior, highly calibrated tool for immediate novel pathogen triage. As a secondary proof of the quantum stack's accuracy, the authors also demonstrate a VQE simulation on molecular hydrogen (H2) that perfectly matches exact diagonalisation to <2 × 10^-7 Ha, correcting a massive 0.22 Ha error inherent in classical Hartree-Fock mean-field methods.

title: Transformación digital y su incidencia en el crecimiento económico de las medianas empresas del sector comercial en Machala, durante el período 2020-2025
abstract: This research aimed to analyze, based on the perceptions of business representatives, how digital transformation is related to the economic growth of medium-sized companies in the commercial sector of Machala during the 2020–2025 period. A qualitative approach with a descriptive and interpretive scope was employed, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with representatives of fourteen companies from the sector under study. The inquiry addressed the tools implemented, the organizational areas perceived as most transformed, the main barriers to their adoption, and the economic benefits identified by the participants. The testimonies indicated that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of ERP and CRM systems, e-commerce, social media, electronic invoicing, and inventory control platforms. According to the interviewees, these tools were associated with perceived improvements in sales, logistics, administration, and customer service, mainly due to error reduction, time optimization, operational control, and the expansion of commercial channels. Most participants estimated that the contribution of digitalization accounted for between 30% and 40% of revenue growth. It is concluded that the participants perceived a favorable relationship between digital transformation, productivity, competitiveness, and business sustainability; however, they identified barriers related to costs, resistance to change, and the shortage of digital skills.

title: The Effect Of ROA, EPS, And PBV On Stock Prices In The Financial Sector Listed On The Indonesia Stock Exchange 2021–2025
abstract: The financial sector capital market has experienced considerable dynamics and fluctuations in the post-COVID-19 period that have not always moved in line with companies’ financial fundamentals. An empirical anomaly occurred in 2023, when improvements in financial ratios were followed by a weakening of the sectoral stock price index. Objective This study examines the effects of Return On Assets (ROA), Earning Per Share (EPS), and Price to Book Value (PBV) on stock prices of financial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021–2025. Method: A quantitative explanatory approach was employed. Using purposive sampling, 13 companies were selected, resulting in 65 observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. Results: ROA has no significant effect on stock prices (Sig. 0.053 > 0.05), while EPS and PBV have positive and significant effects (Sig. Simultaneously, ROA, EPS, and PBV significantly affect stock prices, with a coefficient of determination of 52.2%. Conclusion EPS and PBV are stronger determinants of investor decisions than ROA. The findings confirm the applicability of signaling theory in the Indonesian capital market.
journal: Jurnal Ekonomi Bisnis, Manajemen dan Akuntansi

title: Diversifying deaths: the shifting spectrum of childhood respiratory infectious mortality, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
abstract: Background Childhood respiratory infectious deaths are partitioned across four Global Burden of Disease cause modules-26 etiological attributions within lower respiratory infections, tuberculosis, COVID-19, and whooping cough-never jointly reported. Whether the structure of this combined mortality spectrum has changed over time, and with what implications for intervention design, has not been quantified. We assembled and analyzed the integrated spectrum for children and adolescents aged 0-19 years, 1990-2023. Methods We integrated Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (release v8352) estimates into a 29-node spectrum-26 lower respiratory infection etiologies plus tuberculosis, COVID-19, and pertussis-globally and across seven super-regions, with uncertainty propagated by summing bounds. We computed Shannon diversity, Herfindahl concentration, and effective cause counts; phenotyped pandemic-window collapse and rebound per cause; linked pathogen shares to WHO/UNICEF vaccine coverage; and mapped geographic concentration in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Reporting follows GATHER. Segmented (joinpoint) log-linear models with breakpoints selected by the Bayesian information criterion were fitted to annual totals, Shannon diversity and leading pathogen shares. Results In 2023 the 29 causes jointly accounted for 965,330 deaths (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 680,096-1,342,437). Shannon diversity rose from 2.336 to 2.711 (+16.1%) between 1990 and 2023; the effective number of causes nearly doubled (5.57 to 9.94), inversely coupled to total deaths (Spearman rho = -0.997). Whooping cough ranked second (112,954 deaths; 95% UI 64,576-185,708; 11.7%) and showed the spectrum's only rebound above 100% (-57.4% collapse, +111.0% rebound). Tuberculosis ranked third (87,764; 57,779-124,912; 9.1%) with the highest concentration in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia (87.1%). COVID-19 entered at rank five (52,899; 47,275-59,183; 5.5%). Nineteen of 29 causes exceeded the poverty-lock threshold (>80.59% of deaths in sub-Saharan Africa plus South Asia). Joinpoint analysis placed breakpoints in total deaths at 2011, 2018 and 2021-the decline slowed from -3.4% to -2.3% per year after 2011, steepened to -7.1% per year in 2018-2021 and rebounded +4.5% per year in 2021-2023-while diversification accelerated to +1.18% per year in 2013-2020; all six leading pathogen shares carried a pandemic-window breakpoint at 2019 and 2021 (S. pneumoniae at 2018 and 2021). Conclusions Childhood respiratory infectious mortality has become more diverse and more concentrated in poverty as it has declined. Single-pathogen interventions now address a shrinking share; the spectrum's structure argues for platform interventions-oxygen, antimicrobial access, referral-tailored jointly by age and geography, implying that pathogen-specific strategies alone cannot finish the remaining mortality agenda.

title: Human-supervised Agentic AI for Hypothesis Generation and Experimental Assistance in Drug Repurposing
abstract: Computational drug repurposing has focused largely on rapid hypothesis generation, yet real-world applications span a much broader lifecycle: suggesting drug candidates, designing experiments, analyzing assay data, and iteratively refining hypotheses. Here, we demonstrate that agentic AI can operate throughout this lifecycle. We developed RepurAgent, a hierarchical multi-agentic system comprising a supervisor agent and a planning agent that coordinates four specialized sub-agents (research, prediction, data, and report) with human in the loop, supported by episodic memory and retrieval-augmented generation. The system is grounded in repurposing-specific data, tools, and standard operating procedures developed within the REMEDi4ALL consortium. We validated RepurAgent across three scenarios spanning distinct stages within the repurposing lifecycle: in acute myeloid leukemia, a blinded expert evaluation indicated that RepurAgent produced substantially more candidates that were both novel and mechanistically credible than a vanilla LLM baseline; in a retrospective COVID-19 antiviral screen, RepurAgent acted as an adaptive experimental collaborator, prioritizing compounds with AUC-ROC up to 0.99 and average precision up to 0.91 without predefined thresholds and flagging confounders missed in manual review; and for multiple sulfatase deficiency, it prioritized 81 high-confidence candidates from 5159 compounds, which were further corroborated by domain experts. These results show that agentic AI can support work across the drug repurposing lifecycle, from hypothesis generation to experimental analysis. RepurAgent is open source and deployed at https://repuragent.serve.scilifelab.se/.

title: No convergence in three decades: national trajectories of episode-fatality ratios for childhood lower respiratory infections in 204 countries, 1990-2023
abstract: Background Lower respiratory infections (LRI) remain the leading infectious cause of death in children, and survival once ill is a direct tracer of health-system quality. Whether countries are converging toward the best survival performance achieved within their own region has never been tested at national level. We measured each country's distance to an empirical episode-fatality-ratio (EFR) frontier in 204 countries from 1990 to 2023. Methods For each country and year we computed EFR = LRI deaths/incident episodes using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates for ages 0-19 years. Deaths span the full 1990-2023 series; episodes are observed for 1990, 2019 and 2023, with intermediate years linearly interpolated. The frontier was the 10th-percentile country EFR within each GBD super-region and year (sensitivity: 5th and 25th percentiles); the gap = EFR_country/EFR_frontier. We classified 33-year gap trajectories into catch-up phenotypes, ranked COVID-window (2019-2023) movers, cross-tabulated gap against avoidable deaths to build a priority list, and benchmarked upper respiratory infections (URI) at three time points as a near-zero-fatality contrast. Findings The median country's gap was 1.86 in 1990, 1.80 in 2019 and 1.86 in 2023; the share of countries more than twice their regional frontier was 44.6% in 1990 and 46.6% in 2023. Of 137 eligible countries, 67 narrowed and 69 widened their gap, with one unchanged. Nineteen countries achieved sustained catch-up, concentrated in North Africa and the Middle East (7) and Latin America (5), with China closing from 2.43 to 0.50, below its regional frontier; 28 countries regressed, led by Central Asia (Uzbekistan x3.5) and including the United States (x2.0). Over the COVID-19 window the median gap peaked at 2.00 in 2021 (+10.8% versus 2019, from unrounded medians) before returning to 1.86. Combining gap with avoidable deaths identifies two distinct policy problems: high-burden, moderate-gap giants (Nigeria 67,490 avoidable deaths, gap 2.4; India 54,109, gap 1.6) and extreme-gap outliers (Uzbekistan, gap 28.6). The Sub-Saharan Africa frontier fell further behind the High-income frontier (ratio 4.2 in 1990, 9.5 in 2023); the median Sub-Saharan African country sits 11.0 times the global 10th-percentile frontier but only 1.78 times its own regional frontier, so within-region benchmarking understates the region's true distance. URI gaps likewise did not converge (median 4.15 to 4.60). Joinpoint regression formalized the pattern: the median gap showed no net narrowing over 33 years (average annual percent change +0.03% per year, 95% CI -0.05 to 0.12). Interpretation Convergence toward the survival frontier is not the default national trajectory: over three decades the typical country made no net progress toward the best decile of its own region, and pandemic-era divergence was only partly reversed. National gap trajectories separate system-wide quality shortfalls from extreme outliers warranting audit, and expose a measurement trap in which regions whose frontiers stagnate appear closer to best practice than they are.
